## r338 + r339 (2026-09-25) — seven items, shipped as one deploy after four failed attempts on box memory. `main@3e094ae8`, migration **0488**.

Closed: `639bf4a5`, `73ddd5a1`, `00e28308`, `bb2b2e86`, `4ca06dea` (r338); `04b88724`, `20837372` (r339).
Gate: **998 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, `gate:shadow` **PASS 401/401**. Render check: 4 screens × 6 locales, 24 × 200, zero poison tokens, and the corrected child reliefs verified **on screen** (RM 8,000 ×2, RM 16,000 ×1, retired RM 14,000 absent).

⚠️ **Gated as ONE receipt across two rounds**, because main moved past r338's receipt while its deploy was blocked. That is the honest shape: the tree that shipped is the tree that was gated.

### THE REPORTER WAS RIGHT AND WE WERE WRONG — TWICE, ON STATUTORY MONEY

`04b88724`: we told them our five `childByCategory` figures "match HASiL line for line". They contested, citing the LHDN 2026 MTD specification. **They were right.** Printed p.27 gives a qualifying-children table — a disabled child counts as **4** children (RM8,000), one in further instruction as **8** (RM16,000). We held RM6,000 and RM14,000: the **annual assessment** figures. Malaysia has two schedules and they disagree for disabled children.

**Our own code had said so.** That object carried `⚠️ RATE-ONLY, NOT YET VERIFIED` and we quoted it as confirmation anyway. Every value now carries its printed-page citation.

Three things the build found that the brief did not name:
- **Nobody was affected** — stronger than "at most one". The money path reads `child_relief_table` gated on `auto_table`; the one disabled child belongs to an `auto` employee.
- **A THIRD source carried the old figures.** `localization/statutory-pack/bundled/my-2026.01.01.pack.json` embeds a **signed** copy; `pnpm statutory:sync` would have reinstated 6,000/14,000 **over** the fix and stamped them 2026.7. Caught by an existing guard, fixed by rebuilding the pack.
- **`disabledSpouse` is wrong too** — p.28 item f gives RM6,000, we hold RM5,000. Raised as `57d48735`, not swept in.

### TP3's SECTION D REACHED NOTHING

`20837372`: LHDN p.22 — *"The information amount from the TP3 Form shall be treated in the formula as variable (Y−K\*), X, Z and ∑LP."* We wired three. Section D was captured, validated, stored and read by **nothing**, and ∑LP is subtracted inside P — so a new joiner who declared previous-employment reliefs was **over-deducted**.

⚠️ **CORRECTING MY OWN BRIEF, MEASURED AFTER THE BUILD:** I told the agent this was live. The one production TP3 form has a Section D with seventeen keys and **every amount zero** (Section C totals 75,579). The 0488 backfill carries `AND d.lp <> 0`, so it correctly skipped it: `tp3_lp` is NULL, read as zero, **no payslip moved**. The structural defect was real; the urgency was mine.

Three of that brief's premises were wrong and the source won: **C2 was already five sub-items** (`c.c2?.amount` is the server's *sum*); **the TP3 form prints no limit column on Section C**, so ADR-0008 decides it — captured, never blocked; and therefore **capping C2 would tax the same ringgit twice**, because p.20's "any amount exceed the restricted amount shall be taxable" addresses the *previous* employer, whose over-limit portion is already inside C1. Two of the five C2 limits are `null` and stay null — the build **stopped rather than invent**, which is the discipline `04b88724` proved we needed.

### THE GATE CAUGHT WHAT NO WORKTREE COULD

One red chunk: `employee-import-field-parity` walks the **merged** schema and found `tp3_lp` neither carried by an import column nor excluded with a reason — invisible from inside the TP3 worktree, the same shape as `maritalStatusSourceRequestId` in r334. Given its **own** exclusion entry rather than appended to the four existing `tp3*` fields, because their stated reason (*also loaded by the payroll history import*) is **not true** of a form-only column; appending would have made the guard assert something false.

### r338's FIVE

`639bf4a5` **reverses r336 one round after it shipped**, on the reporter's contest: Locations returns to Attendance as a company listing with dedicated screens. Route and `screenKey` deliberately did not move; the drift ratchet is byte-untouched (it governs imports, not menus); a company's second location is **shown**, rowSpanned, because production has 8 locations across 6 companies and the ticket's one-per-company example did not match the data.

`73ddd5a1` proved **my plan overstated the cost**: I told the reporter blank marital status would cost Caregiver *and* Natural Disaster Leave; `NDL` has no eligibility row at all. Now an assertion, not prose. It also made concrete that production holds **5,922 days of granted-but-invisible balance** — created before the read and grant paths agreed, never created again, existing days untouched.

`00e28308` caught that there are **TWO** find-or-create sites, not the one I named — r337 made a non-regular run able to open a month, so stamping only `createBatch` would have left every **bonus-led** month unstamped. Stamped at creation so **no `UPDATE` of the column exists anywhere**, making a later stealth backfill structurally impossible.

`4ca06dea` found a **third** omission I had missed (the `groups` array), so a corrected count alone would have disabled Process **without saying why**; and `actions.ts` was reporting the wrong reason entirely.

`bb2b2e86` found the 50-row cap default was **never pinned**, and that its own first locale guard would have shipped a **malformed Thai ICU string green** because next-intl swallows `FORMATTING_ERROR`.

### THE DEPLOY, AND THE BOX IS OUT OF RUNWAY

**Four failed attempts**, ~40 minutes producing nothing, every one memory. `deploy.sh`'s heap cap went `4096 → 2560 → 3584 → 4096` across r336–r339 as the diagnosis converged. The rule now recorded there: **the cap must fit RAM + free swap, not RAM alone**, and a cap above what the box can back converts a clean V8 self-OOM into a kernel kill. Also recorded: a killed `pnpm build` leaves a **~2.5 GB orphan reparented to init for ~10 minutes**, which starves the retry and looks exactly like capacity — check `ps --sort=-rss` before blaming the number.

⚠️ **The next bump does not fit.** 4096 plus overhead is ~80% of this box's entire 5.6 GB. The type pass has needed more memory in four consecutive rounds. **Add RAM or grow `/swap.img` (267 GB of disk free) before touching that number again.**

### NOT DONE

`disabledSpouse` (`57d48735`, raised). TP3 **R1**: C1's Malay caption reads *"yang dikenakan cukai"*, which if correct means `C1 − ΣC2 − C3` double-subtracts and **under**-deducts — not flipped on an unresolved reading; the only document that settles it 404s on both LHDN URLs. **R2**: TP3 Section D and our own TP1 now both feed ∑LP and `checkTp1OverClaim` has never seen a TP3. The child-relief mode migration for the other 74 employees stays the reporter's separate trigger.

## r337 (2026-09-24) — one item, and it caught a silent under-remittance to LHDN. `main@9cff0a25`, no migration.

Closed: `23e7dac3` (payroll cycles in any order).
Gate: **991 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, **zero red chunks on the first pass**, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No shadow gate: no migration, journal verified unchanged after the merge at 400 entries / max idx 487. Render check: 3 screens × 6 locales, 18 × 200, zero poison tokens in the dev log and in `<script>`-stripped markup.

### THE FINDING: OPENING THE SELECTOR NAIVELY WOULD HAVE UNDER-PAID LHDN

The reporter asked to run BONUS or Off Cycle before Monthly. Measured through the real kernel **before any code was written**: RM5,000 salary + RM500 overtime + RM3,000 bonus, bonus first, produced month **PCB 60.00 instead of 100.00**; a variant put EPF employer at **1,030 instead of 1,080**. The regular run was not a delta — it recomputed the whole normal-wage month beside an increment taken on a base that did not yet contain the overtime.

So the load-bearing half of this item is **the month restating when the regular run lands**, which ADR-0085 lists and the brief did not emphasise. Both orders now telescope to the same month, pinned as literals, with the same month paid as a single run as an independent oracle.

### AND THE ADR WAS WRONG ABOUT WHY IT WAS BLOCKED

ADR-0085 §1.2 said order-independence is unbuildable without signed deltas (step 3), because the first run would be "taxed as though its payment were the employee's normal monthly pay". **False against the kernel**: `wagesExOt` is recomputed per employee from the COMPENSATION RECORD on every run, so the month's normal wage is in the statutory base whether or not the regular run has happened — Y1 was never taken from the runs. Recorded as a correction in the ADR rather than relied on silently. **Step 3 remains NOT STARTED; `clampDelta` and `deltaStat` are untouched.**

### BUILD ORDER WAS THE SAFETY ARGUMENT, AND IT WAS HONOURED LITERALLY

Step 4 — the refusal for a month already filed with LHDN, EPF or SOCSO — is commits 1 and 2, **proven before a line of the selector or the kernel order moved**. It consumes r330's `periodFiledTx` unchanged and adds `describeFiledEvidence` so the message names the return, its period, its filing date and the acknowledgement. Three doors: `createAdditionalRun`, `createBatch`, `generatePayslips`. The line is `run_seq > 1` — "a run that changes a figure an earlier run already produced" IS "a run that is not the month's first" — which keeps a lone regular run byte-identical and preserves r292's judgement that a wrongly filed month must stay correctable.

### ONE RESIDUAL, BOUNDED AND DISCLOSED

The EPF Third Schedule steps the EMPLOYER column at RM5,000 and `deltaStat` still clamps at zero, so whichever run crosses the step contributes RM0 rather than handing the difference back. **Bound RM38.00** — the step's size — and **upward only**, so an out-of-order month is never under-remitted, only over, and the excess lands in the employee's own EPF account. Absorbing it on the regular run works arithmetically and was **rejected**: that is step 3 under another name, and it would make a regular run's EPF disagree with the Third Schedule row for its own wage on a payslip an employee reads.

ADR-0085 also gained the **§7 worksheet its own build order cites and did not have** — the citation pointed at ADR-0024 §7, which always runs the regular run first and so structurally cannot answer "does the order matter?". The example is traced both ways with every per-run figure pinned as a literal in the test, so document and kernel cannot drift.

### THE DEPLOY, AND THE BOX IS OUT OF RUNWAY

Two attempts. r337's ~1,270 added kernel lines pushed the type pass past the 3584 cap r336 had settled on — a clean V8 self-OOM — and 4096 got it through on 5.6 GB of RAM+swap.

⚠️ **The trend now matters more than the number**: `2048 → 3072 → 4096 → 3584 → 4096` across R52, r83, r336, r337. The pass has needed a bump in **consecutive rounds**, and 4096 plus node overhead is already **~80% of this box's entire RAM+swap**. The next bump does not fit, and raising past what the box can back converts a clean V8 self-OOM into a kernel kill (the r336 story). **Add RAM or grow `/swap.img` — 267 GB of disk is free — before touching that number again.** Recorded in `deploy/deploy.sh`.

### NOT DONE

`batchDownstreamWarnings` is **narrower than the filed-period predicate**, so a month can read *filed* to the new refusal and *not-filed* to the amber banner an operator is looking at. Widening it changes a warning four screens rely on and wants its own round — **this is the one open decision handed back**. Per-leg filed granularity is still period-coarse (a filed Borang A bars a run that would only have moved PCB); the release valve — reverse the filing — is tested. The multi-cycle worksheet screen still excludes out-of-order months, documented in place rather than fixed, because teaching it the restating rule would move ADR-0024 §7's signed-off figures for no live caller.

## r336 (2026-09-24) — eleven items, six concurrent builders, and eight defects only the gate could see. `main@94ec3522`, migration **0487**.

Closed: `1bb09a73`, `3783fd87`, `7f251381`, `8d3a7bff`, `20f6c6a8`, `da7463b4`, `7d2df42a`, `639bf4a5`, `cbfa8b0b`, `99b2d6c0`, `2a57a007`.
Gate: **988 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, `gate:shadow` **PASS 400/400**. Render check: 5 screens × 6 locales, 30 × 200, zero poison tokens, the one new string asserted to resolve per-locale rather than by English fallback. Chunks 1–10 were **re-run on the final tree** because two fixes touched product code; a green gate has to be green on what ships.

### THE CONCURRENCY MODEL CHANGED, AND THE OLD RULE WAS MY OWN WRONG INFERENCE

"Two builders max" came from watching three agents stall and blaming the agent count. Measured: 12 cores sat **~57% idle** at 284 MB free. RAM binds only while *vitest* runs — an agent costs ~200 MB reading code and 1.5–3 GB testing. So `~/.aihr-gate-state/testlock.sh` caps **test runs** at 2 while any number of agents read and edit. Six ran concurrently on hardware that had held two.

A second lock followed, and an agent found the need, not me: `pnpm db:seed` **truncates the one shared `ai_hr_dev`** every render check reads, so two overlapping checks silently swap each other's data. `devdb-lock.sh` serialises the whole check — seed, server, curls, kill — because holding it only for the seed leaves exactly the window it closes. It was live risk for several hours.

### FOUR VACUOUS GUARDS, FOUND BY FOUR DIFFERENT AGENTS AND BY THE GATE

- **r332's holiday-claim guard** — and this one had shipped a lie. ADR-0086 removed the work site's hold on public holidays a fortnight earlier, but only the `stateNote` KEY went; the sentence survived in `admin.locations.pageDescription` and was **live on production in all six languages**. The guard could not have caught it twice over: it matched `stateNote`'s exact words, which the other key's wording never matched, *and* that case mocks `getTranslations` to echo key names, so no English sentence was ever in the markup it searched.
- **A clocking-grouping test** asserting order and the unlinked group's existence — so a page that had stopped grouping altogether stayed green.
- **`3783fd87`'s "not required" check** — `/name="companyLabel"(?![^>]*\brequired\b)/` scans forward from `name=`, and React emits attributes out of JSX order, putting `required` first. It was green **with the field required**.
- **`cbfa8b0b`'s own submit-blocking assertions** — passing because an empty form disables the button anyway.

### EIGHT INTEGRATION FAILURES THE GATE CAUGHT THAT NO BRANCH COULD

Only one was a product defect: the Leave Credit dialog's rewrite dropped its `lib/day-format` import and printed **raw day counts — `0.5` where every other leave surface says `0.50`** — the fault a `toFixed` grep cannot see, because the screen never formatted at all. The other seven were guards following code that legitimately moved; each was **updated with its reason, none loosened**, and four would otherwise have kept passing against **dead keys or renamed ids** while the screen said something else.

### MY BRIEFS WERE WRONG FIVE TIMES; THE SOURCE WON EACH TIME

- The **LHDN e-Data writer already ships** (`localization/my/cp39-file.ts`, served by `/payroll/reports/cp39-file`). I verified no *specimen* existed and read that as no *writer*. Listing it unavailable would have reshipped the r296 defect — a screen denying a file another screen hands over.
- The draft employee's **IC→DOB server path already existed** (`core/employee-draft.ts:755`); the gap was that nothing derived *while the draft was being filled in*.
- **`isValidIC` is `/^\d{12}$/`** — a digit count with no date check. Month 13 passes, the DOB silently comes back null, and the employee is created without one. Nothing refuses it anywhere.
- **An off day IS bankable** from the employee-request path; r334's finding held only for the roster election. The divergence is between *paths*, not day kinds.
- **"Most of point 1 is DONE" was false.** Only Balance is zero on a pooled borrower; Entitlement and Earned to Date still print the POOL's figures, because `rows.ts` resolves the breakdown through `balanceStoryTypeId`. Left open deliberately — reversing it re-opens the r209 red-notice trap and is load-bearing for `8d3a7bff`, which shipped this round.

### DECISIONS

- **`20f6c6a8`** — `verification` is a REQUIRED field on every payment format: `filed-file` (EPF, SOCSO — byte-equal to files the customer really filed), `specification-sample` (LHDN), `field-table-only`. The lesson from the wrong Borang A is not "only ship formats with a filed file", which would delete a shipped capability; it is that **a file's provenance may never be invisible**. Its LHDN row was taken OFF the new shelf **during the gate** rather than add debt to a ratchet that only shrinks — the row stays listed, with its provenance, pointing at the screen that serves it today.
- **`99b2d6c0`** — not one disabled-relief amount changed. The LHDN spec was never supplied, and `childByCategory` turns out to be flagged RATE-ONLY too. Also pinned **two kernel gates no test reached**: deleting either `auto_table` mode read would have left the whole suite green while every such employee silently reverted to flat child-relief counting — a wrong PCB with nothing on screen.
- **`cbfa8b0b`** — `eligible_minutes` is a record, never a valuation input (`day_type` stays NULL); `EXCLUDE_TOIL_BANKED_DAYS` byte-untouched, proven by a mutation showing **RM173.04 of overtime** would be paid on a banked day without it. Ticket point 4 stayed unbuilt as the plan promised. Migration **0487 extends** `replacement_leave_request_date` rather than adding a claim-line table, because a separate table would give "what did this employee claim for this date" two owners.
- **`2a57a007`** — the pooled Share columns go positive. Verified safe first: nothing computes from them, and the `sum(balance)` invariant is about `balance`, not the displayed share. Said so **at the line that decides the sign**, or the next reader restores the minus.
- **`639bf4a5`** — the work-site register MOVED pack surface rather than merely stopping being advertised, because the pack's surface claim was the only thing authorising its direct `core/clocking-location` import. The ratchet **shrank** by one entry and nothing was added at the new address.

### CORRECTIONS OWED TO THE REPORTER

- **`7f251381`'s approved mockup mislabels four symbols.** It captions `Y1` "Previous employment income" and `Yt` "Accumulated remuneration"; the engine has `Y1 = p.monthlyWage` (this month's wage) and `Yt = p.additional` (the bonus). Building to it would have printed a bonus under an accumulator caption — the exact defect the item exists to remove. The screen is right; the picture they approved is not.
- **`73ddd5a1` is wider than we told them**: three leave types, not one (Maternity 5,390 days, Paternity 385, Marriage 147 — 5,922 standing across 74 employees). Sent with the correction at the top. The useful half: **all 19 clear-cut cases are already reversed at net 0.00**, so every remaining day hangs on a blank field and filling them in genuinely resolves it.
- **`20f6c6a8`'s plan says we are waiting on their LHDN file.** We are not waiting to *write* it — it exists. We are waiting to *verify* it against a real filed one, which moves the entry to `filed-file`: a one-word registry change, not a build.

### THE DEPLOY, AND A REAL BUG IN `deploy.sh`

Four attempts. The script capped the build heap at **4096 MB on a box with ~2.5 GB available**, so V8 never approached its own limit, never collected hard, and the kernel killed it first — a bare `Killed`/137, unlike the two earlier OOMs this file records, which died as V8's own `Ineffective mark-compacts`. **Different failure, opposite fix.** Lowering to 2560 converted 137 into V8's own `FatalProcessOutOfMemory`, proving the mechanism and showing 2560 was simply too low; **3584** got it through.

The rule is now stated correctly in the file: the cap must fit **RAM + free swap**, not RAM alone. And the confounder is recorded, because it cost a wrong diagnosis: a killed `pnpm build` leaves a **~2.5 GB `next` worker reparented to init in D state for ~10 minutes**, which starves the retry and makes a capacity problem out of a cleanup one. Check `ps --sort=-rss` before blaming the number. `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors` was never on the table — that pass catches RSC boundary errors `tsc` alone does not.

### NOT DONE

`23e7dac3` is **built and gated-pending** on `build/r337-23e7dac3`, deliberately unmerged so these eleven could ship against a known sha. `73ddd5a1` step 2 is the reporter's own data entry. Three items await their answer (`bb2b2e86`, `4ca06dea`, `00e28308`). The `unpayablePayMode` screen/server mismatch and the missing `pay_period.statutory_version` were **raised, not fixed** — both sit on the money path and both are the reporter's call.

## r335 (2026-09-24) — two items, and both corrected something I had written. `main@6281abb3`, no migration.

Closed: `0fe1ca2e` (rev 6), `6af80f5d` (rev 2). Gate: **971 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, ~15,040 tests, **zero red chunks on the first pass**, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No shadow gate: no migration, journal verified unchanged at 399 entries / max idx 486. Render check clean.

### `6af80f5d` — MY BRIEF CONTRADICTED ITSELF, AND THE BUILD CAUGHT IT

I wrote "round the DISPLAY field only — `currentYearEntitlement`" and, two paragraphs later, "the SUM must use the exact figure (to tile)". **`currentYearEntitlement` is not a display field.** `core/read.ts` builds `totalEntitlement` from it; `entitlement-panel-config.ts` lists it in `RECONCILIATION_ADDENDS` with `sign: 1`, where `reconciledBalance(b)` must equal `b.balance`; `lib/leave-summary-explain.ts` builds the HR sentences and the Total formula from it. Rounding it is exactly what my second instruction forbids. I verified the addend membership directly before merging.

Resolved by the repo's own r313 `DisplayEntitlement` precedent: a new `currentYearEntitlementRounded`, **required rather than optional** in both mirror types, so no hand-built breakdown can silently fall back to the unrounded figure.

**And it explained why 11.18 exists at all** — worth telling the reporter: `accrueEarnedLeave` *already* rounds at source (b81d3c52), but tops up by `toGrant = earnedToDate − already` behind a `toGrant > 0` guard, the forward-only contract. Days credited **before** a rounding table was configured are never clawed back, so the cycle keeps its raw running total. A display fix is the only answer that does not rewrite ledger rows.

Mutation B (rounding `cycleAccrual` at source) fires both named invariant guards: *"totalEntitlement is byte-identical with the rounding rule on and off — expected 11 to be 11.18"* and *"Σ(addends · sign) still equals the balance — expected 6 to be 6.18"*.

### `0fe1ca2e` — IT CLOSED A COVERAGE GAP MY BRIEF ASSUMED EXISTED

`test/clocking-map.dom.test.tsx` drove a **hand-built look-alike `<form>`**, never `ClockingLocationForm`. So **no test in the suite could have caught the address search leaving the form's subtree** — trap 1, and the one failure mode that is silent, because `form-bridge` finds its inputs through the enclosing form.

A new describe mounts the real component. Mutation (d) renders the search outside the form and fails with *"the address the search wrote: expected '' to be 'Menara KL…'"* **while the other 11 DOM tests stay green** — demonstrating the old harness's blindness rather than asserting it.

Order is asserted by **measured index** in the stripped markup, not by presence (a presence check passes on today's layout too), and the search is anchored on its `aria-label` read out of `en.json` rather than a hardcoded English sentence.

Two of the three things the reporter asked for were **already built** since r279 — the search already filled Address/Latitude/Longitude and already sat above Latitude. The real complaint was the card boundary between them, and the plan said so rather than claiming credit for building them.

### OPERATIONAL

- **The gate ran under heavy swap pressure** — 146 s on chunk 1 against a 124 s baseline, load ~17–20, ~5 GB swap in use after 1M+ swapouts across two days. Still green first pass.
- **Three builders stall this machine; two do not.** Two agents were lost to the 600 s watchdog earlier in the session at *lighter* load than the gate ran at. The working limit is two concurrent builders, and the gate alone.

### WHAT WAS NOT DONE

- **Six items approved and unbuilt**: `1bb09a73` and `3783fd87` (building at the time of writing), `20f6c6a8`, `7f251381`, `99b2d6c0`, `da7463b4`.
- **`8d3a7bff` planned**: the second "Special Leave" card is **Compassionate Leave** drawing on the Special Leave pot — measured, and it must NOT be removed. `lib/shared-leave-balance.ts`'s header records why the borrower tells the pool's story.
- **`73ddd5a1` open**, awaiting the reporter: 55 of 76 active employees have no gender recorded and 48 no marital status, which decides who gets which leave.
- `20f6c6a8` cannot start its LHDN writer, and `99b2d6c0` cannot change its two disabled-relief figures, until the reporter supplies the authoritative LHDN documents. Both plans say why, and `statutory-tables.ts:99` already records one of those values as *"RATE-ONLY, NOT YET VERIFIED"*.

### RECORDED

## r334 (2026-09-24) — three items, and a flake that had been measured and written down before it was written in. `main@86fa1231`, **migration 0486**.

Closed: `d272834b`, `928f0454`, `5b2a7f0f`. Gate: **969 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, ~15,007 tests, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, shadow **PASS 399/399**. Render check clean.

⚠️ **Round numbering: this one is right.** The number was taken from this file's top entry *before* the worktrees were named, which is the fix recorded after r332 and r333 both shipped under the previous round's prefix. Branches and commits all read `r334`.

### THE RED CHUNK WAS REAL, AND THE DIAGNOSIS WAS ALREADY IN THE REPO

Chunk 5 failed with a genuine `AssertionError` on `test/2a1a6f42-ea-preview.test.ts` — the §4 rule (`grep -c AssertionError` first) separated real from environment in one command, though it needed `grep -a` because a PDF diff makes the log binary.

The helper blanked `D:\d{14}` in the raw bytes and called two renders comparable. They are not: `pdf-lib`'s `save()` defaults to `useObjectStreams: true`, so the Info dictionary — and the dates with it — lands **inside a deflate stream** where a text regex cannot reach.

**r331 measured exactly this and wrote it down** — *"the delta is pdf-lib's timestamp inside a deflate stream"* — and the regex was written anyway. It then passed the r332 and r333 gates by luck and went red under r334's load. The identical helper sat in the sibling `72b100cd` test; **both** now reload, stamp the dates to a constant and re-save without object streams. Non-vacuity is built in: the same test asserts the Malay sheet is not the English one, so an over-normalising helper fails it.

### `d272834b` — TWO CHALLENGES TO MY BRIEF, BOTH RIGHT

- **It refused to flip the grant path to `'exclude'`.** After the normalisation the only lists still reaching that policy are *genuine* restrictions, including CGL and NDL's five-of-six marital lists. I measured what it could not (it was refused production reads): **48 of 76** active employees have no marital status, so flipping would have withheld Caregiver and Natural Disaster Leave from 48 people — the failure mode `UnknownAttributePolicy`'s own header records. Raised separately as `73ddd5a1`.
- **It rejected my location for the fix.** I said the write-time normaliser in `core/admin.ts`; that runs only on *save*, so the eight production types already storing `["male","female"]` would be unreached until each was re-opened and re-saved — and a write-time strip would show an admin who ticked both genders a form with neither ticked. It went at interpretation time, and found a **third** copy of `['male','female']` in the picker on the way.

**It also fixed a live defect nobody reported, in the opposite direction.** The read gates pass `'exclude'`, eight types list both genders, and **55 of 76** active employees have no gender recorded — so those 55 were losing all eight types from their cards *and* their apply dropdown. And it corrected the mechanism: `leaveBalances` *did* gate, but only on the tail deciding whether to **invent** a row; a row backed by ledger activity was never asked, which is why Daniel Tan's +98/−98 pair kept its card.

### `928f0454` — THE MONEY FINDING WAS WORTH 50%

The accrual stamps `dayType: null`, not `'workday'`. `convertAmountFor` prices an expired First-Schedule credit as **exact statutory cash** over the stored minutes, but a tier **rounds down** — so 7h59m banks 0.5 day and would have cashed out as nearly eight hours of overtime. Measured: **RM86.52** of s.60A cash against a **RM57.69** credit. Same over-valuation r299 closed one function away.

The named rule is **not** widened — `RL_ELIGIBLE_DAY_TYPES` still reads `{rest_day, holiday}` with the new path forked beside it. A mutation was initially vacuous (`overtimePay` answers `eligible: false` above the RM4,000 ceiling, so the payslip read 0 either way) and was fixed with an RM3,000 fixture plus a control employee in the same payroll run.

Two measured contradictions of the ticket: an **off day has never been bankable from the roster election**, left byte-identical rather than silently closed; and `maybeAutoAccrueOnApprovalTx` decided the day type *before* reading the policy, so the new switch was unreachable from that path however it was set.

### `5b2a7f0f` — THREE FINDINGS, NONE OF THEM VISIBLE TO A TEST

- **`@pdf-lib/fontkit`, which my brief named as required, writes corrupt subsets.** Its CFF output rendered as a row of unrelated ASCII letters — and `/ToUnicode` extraction returned *perfect Chinese* from the broken document. **Only rasterising the page found it.** Upstream `fontkit@1.9.0` does it correctly.
- **Turbopack takes fontkit's ESM build**, which imports a dead `@swc/helpers` export: a **500 on both payslip PDF routes with the vitest suite green either way**. `serverExternalPackages: ['fontkit']`. Caught by the §8 dev-server check and nothing else.
- **A real translation is longer than a question mark.** Vietnamese's `TỔNG CHI PHÍ NGƯỜI SỬ DỤNG LAO ĐỘNG` printed straight through `MYR 8,141.55` on the one baseline that cannot wrap.

Mixed script resolves **per drawn string** against a face that covers both, because splitting the run would mean splitting every measurement and `wrap()` measuring against the real font is what keeps this document from clipping. 6.5 MB of brotli-compressed fonts, largest face 5.81 MiB (16.4 MB and 17.8 MB alternatives measured and rejected). EN payslips are byte-identical — three SHA-256 digests pinned.

**A correction to an item I raised:** I said Malay loses 10 of 65 strings. Measured properly it is **0 of 68** — seven em dashes the existing fold already handles, in English too. The Tamil/Chinese/Thai figures stand.

A plain `tx.update(person)` inside the approval is refused by Postgres and takes the whole approval down — and **a test that approved as an admin would never have seen it**. The write goes through two SECURITY DEFINER functions (the idiom 0207/0433 established), each deriving everything from the request id and returning an outcome code so core can tell "lawfully did nothing" from "refused". ## r331 (2026-09-23) — three items, and an agent finding the gap that would have made a promise false. `main@78745e66`, **migration 0483**.

Closed: `72b100cd`, `a96d320c`, `07ebd04d`. Gate: **957 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, **zero red chunks**, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, shadow **PASS 396/396**. Render check clean.

### THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST: `attendance_rule` IS ALSO THE PAY RULE

The `07ebd04d` plan told the reporter, in plain words, *"We are not touching how anything is calculated."* Neither the plan nor my brief noticed that **`attendance_rule` is the Schedule Group AND the lateness / early-out / overtime rule** — `late_grace_period_minutes`, `deductions_effective_from` and the whole `attendance_rule_ot_row` band table hang off it.

**Creating three bare groups would have silently re-priced all five shifts**, and that sentence would have been false the day it shipped. Migration 0483 now copies every calculation column and every OT band onto each new group, pinned by a mutation that fails when the copy is disabled. It also carries `deductions_effective_from`, unlike `copyAttendanceRule` which deliberately drops it — different case, and the reasoning is recorded in the migration header.

Two more judgement calls the agent made rather than assumed: the tenant's `is_default` "Standard" rule keeps NULL patterns by explicit predicate (a week on it would be imposed on every ungrouped shift in the tenant), and a fourth unapproved working week, a name collision, or any employment left behind in the emptied group **aborts the whole block** rather than half-applying.

### TWO DECISIONS RAISED TO THE REPORTER, NOT TAKEN HERE

- **`aec53564` — the shift form will edit a week that no longer decides anything.** After 0483 the group's week wins and each shift's stored week is dead weight: open a shift, change its Saturday, press Save, and the system accepts it, stores it, and changes nothing. Proved, not inferred — a passing test shows a group that does not work Saturday makes Saturday a rest day *even though the shift works it*. Two owners of one money-bearing fact is what §1 says to stop for. Recommended: the week is edited on the group and the day fields come off the shift form.
- **`048f1e9d` — the payslip identity panel.** The approved plan promised *"the employee details block is rebuilt"* and this round did not build it. Raised rather than left inside an item about to close. We did not guess at it on purpose: "make it more modern" does not say what it should look like, and a payslip is not a screen to redesign on a hunch.

### THE PAYSLIP: ONE NOTCH REPORTED, THREE DEFECTS FOUND — AND ONE OF THEM WAS OURS

⚠️ **CORRECTION OWED, AND IT REVERSES WHAT I TOLD THEM.** The rev-2 plan and commit `c1e84cd9` said the border notches were *"pre-existing, not an r328 regression"* and that `paintBox` *"was never touched"*. Verified against the source: **before r328** the row hairline was `x + 6 → x + p.w - 6`; **after r328** it is `x → x + p.w`. So r328 *did* touch `paintBox`, and widening that hairline turned a 0.5pt line over the 0.8pt bottom border from washing out the middle into washing out its whole length — **on Payment Information, which is one of the four boxes they circled**.

So: the NOTCH predates r328; the WASHED-OUT BOTTOM BORDER does not. Both are fixed. The source comment that carried my wrong claim is corrected where the next reader meets it.

Also found beyond the brief: **two bands per box, not one** (the header band and the total-row band, same construction) — reverting the fix reports **seven** offenders on a one-page payslip, not four. And `drawGrid` never had the defect at all; its band belongs to `drawEmployeePanel` and sits above the grid with no overlap.

**A better design than my instruction.** I wrote "test the election, not the amount" for `socsoSkbbk`. Not possible from a payslip — `subject_to_skbbk` lives only on `employee_statutory_my` and the run stamped only who *funded* the leg. The agent added a kernel stamp and then refused election-alone reasoning, because `null` on every existing payslip would drop a real deduction off a historical document whose printed total still counts it, and reading today's row would let unticking a box today rewrite last January. Shipped `subject === true || amount !== 0`.

### A LATENT BUG UNDER A READ I CALLED SOUND

My `72b100cd` brief presented `pcbPaymentsForYear` as the year-at-a-time read that "already exists". It had **no `ORDER BY`** on main — and an existing test asserted key order off a `Map`'s *insertion* order, a planner-order coin toss that happened to pass on one row. Fixed. §8 says it outright: any asserted array from a query needs `ORDER BY`.

Two more brief corrections: the one-writer guard I cited greps **raw** source, not comment-stripped — which matters exactly here, because the new files explain the one-writer rule in prose; and "new guarded page ⇒ new `SCREENS` column" overstates the rule, since the shelf's convention is to add the route to the existing column when the guard is identical (a separate column would let an admin grant PCB 2(II) while revoking the only place to maintain what it prints).

### WHAT WAS NOT DONE

### THE ROUND'S PATTERN: AGENTS CHECKED MY DOCUMENTS AND FOUND EIGHT ERRORS

r329's entry recorded three wrong briefs and promised I would verify premises before briefing. I did verify four this round — and the agents still found five more, because I verified what I thought to check rather than what the plan asserted in passing.

1. **ADR-0085 keyed its predicate on `statutory_report.ack_ref`.** The OWNED definition is `STATUTORY_FILED_STATUSES` (`db/schema.ts:6514`), whose own comment says it lives in the schema so two modules resolve against ONE list — *"two hand-kept copies of 'which statuses count as filed' is how a further status ships that only half the codebase believes in."* My design was that second copy.
2. **ADR-0085's "no new state machine" understated what exists.** `batchDownstreamWarnings` (`core/payroll.ts:874`) already computes `statutoryFiled` and feeds an amber banner on four screens. The step-2 predicate is deliberately wider, so **a month can read filed to the predicate and not-filed to the banner an operator is looking at** — a DECISION REQUIRED at step 4, now stated in the ADR.
3. **The two filed-signals do not share a visibility rule.** `statutory_report` is RLS'd tenant AND `is_admin_for(company)` (0026); `pcb_payment` is tenant-only (0476). A naive predicate answers from half the evidence and **fails OPEN on a money guard**.
4. **`scripts/report-schedule-group-split.ts` already existed** (r322 `142d049d`, amended r325). I briefed "write it". The agent upgraded it instead — it had never read `employment.attendance_rule_id`, missed the `default_shift_id` fallback, had no `ORDER BY`, and dated its filename off a UTC instant.
5. **`shift.day_type` / `category` are NOT read by the derivation engine.** I repeated the plan's claim; a grep returns ZERO and `db/schema.ts:4200` says "RECORDED ONLY in stage 1". Those files read `attendance.day_type`, a different column on a different table. DECISION: they do not move.
6. **`feedbackRequest` is at `db/schema.ts:7967`, not ~7847**, and **`raiseFeedback` is the operator CLI** (`scripts/improve/remote.ts`); the in-app writer is `submitFeedback`.
7. **My plan told the agent to stamp `reporter_label`. It refused, correctly** — that column exists to show who WROTE an item when the improvement loop borrows a human's employment. Here a real person presses a real button, so stamping would hide the actual author.
8. **The 0fe1ca2e headline was false** — see below.

### TWO CORRECTIONS OWED TO THE REPORTER, BOTH MEASURED, BOTH DELIVERED

**07ebd04d — I gave them a pay rate that is only conditionally true, in a plan AND in a picture.** `core/attendance.ts` ~1020's off-day → 1.5× branch sits in the DEFAULT-SHIFT step, reached only when the date has NO roster row. ### THE DEPLOY OOMed, AND THE DESIGN HELD

`deploy.sh` exit **137** (SIGKILL) during type-checking on a 3.9 GB box. Production was untouched: `stale_build=1`, `.next` still r329's, service still serving the old build, **nothing marked deployed**. The cause was a **2.7 GB orphaned build process** (parent PID 1) left by the kill, holding the memory a retry needed. Identified positively against `systemctl show aihr -p MainPID` before touching it, killed that PID alone: available memory **203 MB → 2,860 MB**, service up throughout, retry clean.

### ADR-0085 — signed statutory deltas, and a defect it found today

The codebase asked for this by name: `localization/my/multicycle.ts` says closing the EPF gap "needs the reversals ADR, not a code change here". **The clamp is already producing a wrong figure** — the EPF Third Schedule steps the employer column DOWN 13%→12% at RM5,000, so RM5,000 alone is RM650 and RM5,050 alone is RM612, but RM5,000 then RM50 clamps to RM650 + RM0 and ends **RM38 OVER the published table**. The same clamp is what makes `23e7dac3` unbuildable. **One clamp, two problems.**

The decision leans on a seam that exists: `pay_period.status` separates assembling from closed, `statutory_report.ack_ref` / `pcb_payment` record what was filed. **A delta may go negative while unfiled; once filed it is an amendment and is refused by name.** No payslip prints a negative statutory line; banked net pay is never reduced.

⚠️ **STEP 1 FOUND A DEFECT LIVE TODAY.** `docs/audits/0085-delta-keys-sign-inventory.md`: four sites render a statutory line only when `> 0` (`lib/payslip-pdf.ts:675` and the three payslip screens), so a negative would make the line **VANISH** rather than print wrong. All four are `socsoSkbbk` — and `subject_to_skbbk` is a real boolean election, so `> 0` is standing in for "this employee does not have it". **An employee who HAS SKBBK and contributed 0.00 is indistinguishable from one who does not.** Wrong today, independent of the ADR. Negative results recorded too: no unsigned column, no `CHECK (>= 0)`, no stray `Math.abs`.

### ADVERSARIAL VERIFY FOUND WHAT A GREEN REPORT DID NOT

Every agent's non-vacuity claim was re-derived here rather than accepted. Four held. One did not:

**`a96d320c`'s two OT equality gates were UNGUARDED.** They decide whether a payslip may print "2 hours × MYR 18.75" beside an overtime figure. Replacing the copy gate (`core/payroll.ts` ~5887) with `true` left **11/11 green**; dropping the write gate (~2775) left **61/61 green**. The agent had sincerely proved the derivation is WRITTEN and is READ — neither is a proof that the gate REFUSES. Sent back; now pinned by 7 new guards across `overtime-provenance` and `pay-component-1a`, tests-only (0 lines under `core/ lib/ localization/ db/ messages/`).

⚠️ **CONSEQUENCE THE REPORTER WILL SEE, and it is not a defect:** `minutes/60` survives 2-dp rounding only when the minute count is a **multiple of three**. Quarter-hours keep their caption; OT derived from raw clock-in/out times usually will not. The gate refuses rather than lies and no money moves, so "the payslip shows the hours and the rate" is not universally true on day one. **Do not loosen the gate.** Storing `qty` at higher precision does not fix it either — printing "1.67 hours × 18.75" still fails to reconcile to 31.25 on the page. The honest fix is to print **1 h 40 m × MYR 18.75/h**, where the product is exact. Not done; recorded.

### A LIVE STATUTORY DEFECT FROM r323, FOUND WHILE CHECKING SOMETHING ELSE

`localization/my/pcb2ii.ts` took the employer's **E-number, months and receipts** from `p.companyId` but the **legal name and address** from the employment's CURRENT company. Identical for anyone who never transferred — which is why it shipped green — and different for exactly the case the parameter exists for. **After an entity transfer, company A's PCB 2(II) printed A's deducted months and A's employer number under B's letterhead**: a statement of tax filed under a name that did not deduct it. `eaStatement` gets this right two files away and says so; PCB 2(II) had not copied it. Fixed, plus a refusal — an employer that neither employs the person now nor paid them in the year returns `null`, which both routes turn into a bare 404. Reverting the fix turns **8 of 23** tests red.

### PRODUCTION ANSWERED TWO QUESTIONS THE AGENTS COULD NOT REACH

The auto-mode classifier refuses agents production reads, so both flagged their gaps honestly. One hypothesis held, one did not:

- **`a96d320c`: confirmed.** No lateness pay component exists (nothing in `pay_component` matches late/lewat), and `late_deduct_minutes > 0` on **0 of 299** attendance rows. Its generic `payRuleQuantityAndRate` design was right, and its finding that the kernel never reads `late_deduct_minutes` holds in the data as well as the grep.
- **`05d2709a`: overturned, and what is really there is worse.** Its guess was that duplicates are created with the IC left blank because the unique index refuses it. Measured: 29 of 32 duplicate records HAVE an IC (9% blank vs 10.7% across all active employments). Every duplicate group shares **name, hire date AND date of birth**, with ICs identical except the **last two digits** — and a MyKad opens with the birth date, which matches the DOB column in all seven groups. **Somebody worked around the unique index by nudging the trailing digits, so production holds wrong national identity numbers on records that file EPF, SOCSO and LHDN returns.** That is a finding for the merge round, not a tidiness note.

So the IC stopped being excluded and became the strongest evidence on the screen — not as equality (which the index makes impossible) but as **birth-date near-identity**, resolved through the country-pack seam (`packFor`, never a `localization/my` import; fail-closed to `not_comparable` on an unknown or mixed jurisdiction). Asked whether it can fire on genuinely different people, the agent answered **yes — twins** and wrote that into the docblock and the screen rather than hiding it.

## r327 (2026-09-22) — The statutory bodies become one list, and SOCSO+EIS one GROUP rather than one setting. `main@46366c14`, **no migration**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `efe424b0`. Gate: **940 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, every chunk exit 0 and counted in full. `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. Shadow **not run and not needed**: `git diff --name-only main..HEAD` matches nothing under `db/migrations`.

### WHAT THE TICKET ASKED FOR, AND THE ONE PART OF IT I REFUSED

The item asked to consolidate the company statutory settings. SOCSO and EIS look like one thing on that screen — same authority, same employer code, filed together — and the obvious reading is "make them one configuration".

**I measured the data before agreeing, and that reading is wrong.** EIS carries its own payment row, and on this tenant it DIFFERS from SOCSO's: `SMSB_EIS` against `SMSB_SOCSO`. Merging the two configurations would have stranded a live payment setting — silently, because the surviving row would look complete.

So they became one ROW, not one CONFIGURATION: SOCSO is the row, EIS is a subordinate line beneath it (`pl-6`, a `⌟` glyph rather than a second authority mark), and both keep their own settings behind their own controls. The consultant gets the grouping they asked to see; the payment account nobody mentioned stays where it is.

### THE REST OF THE SCREEN

- The bodies stop being a grid and become **one divided list** (`divide-y` inside a single bordered block), which is what made the subordinate row legible in the first place — a grid has no way to say "this belongs under that".
- **Seven authority logos** ship as real files under `public/statutory/`, each referenced and each serving 200 at its exact byte count on a dev server before the gate ran.
- **LHDN is renamed "Income Tax (LHDN)"**, in all six locales. The authority's initials are not what the consultant calls the thing.
- **`koperasi` is retired** from `lib/statutory-authorities.ts`, with the measurement that justified it recorded in the comment beside the deletion rather than in a commit message nobody re-reads.

### TWO RED CHUNKS, BOTH GENUINE — AND ONE OF THEM BREAKS MY OWN HEURISTIC

**Chunk 1 had ZERO AssertionErrors and was still a real failure.** `Error: Unknown statutory authority: koperasi`, thrown by a fixture that still named the authority I had just retired. The standing rule in §4 — zero assertion errors means the environment, not the code — has exactly this exception, and it is worth keeping written down: a THROWN error is a real failure that the AssertionError count cannot see. Fixed by swapping the fixture to `ptptn` and adding a case that pins the refusal itself, so retiring an authority now makes it unwritable by test as well as by type.

**Chunk 7 had one AssertionError, and it was the rename.** The new label is `SOCSO & EIS (PERKESO)`; React escapes a text child, so the markup carries `SOCSO &amp; EIS (PERKESO)`, and the six-locale render check compared the raw catalogue value. The browser shows the ampersand — the dev-server render check had already confirmed that — but the test could never match. **Escaped the EXPECTED side rather than unescaping the received one**, so the assertion stays exact, and proved it non-vacuous by truncating the component's label at `" & "` and watching the same assertion fail. Applied to the descriptions and the Open-control count too: any of them can gain an ampersand tomorrow.

### GUARDS UPDATED, NONE DELETED

- `test/statutory-authority.test.ts` — fixture `koperasi` → `ptptn`, plus a new case refusing retired, nonsense and empty authorities.
- `test/company-panel-bank-statutory-layout.test.ts` — the grid assertion becomes a divided-list assertion. **The negation was also NARROWED**: it had forbidden a bare `sm:col-span-2`, which caught legitimate in-form field layouts that have nothing to do with the statutory block. It now targets `xl:col-span-3`, which is the thing that actually means "back to a grid".

### WHAT WAS NOT DONE

- **The 153-line statutory form was not extracted.** Grouping the rows achieved what the ticket asked for; extracting the form is a refactor the ticket did not ask for and would have put a large untested move inside a round about presentation.
- **No migration, so no shadow run.** If a later round gives EIS its own first-class configuration, that IS a migration and this round's grouping is the thing it has to keep working.

### THE GATE GOT 2.7× FASTER MID-ROUND, AND THE REASON IS WORTH RECORDING

### THEY CONTESTED r324 AND THEY WERE RIGHT TWICE

r324 built a Discard on the per-month EDIT screen, and only for drafts. It built a month picker and put it on the VIEWING screen beside Add. From where the reporter sits there was no Delete at all, and the year and month sat where records are read rather than created. Both are ours; neither needed explaining twice.

### DELETE, IN THE COLUMN THAT ALREADY EXISTED

The Transaction History's Actions column has held a View link all along. Delete joins it as a **LINK to a server-rendered confirmation** — not a submit. Two reasons, and the second is the load-bearing one: the reporter asked to be asked first, and a server action handed to that client island as a prop returns a 500 on every request while tsc, the suite and `next build` all stay green (r123's defect, already recorded on the TP1 form). It also works with no JavaScript at all.

ONE ACTION ON THE SCREEN, TWO SERVICES BEHIND IT, CHOSEN BY STATUS. A draft goes to `discardTp1DraftForPerson`; a submitted or approved row to `cancelTp1ForPerson`. Each service's refusal IS the audit meaning of that state — nobody was ever told about a draft, whereas a declared row was declared and then withdrawn — so the screen routes and neither contract loosens. A rejected row offers no Delete: both services refuse one, and an action that can only end in a refusal is worse than none.

⚠️ **STILL NOT A ROW DELETE**, and they were told so in the plan before approving. `tp1CountableWhere` already requires `'approved'`, so a cancelled row stops feeding payroll the moment it is written — no second exclusion to keep in step. "Removed from the transaction history" means it leaves the LIST, with a Show-deleted toggle carried on the url so the choice survives a refresh.

### THE COLLAPSE KEY, WHICH IS WHERE THIS COULD HAVE GONE QUIETLY WRONG

Showing every year meant `listTp1DeclarationsForPersonYear` lost its year fence. That read collapses the append-only rows to one per month, counting the rest as `versions` — and it keyed on the MONTH ALONE. Sound while fenced to one year; silently wrong the moment it is not: **January 2025 and January 2026 share a bucket, one is reported as a "version" of the other, and a whole year's declaration vanishes from the history while inflating another's count.**

The key gained the year. Verified by putting the old one back and watching a January disappear.

### ADD NEW TP1 ASKS FIRST, AND WRITES NOTHING

A step that resolves a year and a month and then **redirects** to the declaration form that already exists. A second write path to `tp1_relief` is the one thing it must not become, and that is pinned. A year and month that already has a record opens THAT record, because the destination is the same href the history links each row to — which makes "Add never overwrites" a property of the destination rather than a promise.

### SEVEN GUARD ASSERTIONS UPDATED, NONE DELETED

Four of r324's own cases pinned the month control on the viewing screen. Three in `test/tp1-relief-redesign.test.ts` pinned the rest of the old shape, one of them commented *"because the list is now scoped to one year by the selector"* — the exact sentence the reporter contested. In every case what the assertion protects is unchanged and still asserted; where it protects it has moved. The one-row-per-month case GAINED the cross-year half, so the collapse key is now pinned from the screen as well as from the service.

`VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1` throughout, ~240s a chunk. That setting is what bought a clean 14-chunk run: at 2 workers the previous two rounds lost four chunks apiece to zero-AssertionError timeouts. ~0.8 GB free RAM and 35 GB of 35.8 GB swap; the 8 GB RAM disk still refuses to detach.

## r325 (2026-09-22) — the last date-from-an-instant, and the answer to the Saturday question. `main@329b128a`, **no migration**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `fc88ba08`. Gate: **940 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, every chunk exit 0 and counted in full. `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, shadow PASS 392/392. Deployed first attempt: `exit_code=0`, `stale_build=0`, §3 dry-run zero lines, `GET /` 401.

### THE THIRD AND LAST OF THE FAMILY

`core/employment-review.ts` stamped `decidedOn` from an instant in UTC, so a decision recorded between midnight and 08:00 MYT read back as the previous day. r299 fixed `approvedOn` in `core/toil.ts`; r324 fixed `requestedOn` at two sites in `core/attendance.ts`. A sweep of `core/`, `packs/`, `lib/` and `test/` found this one and nothing else — every other `toISOString().slice(0, 10)` is calendar arithmetic on a Z-anchored midnight, which carries no timezone at all.

⚠️ **THE GUARD PINS THE TIMEZONE, NOT JUST A DATE, and that is the whole lesson of all three.** The existing tests compared the read against a value derived the SAME wrong way, so they agreed with the bug for sixteen hours out of twenty-four. Every case now uses an instant whose UTC and KL dates DIFFER, plus a file-wide arm refusing any `<x>At/On.toISOString().slice(0, 10)` — verified against the old line, the new line and a legitimate arithmetic line, so it is neither vacuous nor over-broad.

### THE QUESTION THE REPORTER ASKED US, ANSWERED FROM THE ENGINE

They unblocked `07ebd04d` with a full design and one question back: *"'Saturday not at all' and 'Saturday Off Day' may produce different attendance/roster behaviour in your system."*

**They do, and the difference is paid.** `shiftDayKindFor` is a four-way classifier — a weekday in `weekly_pattern` is FULL, in `half_pattern` HALF, in `off_pattern` OFF, and one in NONE of the three is REST (rest is the complement, which is what "not ticked" has always meant). Both rest and off are non-working, but `core/attendance.ts` ~980 routes an OFF day through `policyBranch('workday')` with zero scheduled minutes while REST goes through `policyBranch('rest_day')` — and the rate table is workday 1.5, rest_day 2.0, holiday 3.0.

So merging a Saturday-rest shift with a Saturday-off shift into one Schedule Group would change somebody's Saturday overtime rate with nobody deciding it. Their instinct to keep them apart was right.

### AND THE BLAST RADIUS IS SMALL, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART

Their answer set seven conditions, and step 4 is **get confirmation before migration**. So this round ships steps 2 and 3 and nothing else: `scripts/report-schedule-group-split.ts` is READ-ONLY and prints each shift's week AS THE ENGINE READS IT, so the distinction is visible rather than asserted.

Measured on production: **"Standard" splits into 3 groups, and 5 employees hold an open arrangement across them.** Group 1 (Sat=rest) has AARON AZIZ, Arjun Kumar and LSL; group 2 (Sat=off) has Aisyah Rahman and Eee Lee Yong — **those two are the whole population whose Saturday rate is at stake**; group 3 (Sat=half) has nobody. `A02` needs no split and has nobody on it.

### THE DRIFT RATCHET CAUGHT ME, WHICH IS THE RATCHET WORKING

The new script imported `core/attendance` directly for `shiftDayKindFor`. `test/attendance-pack-drift.test.ts` refused it, and its allowlist **only ever shrinks** — so the fix was the pack facade, not an exemption. Same discipline `scripts/report-a2c-hire-year-deltas.ts` already follows for the leave engine.

### THE MACHINE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT COST AN HOUR

The gate ran with **~0.1 GB free RAM and 33 GB of 33.8 GB swap used**, and the 8 GB RAM disk — unused, the cluster having been rebuilt on SSD — **refused to detach**: `Resource busy` through `diskutil eject`, `unmount`, `unmount force` and `hdiutil detach -force`, with `lsof` showing no holder (most likely the endpoint-security agent's volume reference). Escalating further was declined in favour of not touching the machine.

`VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1` made every chunk reliable at ~250s instead of ~120s. Four chunks first reported red; **all four had ZERO AssertionErrors** and passed on a foreground re-run with an identical test count. §4's rule held for the third round running: assertion count first, and a chunk with none is not evidence about the code.

### NOT DONE

`8cd601d0` stays behind `07ebd04d` — the reporter says so themselves: *"the earlier Schedule Group/Shift data needs to be cleaned or restructured before building Schedule Assignment."* Three items are contested (`72b100cd`, `a57f0584`, `0fe1ca2e`) and one approved (`27605faa`, revision 2); none was started, because a half-built round beside a mid-flight gate is how both get lost.

## r324 (2026-09-22) — TP1 Relief, and a date bug that only exists before breakfast. `main@8665c6e2`, **no migration**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `27605faa`. Gate: **939 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, every chunk exit 0 and counted in full. `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, shadow PASS 392/392. Deployed first attempt: `exit_code=0`, `stale_build=0`, §3 dry-run zero lines, `GET /` 401.

### TWO OF THE THREE REPORTED PREMISES WERE WRONG, AND THE PLAN SAID SO BEFORE APPROVAL

- **"Allow Admin to delete a record"** — a submitted or approved declaration could ALREADY be cancelled, which is right for a tax record because it keeps the history. A **DRAFT could not be removed by any means at all**: `cancelTp1ForPerson` refuses anything not submitted or approved, and production held two unreachable drafts. The real gap was wider than reported. `discardTp1DraftForPerson` refuses every status except draft and goes through the SAME `decide()` writer — status `cancelled`, never a row DELETE. Discard and cancel stay separate because they mean different things: **nobody has been told about a draft**.
- **"The deduction month is automatically the current month"** — it never was. The month is the `[month]` path segment and any month was reachable. The one place it was imposed was the "+ Add New TP1" button: `const addMonth = selectedYear === currentYear ? … : 1`. **That constant was the whole fault.** The current month stays the default; it is no longer the only answer. A month outside 1–12 falls back rather than being honoured, and the options are named through the screen's own `monthFmt`.

### THE HOLE NOBODY ASKED ABOUT, AND WHY IT BELONGED IN THIS ROUND

`requireAdminTarget` checked `isAdmin` and **nothing else**, so an administrator could approve their **own** tax relief. TP1 reduces PCB, which is money, and attendance (`assertCanDecide`) and leave both already refuse a decider who is the subject.

Closed in `approveTp1ForPerson` and **NOT** in the new one-press action: putting it there would have left the two-step screen — the same buttons, one page apart — still able to do it. The rule is `assertCanDecide`'s, mirrored **including its escape hatch** (blocked for hr_admin, allowed for super_admin) so a company whose only administrator is also an employee is not stranded. When the refusal fires the declaration stays **SUBMITTED**: the work is not lost, it needs a second person.

Safe to close because it was measured first: two approvals on production carry an approver, **zero are self-approved**. It belonged in THIS round because this round adds the one press, and a one-press hole is a different animal from a two-screen one.

### A DATE BUG FOUND BY RUNNING THE GATE AT 01:07

⚠️ **PRE-EXISTING, NOT PART OF THE ITEM, AND DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND.** A chunk went red in `test/replacement-leave-controls.test.ts`. It failed **on `main` too**, which is what turned it from a flake into an investigation.

`core/attendance.ts` derived a DATE from an INSTANT in UTC at two sites (`requestedOn`, on the correction and plan paths). That is what §8 forbids, and it is the exact bug **r299 already fixed ONE LINE AWAY** in `core/toil.ts` for `approvedOn` — whose own comment reads *"the UTC date froze an expiry one day early for any approval between midnight and 08:00 in Malaysia."*

So a replacement-leave credit banked in that window carried a **Request Date a day early while the EXPIRY on the same row was resolved in Kuala Lumpur**: one accrual, two dates disagreeing about what day it was. TOIL is leave credit, so it is money-adjacent.

**Two test files carried the same fault on the assertion side**, deriving their expectation with `.toISOString()` — which §8 forbids *"fixtures included"*. They agreed with the code for sixteen hours a day, which is why all of this survived this long: **the existing tests would have passed either way.**

### SWEPT, AND ONE DELIBERATELY LEFT

Every other `toISOString().slice(0, 10)` in `core/`, `packs/` and `lib/` is calendar arithmetic on a Z-anchored midnight — timezone-free and correct. In `test/`, the only other hit round-trips a date the fixture supplies explicitly.

**One genuine instance remains and was NOT fixed here**: `core/employment-review.ts:492` stamps `decidedOn` the same way. It is display-only, in a subsystem this round does not otherwise touch, and shipping an untested fix alongside an unrelated item is how a scoped round stops being one. Raised as `fc88ba08` with a plan and a recommendation, so the decision is the reporter's.

### NOT DONE

Nothing outstanding on the item. The PCB 2(II) picker's empty population (r323) remains shared pre-existing behaviour, unchanged.

## r323 (2026-09-21) — PCB 2(II), the form r321 left building. `main@0c362da9`, **no migration**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `72b100cd`. Gate: **938 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, every chunk exit 0 and counted in full, GREEN ON THE FIRST PASS. `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, shadow PASS 392/392. Deployed on the second attempt (see below): `exit_code=0`, `stale_build=0`, §3 dry-run zero lines, `GET /` 401.

r321 built the SOURCE and said in as many words that the form would follow; the item stayed `building` rather than being closed on a half-delivery. This closes it.

### BUILT FROM THE SPECIMENS, NOT FROM THE TICKET'S PROSE

The reporter attached LHDN's own English and BM sheets. Both were extracted from `feedback_attachment` and read page by page before anything was written — `\copy` corrupts them, so the base64 route from r321 was reused (exact byte counts, valid `%%EOF`). Three things came out of reading them that the ticket does not say:

- **The English sheet heads a column MTD; the Malay sheet heads the same column PCB.** Same figure, two official names. The BM sheet also says `Kepada:`, not `To:`. Anyone tidying those into one label is changing what the form says.
- The first column is headed **"Year"** on the English sheet and **"Bulan"** on the Malay one — transcribed as published rather than corrected.
- The Total row is boxed under the two Amount columns **only**.

### AN EMPTY BOX AND A ZERO ARE DIFFERENT STATEMENTS TO LHDN

Carried end to end rather than asserted once. An amount is `number | null`: a month with no payroll prints **nothing**; a month whose payroll ran and deducted nothing prints **0.00**. The totals follow — twelve absent months total to NOTHING, because summing them to `0.00` would turn twelve absent statements into one positive claim that no tax was deducted all year. Every amount goes through `pcb2iiAmount()` and **the renderer contains no `toFixed` at all**, which is pinned.

### THE DATING RULE IS CP39's, IMPORTED

Both forms report the same deductions to the same body, so a second dating rule here would let two of our own documents disagree about which month a month's tax belongs to. `cp39DeductionPeriodFor`'s own header warns exactly this, and the test pins both that it is imported and that `epfContributionPeriodFor` is nowhere near it.

### SECTION 3 IS EMPTY BY REFUSAL

The third table wants prior-year income and the MTD attributable to it. `back_pay_line.affected_period` can identify such arrears, but PCB is computed on a whole month's pay and splitting it would be **an apportionment nobody performed, printed on a tax document**. Measured on production: zero back-pay lines whose affected period is an earlier year. The three ruled rows print blank, as the published form ships them, and `priorYearRows` exists so there is one place to fill the day that attribution becomes real.

### THE RENDER CHECK EARNED ITS PLACE AGAIN

The picker reused the EA's `eaNoneForYear`, so an empty year on a PCB 2(II) screen said *"there is no **EA statement** to produce"*. It typechecked, the suite stayed green and `next build` stayed green. Only rendering the screen and reading the sentence showed it.

Two layout faults were also caught by looking at the output beside the specimen: the sub-column rules ran up through the grouped headings and sliced them (`Receipt Date/Tr|ansaction`), and receipt references were being clipped — the identifier LHDN matches a payment by. Group boundaries now rule full height and sub-splits start below the heading; the receipt columns are the widest on the sheet.

### DEPLOY FAILED ONCE, AND THE BOX'S OWN GUARD HELD

First attempt: `next build` compiled in 106s then the **TypeScript worker was OOM-killed** (SIGKILL) on the 3.8 GB box, leaving `state=failed`, `exit_code=1`, `stale_build=1`. Production was untouched and still serving r322 — which is exactly what §7 says an OOM does. Re-run unchanged it succeeded. Worth remembering: the box has 3.8 GB and 3.8 GB of swap, and `next build` there is close enough to the edge that a transient spike loses it.

### NOT DONE, AND SAID PLAINLY

The **employee picker lists nobody on the demo tenant**, because its population is `my.cp8d` — and the EA screen, which has used that same population since r256, shows the identical empty state on the identical data. So this is pre-existing shared behaviour, not something this round introduced; it was verified by running both screens side by side rather than assumed. The part this round owns — read, model, labels, renderer, download route — was exercised end to end and returns valid PDFs in both languages.

`branch` and the officer/designation/telephone block are rendered as the form's own blank ruled lines: nothing in this repo records an LHDN branch or a signing officer for this statement, and inventing either on a tax form is the one thing §8 forbids outright.

`07ebd04d`'s own approved plan required a READ-ONLY comparison before any migration, and it earned its place. Schedule Group **"Standard" holds five shifts that disagree about Saturday**: three ignore it, `AM02` makes it a HALF day, `MB28 SAG MORNING FULL` makes it an OFF day. A group cannot own a working week until somebody says which week it is, and picking one would have silently changed who is rostered on Saturdays.

Put to the reporter as two options with a recommendation: name the week, or — more likely — these are separate Schedule Groups wearing one name. `8cd601d0` is blocked behind it, because "assign by group, refuse a shift outside it" means nothing until the group carries the pattern.

`fdfd8ec7` is a DATA task and its plan said so. Measured today: 75 active employees, **55 needing attention — 48 missing both gender and marital status, 7 missing gender only, none missing marital status alone**. That last figure is the useful one: it is one gap ("these profiles were never completed"), not two problems. It now opens on every authorised company; the picker narrows rather than decides. Verified on a dev server: 6 + 2 = **8**, and the Company column appears only when more than one company is on screen.
- **`f728826a`** reported overlapping columns as one fault. There were TWO, and fixing either alone still leaves overlap: `w-full` squeezed 29 nowrap columns below content width, and three frozen columns sat at `left-0` / `left-[7rem]` / `left-[19rem]` with **no width on any of them**.

### A PROXY THAT WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS

`f728826a`'s real lesson. `7 + 12 = 19` held only if the first two columns really were 7rem and 12rem, and nothing made them so. The offset is no longer written down: `lib/sticky-columns.ts` derives it as the running sum of the declared widths, and the same number is applied as the width, so the two cannot disagree.

The guards told the same story. `test/cp39-form.test.ts` (r321) counted `<form ` as a stand-in for "no form nests"; **verified, that count PASSES two genuinely nested forms when a third sibling is deleted in the same change**. `test/dde08629` pinned Daily's `left-[7rem]` literal — the very assumption that was the bug. Both now measure the property instead of a symptom of it.

`a0b90c81`. An earlier round promised to hide the six Special Leave reason cards. `visible_to_employee` hides a card AND removes the type from Request Leave — one flag, two consequences — so honouring that promise would have deleted every Special Leave reason from the apply dropdown, including the per-reason Apply buttons shipped alongside it. `dae7a10f`. An administrator now fixes a day in one action. It calls `requestAttendanceCorrection` then `decideAttendanceCorrection` — the SAME services the two-step calls — never a direct write, because approval re-derives the day through the time engine so corrected OT reaches payroll. **The permission barrier the ticket assumed does not exist**: `assertCanDecide` blocks the SUBJECT, not the requester, so an admin deciding somebody else's correction was always allowed.

⚠️ Self-correction still refuses, **and the request survives the refusal as pending** — the work is not lost, it needs another approver. An admin is very often also an employee; swallowing that refusal would let one approve their own overtime.

## r321 (2026-09-21) — what the employer actually PAID LHDN, which nothing here recorded. `main@f24fdbee`, **migration 0476**.

`72b100cd` stays **building**, deliberately: this round ships the SOURCE for PCB 2(II), not the form. Deployed anyway rather than held — the payment references can be keyed from today, and gated code sitting unmerged is how main and production drift apart. Gate: **933 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, every chunk exit 0 and counted in full. `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, shadow **PASS 392/392**. Deployed: `exit_code=0`, `stale_build=0`, `GET /` 401, `pcb_payment` present, 392 applied on the box.

### WHY A TABLE AND NOT `statutory_report.ack_ref`

That column is ONE acknowledgement for the **return** — the CP39 lodgement. A payment is a different act. An employer may pay more than once against a single return, LHDN issues a receipt per payment, and PCB 2(II) prints **MTD and CP38 in separate columns**. One reference cannot express that, so widening it would have made the field mean two things depending on who read it.

Measured on production before deciding: all six CP39 rows are `status=draft` with `ack_ref` and `filed_on` NULL. Nothing was lost by leaving that column alone — the alternative was reinterpreting a field nobody has used yet.

### AN ABSENT BOX IS NOT A ZERO

A month with nothing recorded is **absent from the map**, never `0.00`. On a tax form those are different statements to LHDN: an absent box asserts nothing, a zero asserts the money does not exist (§8). The renderer in the next round has to be able to tell them apart, so the service must not flatten them now. The receipt reference is also deliberately **excluded from the event payload** — it is evidence, not telemetry.

No format check is imposed on the reference itself. This repo cannot verify LHDN's receipt format, and policing one would be inventing third-party behaviour — the same decision `ack_ref` already records.

### A GUARD UPDATED, NOT LOOSENED — AND THE PROXY WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS

`test/cp39-form.test.ts` asserted `<form ` appeared **exactly twice** on the CP39 preview, as a cheap stand-in for "no form nests inside another". The payment card is a third, flat sibling: the proxy failed while the property it stood for still held.

Counting was simply the wrong instrument. It fails on a legitimate sibling — and, verified rather than asserted, it **passes two genuinely nested forms** if a third is deleted in the same change (that case reads 2). Nesting is now measured directly, and the thing the count was really protecting — that the three downloads share ONE form, which is what makes them buttons carrying their own `formAction` — is pinned explicitly.

### THE FALSE RED, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WILL RECUR

Chunk 14 first reported red: 8 files, 11 tests, **zero AssertionErrors**, at 1907s against ~80s for every other chunk — seven hook timeouts, a deadlock and a failed query across eight suites with nothing to do with CP39. Cause: board pulls running beside a *background* chunk. Re-run alone in the foreground it passed 66/66 with **the same 1035 test count**, in 84s. The §4 rule earned its place again: assertion count first, and a background gate is not evidence.

### NOT DONE

The PCB 2(II) form itself. It is per-employee (TP1's shape, not a batch table), so it needs its own screen, and it moves `lhdn.pcb2ii-en` / `lhdn.pcb2ii-ms` out of `MY_PLANNED_FORMS` into `MY_REPORTS` at `fidelity: 'agency-layout'` — CP22 is the only `'official'` row and a test pins that.

What was genuinely missing was the workflow: employee, Date From and Date To all sat in one filter row, so looking at the next person meant going back to the top and starting again.

- **The panel is fed from the SAME `listEmployees(s, scopeIds)` read** the dropdown used, and the selection is still re-guarded against that list before any read uses it. A panel-shaped list must not become a second, wider source of employees.

The open/closed state is read from a cookie **on the server**, so the first paint is already correct rather than flashing open and folding; the cookie is this screen's own, so collapsing it says nothing about any other screen's.

Rendered on a dev server: the panel with its search box, the old `<select name="emp">` gone, 29 table headers and 57 sticky cells intact, no `MISSING_MESSAGE`.

Further filtering of the employee list by company or department. The ticket mentions it in passing; the list is already scoped to the caller's own authorised companies, so a second filter layer on top of that is a deliberate decision and the plan put it to the reporter instead of guessing.
