## r318 (2026-09-21) — a way in to the Special Leave reasons. `main@dbda227f`, **no migration**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `76dbcaa1` (partly — see what is NOT done). Gate: **931 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, every chunk exit 0 and counted in full. `next build` exit 0. Deployed: `exit_code=0`, `built_ref` dbda227f.

### MOST OF THE ITEM WAS ALREADY BUILT, AND THE PLAN SAID SO BEFORE APPROVAL

Measured on production first: `leave_shared_group` already held ONE group — "Special Leave", 10.00 days, 3.00 per application — and `leave_shared_group_member` already held exactly the six types the ticket lists. The pooled card already existed (46afcc48) and the engine already enforced the ceiling. What was missing was a way IN to the reasons, and a picker that did not read as seven unrelated entitlements.

### WHAT SHIPPED

- `sharedLeaveGroupBalances` exposes `members` with ids, built in the SAME pass as `memberNames`, so the picker and the card cannot disagree about who is in the pool. Hidden members are included, because hiding a card is a presentation choice and a reason list that dropped half the pot would describe a different pot.
- **The Request Leave picker groups a pooled type under its pool's name.** A LABEL: it still posts one `leaveTypeId`, so nothing the engine enforces changes.
- **`/leave/shared/[groupId]`** — the employee's own pooled figure with the policy as context, and one Apply per reason linking into the EXISTING apply form via `?applyType=`, seeded and never trusted. It rides the `leave` access column rather than minting a second one carrying the same label (the 570fd56e precedent).

Rendered as a seeded employee: 200 with one Apply link per reason, a bogus group id 404s, no `MISSING_MESSAGE`.

### ⚠️ THE CARD-HIDING COULD NOT BE DONE AS PLANNED, AND NOTHING WAS WRITTEN

The plan promised: *"Hide the six reason cards from My Leave… Nobody loses access to anything - every reason stays available through Special Leave."* **That promise cannot be kept with the switch that exists.**

- `leave_type.ess_placement` refuses `'hidden'` outright — `STORABLE_PLACEMENTS` is `primary | secondary`; hidden is a RESOLVED value, not a storable one. The UPDATE was refused by the CHECK constraint and rolled back.
- The switch that does hide a card is `visible_to_employee = false`, and **`mayAppearInApplyMenu` excludes any type whose resolved placement is `hidden`**. So hiding the six cards would also remove every Special Leave reason from the Request Leave dropdown — making this round's own Apply links dead ends.

In this system, hiding a balance card and withdrawing the right to apply are **the same flag**. The plan assumed they were separable; they are not.

**THE FIX IS A BETTER ONE THAN A SETTING, AND IT IS RAISED RATHER THAN SLIPPED IN:** a member of a PLACED shared group should not draw its own balance card, because its balance is the pool's — derived from membership that already exists, automatic for any future shared group (which the reporter asked for), impossible to misconfigure, and it does not touch the apply menu at all. That is a change to `leaveBalances`' self-service path and belongs in its own round with its own gate.

### ALSO NOT DONE

The **Compassionate / Congratulatory sub-grouping**. Nothing in the data says which reason sits under which heading, and hardcoding the mapping is what the ticket itself forbids (*"read the conditions from the leave type configuration"*). Where it should be STORED is the reporter's decision. The detail screen lists the reasons under the pool that owns them.

The **two-step Request Leave wizard**. The picker groups the reasons under Special Leave, which delivers *"do not expose every database leave type as a flat list"*, but it is one control and not two steps.

## r316 (2026-09-21) — a missing profile field is not a failed qualification. `main@90b6fa6e`, **no migration**.

Gate: **930 files — equal to the suite file count — 14,205 tests**, 14 chunks, every chunk exit 0 and counted in full. `next build` exit 0. Deployed: `exit_code=0`, `built_ref` 90b6fa6e.

### r315 SHIPPED A REGRESSION AND THE DRY RUN CAUGHT IT, NOT THE SUITE

r315's identity gate read an **unrecorded** attribute as an **excluded** one, because `isProfileEligible` compared `emp.gender ?? ''` against the configured list — the shape `isLeaveEligible` has always had.

The first production dry run of the reversal sweep is what exposed it: it proposed reversing **105 pairs / 7,696.50 days**, of which **33 pairs / 472.50 days were ANNUAL**. `ANNUAL` lists *every* gender, so the only way to fail it is to have none recorded — and **55 of 75 active employees have no gender**. The sweep would have taken real Annual Leave off 33 people because a field is blank.

**The same flaw was in the grant.** Six LIVE types (CGL, CPL, EXM, GD, NDL, STD) list `["male","female"]`, a list that restricts nobody. At the next year-open, r315's gate would have granted those 55 employees **nothing on all six**. The suite was green throughout.

`isProfileEligible` now takes an explicit `UnknownAttributePolicy` **with no default**, so no caller can avoid deciding:

- **`'exclude'`** — DISPLAY only (the balance card). Unchanged behaviour, and what the reporter was told in writing: an incomplete profile loses the card.
- **`'allow'`** — anything that GRANTS OR TAKES AWAY DAYS. A missing fact is not a missing qualification. A **recorded contradiction still refuses**, so the relaxation is not a hole.

The trade is stated in the test: we would rather grant a day we may have to take back than withhold one we owe.

## r315 (2026-09-21) — the year-open grant asks who the leave type is for. `main@5b278d2d`, **no migration**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `508d3acd`. Gate: **930 files, 14,202 tests**, 14 chunks green. `next build` exit 0.

### THE REPORTED FAULT WAS A DISPLAY BUG AND IT WAS NOT ONE

The ticket asked for the Maternity card to be filtered out for ineligible employees. Measured on production first: **the card is correct.** EMP-0004 really held a 98-day Maternity credit, written by a Leave Generation run that credited the type to all 79 employments — 6,566 days of it to 67 people the gender rule excludes.

`leaveBalances` already filters its no-activity tail through the eligibility gate — which is also the reporter's own edge case 1, already built. It could not fire, because **a credit IS activity**. Hiding the card would have hidden 6,566 wrong days that still sit in HR screens, reports and anything that pays a balance out.

**`openLeaveYear` consulted no identity condition at all.** Harmless while it granted only the three standing codes; `783bf55a` / `baea8e5b` widened it to every type, and it stopped being harmless the moment a tenant configured Maternity for female married employees.

### THE SPLIT: IDENTITY GATES THE GRANT, TIMING DOES NOT

`isProfileEligible` separates gender / marital / organisation-assignment (whose leave this is) from minimum service and probation (when they may take it). The grant uses identity only — **the year-open runs once**, so refusing a new joiner on service would withhold their Annual Leave forever. The card filter uses it too, because the reporter asked in these words that minimum service must not hide a card. The apply gate keeps both halves and is unchanged.

### THE CORRECTION THAT WAS APPLIED, AND WHAT IS LEFT

`scripts/reverse-ineligible-leave-grants.ts` — dry run by default, a negative `adjustment` beside the wrong accrual rather than a DELETE (6574c6b4: the ledger is the record), refusing any pair where days were spent or a request is attached, and idempotent.

Applied on production after the r316 fix: **19 pairs, −1,862.00 days, all Maternity, none Annual.** EMP-0004 now reads **0.00**, so the reported card goes. No balance went negative.

**60 employments still hold a positive Maternity balance. Five of them are correct** (recorded female and married). **The other 55 are there because their gender or marital status is not recorded** — the sweep deliberately will not take days off a person it cannot place. That is the reporter's data to fix, it was flagged in the plan before approval, and it is raised again with the result.

## r314 (2026-09-21) — Roster and Import in two places, because the reporter chose it. `main@3ea20585`, **no migration**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `fe2360f9`, `7c80a168`. Gate: **929 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, every chunk exit 0 and counted in full. `next build` exit 0. Deployed: `exit_code=0`, `built_ref` 3ea20585, active, `GET /` 401, rsync dry-run clean.

### THE DECISION WAS THE DELIVERABLE, AND IT WAS THE REPORTER'S TO MAKE

`fe2360f9` asked for Roster and Import under Admin › Attendance **and** for their permissions to be unchanged. Those cannot both hold: the admin group gates at GROUP level before individual rows are considered, so a `managerUp` row inside it is invisible to every non-admin manager. That is not a limitation to code around — it is why `a324a4b3 rev3` moved both rows OUT of that node in the first place.

`7c80a168` put the trade to the reporter in writing rather than choosing for them, with a recommendation: put them under Admin as asked AND leave the manager rows alone, accepting that an administrator sees each row twice. **They approved it.** So the node now carries `adminOnly` copies and `ATTENDANCE_MANAGE_LINKS` is untouched.

Taking a function away from their managers was never ours to choose. The cost of asking was one round of waiting; the cost of guessing would have been two screens silently disappearing from every manager's rail.

### THE GUARDS WERE INVERTED, NOT LOOSENED

Four assertions pinned the decision this round reverses, and each now pins the NEW decision plus the thing the old one was really protecting:

- **`attendance-menu-relocation`** asserted `/roster` and `/attendance/import` "must NOT be in the admin node". It now requires them to be there AND `adminOnly`, AND requires each to still exist as a `managerUp` Manage row — so losing the manager half fails, which is the promise that was made.
- **`attendance-pack`'s "no href is listed twice"** was `toEqual([])`, tightened there by f3e6c36e. It now NAMES the declared pairs (`PAIRED_HREFS`) and requires each pair to be exactly one `adminOnly` and one `managerUp` copy. An undeclared duplicate still fails, which is what the line has always been for.
- **`sidebar-attendance-group`'s** "Import is NOT in the admin-gated node" is inverted the same way, with the node copies required to carry `adminOnly` and forbidden to carry `managerUp`.
- The **camelCase labelKey guard** exempts the pairs, because they deliberately share their Manage twins' keys so one screen reads identically from both menus — and a new assertion requires exactly that.

### ⚠️ FOUND, PRE-EXISTING, DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE

**`/attendance/import` calls `requireAdmin()`, which redirects a non-admin to `/`. Its Manage row is `managerUp`.** So that row advertises a screen every manager is bounced out of, and has done since before this round. r314 changed neither the row nor the page.

It is pinned by a new test arm so it cannot later be mistaken for something this round caused, and **raised as its own item**: whether managers may import attendance is a policy question with two opposite fixes (grant them access, or drop the row), and it is the reporter's to answer. Roster, by contrast, is `scopedSession` and genuinely works for managers — which is exactly why the two rows needed checking separately rather than as a pair.

### THE GATE WENT RED ON A BACKGROUND RUN, AND THE RULE CAUGHT IT

Chunks 11 and 12 failed with **zero AssertionErrors** — a Postgres deadlock on the harness's ~100-table TRUNCATE, plus hook timeouts, across eleven unrelated suites. Both passed with identical file counts when re-run in the FOREGROUND. That is precisely the environment-not-code signal §4 documents, and the reason the rule is "count AssertionErrors first".

### NOT DONE

- The render check could not see the new rows. The sidebar server-renders node HEADERS and flat links; node CHILDREN (Leave config's and Claims config's too) render on expand, so they are absent from the initial HTML by construction. The nav structure is pinned by the three source-reading guards instead — which is why those guards read the pack source rather than a rendered page.

## r313 (2026-09-20) — Entitlement means this year's entitlement. `main@a3014277`, **migration 0475**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `845903a3`. Gate: **929 files — equal to the suite file count — 14,190 tests, 0 AssertionErrors**, 14 chunks, every chunk exit 0 and counted in full. `gate:shadow` PASS (391/391). `next build` exit 0. RENDERED on a dev server: Employee Balances reads "Entitlement", no "Full Entitlement", no `MISSING_MESSAGE`.

### WHAT SHIPPED

"Full Entitlement" is now "Entitlement" in all six locales, and for an employee who joined part way through the leave year it shows THEIR entitlement for this year: `min((band / 365) × days-from-hire-to-31-Dec-inclusive, band)`, rounded by a NEW second rounding rule that HR maintains themselves. The Explain panel prints the working — band, hire date, eligible days, divisor, unrounded figure, which rule was in force, final figure. Earned to Date, every grant and every ledger row are untouched.

### ⚠️ THE APPROVED PLAN'S PREMISE WAS WRONG, AND THE REPORTER IS OWED THE CORRECTION

The plan led with a correction OF the reporter: that the prorated figure was already on that screen as **Earned to Date**, because a2c grants a first-year employee their part-year amount up front. Verified afterwards, and it is false for the only type they use.

- The seeded `ANNUAL` type is **ARCHIVED**. Their live Annual Leave is `AL` ("*Annual Leave"), `role = 'annual'`.
- `isA2cFirstYear` matches the **literal code `'ANNUAL'`**, so the up-front path never runs for `AL`.
- Measured: of their six 2026 joiners with an AL accrual, **4 match the to-date slice and 0 match the year-end slice**. Their Earned to Date is what they have earned so far, not the year's allowance.

So the figure was genuinely missing and this item is not a second rendering of an existing one. **An item correcting the record is owed to the reporter** — the same shape as `52aaee75` after r307. It is not raised here because the build is unaffected; the deliverable was right either way.

### THE GATE IS THE ROLE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE FEATURE ON THIS TENANT

Gating the proration on `isA2cFirstYear` would have shipped a column that prorates **nothing** for `AL`. `isEarnedAccrualType` asks `leave_type.role` first and falls back to the seeded code — precisely the fix 65f466e2 made for the earned sweep after the identical trap ("a tenant's own Annual Leave on a code the pack never seeded could never accrue a day").

**`isA2cFirstYear` itself is deliberately untouched.** It decides HOW MANY DAYS PEOPLE RECEIVE; moving it to the role moves balances and is a separate, recorded change. This function decides only what a column says, so it may use the better predicate without moving anybody's ledger. SICK and HOSPITALIZATION are never prorated — per-calendar-year entitlements under EA-1955 s.60F must reach a mid-year joiner in full.

### DISPLAY-ONLY, ENFORCED BY WHERE THE COLUMNS ARE NOT

0475 adds `entitlement_rounding_{method,threshold,bands}`, all nullable, mirroring the accrual trio so `applyRounding` / `checkRoundingBands` and the band editor are REUSED rather than forked — the reporter asked for that in writing. They are deliberately **outside `leaveTypeRuleColumns`**: that map exists so the granting engines and the projection kernel read the identical rule set, and a rule one reads and the other does not posts a permanent oscillating delta (7cd914b1, twice). A display rule must never reach a ledger write, which is the reporter's "Earned to Date must not change" stated as a constraint. Rounding is applied ONLY when proration happened — an entitlement straight from the table is the number HR configured.

### GUARDS UPDATED, NOT LOOSENED

The marker count (29 → 30, its own tri-state so a form rendering one rule and not the other preserves the other), the F9 field pins (the table's posted name is a prop now, so the pin moved to where the name is DECIDED — stricter, because it catches a changed default repointing every save), r279's label assertion, and the explain ARGS map (which caught a real `FORMATTING_ERROR` before it shipped). **r303's byte-for-byte employee-panel baseline was regenerated and then DIFFED**: all 18 differing sections, across six locales and three surfaces, were the removal of the qualifier — "Full " / " Penuh" / "முழு " / "เต็มปี" / " cả năm" / "全年" — and nothing else. That diff is recorded in the test so the next person diffs before regenerating.

### NOT DONE

- **Effective dates on the rounding tables.** The reporter made it conditional on the framework supporting it; rounding is held on the leave type with no dated history. Told them so in the plan.
- The CSV/XLSX export of Employee Balances still exports the band figure, not the prorated one. Same read, one field; worth a follow-up so the file and the screen cannot disagree.

## r312 (2026-09-19) — the seeder stopped treating a schema fixture as somebody's data. `main@8b6b0016`, **no migration**.

No board item — asked for directly, off the back of r311's finding. Gate: **928 files — equal to the suite file count — 14,167 tests, 0 AssertionErrors**, 14 chunks, every chunk exit 0 and counted in full. `next build` exit 0. Deployed: rsync dry-run clean, active, `GET /` 401, deploy `exit_code=0`, "Demo data already present — skipping seed" as expected.

### TWO DEFECTS, ONE CAUSE

Migration 0151 inserts a reserved nil-uuid tenant, `System (auth audit)`, on **every** correctly migrated database. It is a valid FK target for pre-auth auth events (login-failed on an un-invited email, a reset request for an unknown email) — `app.append_auth_event` COALESCEs their NULL tenant onto it — and by construction it holds no companies, people or employments.

**1. R4 counted it as a foreign tenant.** So `foreignTenantRefusal` fired on every database there is: `pnpm db:seed` could not run on a freshly rebuilt local cluster without `SEED_MAY_DESTROY_OTHER_TENANTS=1`. That is not a stricter guard, it is a broken one — **an always-on refusal teaches the operator to type the override by reflex, and the override is the last thing standing between a real database and the TRUNCATE.** The refusal is worth more when it means something. R4 still refuses a real tenant standing beside the system row, and the count in its message no longer bills the operator for a row that is not theirs.

**2. The seeder destroyed it and never put it back.** `tenant` is in the TRUNCATE list, and nothing re-creates the row, because 0151 is already applied and migrations do not run again. So on any seeded database `app.append_auth_event` raised a foreign-key violation on exactly the events that exist to record someone knocking on the door. The seeder now re-inserts it immediately after the TRUNCATE, idempotently, mirroring 0151's own `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` — which also repairs a database seeded by an older build without needing a migration to do it.

**Both proven against the live cluster, not reasoned about.** `pnpm db:seed` ran with no override; the reserved row survived; `app.append_auth_event(NULL, …)` wrote a row onto it. The failure it prevents was demonstrated inside a transaction that deleted the row, watched the FK violation, and rolled back.

### ⚠️ WHAT THIS CHANGES ON THE CONSULTANT BOX, AND IT IS NOT NOTHING

R4's always-on refusal was also, by accident, the thing that made `./deploy/deploy.sh --reseed` a no-op on that box. **It is no longer.** `--reseed` now does exactly what its own help text says — TRUNCATE 24 tables and re-plant Demo Group — which on that box means the feedback board's 853 items and every consultant record go with it. That is the documented semantics restored, not a new hazard invented, and the normal deploy path is untouched (`Demo data already present — skipping seed`). **RECOMMENDATION, not built: replace the accidental protection with a deliberate one** — a refusal keyed on the target database holding real usage (feedback items, payslips) rather than on a tenant row that says nothing.

### PROCESS

Pre-gate sweep of everything naming these surfaces — 59 files, 1,692 tests, green first pass. `test/r290-customer-deploy-path.test.ts` was UPDATED, not loosened: three new arms (the system row alone is tolerated; a real tenant beside it still refuses and is the only one named or counted; the seeder's restore comes AFTER the truncate). Reverting either half fails all three.

## r311 (2026-09-19) — Attendance Breakdown Detail, and a guard that was hiding a link instead of shutting a door. `main@8d7cbf34`, **no migration**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `22d67223`. Gate: **928 files — equal to the suite file count — 14,164 tests, 0 AssertionErrors**, 14 chunks, every chunk exit 0 and counted in full. `next build` exit 0. RENDERED on a dev server: 29 headers, 19 day rows, 551 cells, no `MISSING_MESSAGE`.

### THE SCREEN

`/attendance/breakdown` — one employee, one date range, every figure the engine recorded per day: shift and schedule source, declared vs deducted break, span, actual hours, lateness and its deduction, early out and its deduction, under-time, OT total and all six rate bands, status, flag, and the raw clocking trail. Twenty-nine columns, admin-only.

It is the deliberate **counterpart of 570fd56e** (r306), which took eight calculation columns OFF Individual Attendance because eighteen columns could not be scanned. Those columns were moved, not deleted, and this is where they were moved to. One screen to review a month, one to interrogate it — neither may later be removed on the argument that the other covers it.

### ⚠️ THE DECISION THAT MATTERS: IT WAS BUILT WITH THE WRONG GUARD FIRST

The screen was written `scopedSession`, to match `/attendance` next door. **That was a leak, not a style choice, and it was caught by asking what the guard actually narrows rather than by trusting the comment on the neighbouring file.**

`scopedSession` resolves a **company** scope. The employee picker is `listEmployees`, which is `withTenant` and filtered only by those company ids — **no narrowing by role at all**. A plain employee who typed the URL would have been offered every colleague in their company and served any one of their full calculation audits. The `adminOnly` flag on the nav row hides the LINK and protects nothing, which is precisely the failure `test/attendance-menu-relocation.test.ts` exists to prevent.

`/attendance` may be `scopedSession` because it is genuinely self-service and its service narrows the reading. This screen has **no self-service entry point anywhere**, so it refuses at the door: `scopedAdmin`.

It also takes **its own column in the access grid** rather than riding the `attendance` column. Listing an admin-only route on a `scopedSession` column would have been worse than a wrong guard — it would have told every reader of that grid that ordinary staff reach a screen they are refused. The precedent is `/attendance/my-records`: a different audience is a different SCREEN, not another route on an existing one.

Non-vacuity: reverting to `scopedSession` fails **two independent guards** — the item's own, and the relocation guard's per-route loop.

### A THIRD OF THE REQUESTED COLUMNS HAVE NO SOURCE, AND STAY UNBUILT

Half-day splits, break-level lateness, Shift Group ID, Day Type Today, Day Code, Early In / Late In Shift, Schedule Overtime vs Approved Overtime. ## r309 (2026-09-19) — Taken counts the days taken. `main@87cc021e`, **no migration**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `690d4400`. Gate: **927 files — equal to the suite file count — 14,138 tests, 0 AssertionErrors**, SECOND run, 14 chunks. `next build` exit 0. Deployed: rsync dry-run clean, active, `GET /` 401, `/health` 200, `stale_build=0`, `built_ref` 87cc021e.

### THE FAULT WAS A COLUMN FAITHFULLY REPORTING THE WRONG QUANTITY

`finalizeLeaveApproval` writes the ledger debit as `-(approvedDays - unpaidDays)` — only the part that came
OUT OF A BALANCE (core/leave.ts ~:4896, and ~:4892 already spelled the distinction out). For a fully unpaid
leave those are equal, so the debit row is written with **0.00 days**. The row EXISTS; it is zero. A Taken
column derived from debits then reports 0.00 for someone who was absent all week.

Not a UPL special case, which the reporter asked for explicitly: any request with non-zero `unpaid_days`
under-reported by exactly that much, including a PAID type that went part-unpaid when the balance ran out.

**The fix is an identity, not new arithmetic.** absence = need + unpaid, and the debit already IS need, so
summing `leave_request.unpaid_days` for approved requests completes it with no new stored figure. Summed from
the REQUEST (never joined onto the ledger, so a request cannot be counted twice) and grouped by the type it
was FILED under — r306's attribution. r302 split survivors each carry their own `unpaid_days`, so a partially
cancelled leave contributes only what survived.

### WHAT IT DELIBERATELY NARROWS, PINNED FROM BOTH SIDES

39136455 (r306) promised `Balance = BF + Entitlement + Share - Taken - Pending - Pending Share`. That held
only because `taken` was balance-spend. It now holds for fully-paid leave and NOT for part-unpaid, where
absence legitimately exceeds what left the balance. **The reporter was shown that trade in writing before it
was built.** r306's own assertion now carries why it still closes on its own fixture, and a new part-unpaid
arm proves exactly where it stops — the narrowing is a tested property, not a sentence in a plan.

BALANCE IS UNTOUCHED and asserted in both directions: the unpaid leave moves the ledger by 0, and the Balance
column with it. It stays `sum(leave_ledger.days)`, never re-derived from these columns (6574c6b4 — re-deriving
it once turned a true +14 into -14).

Non-vacuity: reverting the unpaid half reproduces the reported fault exactly (`expected +0 to be 5`).

### ⚠️ THE FIRST GATE WAS RED, AND IT CAUGHT r307's SLOPPINESS, NOT THIS ITEM'S

One AssertionError: the ADR-0080 D9 leave-pack drift ratchet flagged
`scripts/report-a2c-hire-year-deltas.ts` importing `core/leave` directly.

**How it reached main ungated is the part to remember.** r307's gate ran on branch tip `97c316d3`; the report
script was committed AFTER that, straight onto main. Two commits therefore shipped without ever passing a
gate, and this was the first full run to see them. Earlier in the same session r306's first gate was voided
for changing code DURING a run — this is the looser version of the same error, committed after one. **A
commit after the gate is a commit nobody tested.**

Fixed by importing through `packs/leave/service`, which `packs/leave/service.ts`'s own header names as the
right answer for an operator script ("the alternative was a fifth scripts/ entry in the audited debt"). The
allowlist only ever shrinks; nothing was added to it.

### NOT DONE / KNOWN

- No browser render, five rounds running — `pnpm db:seed` is classifier-refused. The Taken column's new value
  is proven by tests and unseen by eye.
- `fe2360f9` and `22d67223` are both approved and both edit the SAME exact-set nav guard that already caught
  r306 out. They are sequenced deliberately: fe2360f9 first, 22d67223 last. `sidebar-attendance-group` holds
  an explicit `'Roster is NOT in the admin-gated node'` assertion — the decision fe2360f9 reverses, so it gets
  updated with the reason rather than deleted.

## r307 (2026-09-18) — the a2c hire-year divergence closes, and the reporter's premise turns out to be stale. `main@5aa7ae83`, **no migration**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `d58bfa3f`. Gate: **926 files — equal to the suite file count — 14,132 tests, 0 AssertionErrors**, FIRST pass, 14 chunks at `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=3`. `next build` exit 0. Deployed: rsync dry-run zero lines, active, `GET /` 401, `/health` 200, `stale_build=0`, `built_ref` 5aa7ae83.

**Merge note:** not a fast-forward. `main` had moved ahead by one DOCS-ONLY commit while the branch gated; verified `git diff 97c316d3..HEAD -- . ':!docs'` empty before merging, and the receipt records that the gate ran on the branch tip.

### THE BLOCKER WAS NOT WHERE THREE ROUNDS SAID IT WAS

r300 wrote "I could not read production" and this session repeated it. That was true of ROW DUMPS and false of
AGGREGATES: the auto-mode classifier permits counts and existence checks. Every read r300 recorded as owed,
plus two it never listed, was answered in about five minutes once that was tested rather than assumed. The
lesson is cheap to state and was expensive to miss — **a refusal on one query shape is not a refusal on the
capability.**

### d58bfa3f — the fix, and why it is one call rather than new arithmetic

`projectExpectedEntitlement` tested `isA2cFirstYear` BEFORE its earned branch and projected the up-front
part-year; `accrueEarnedLeave` had no a2c handling and credited daily slices. bc36c768 recorded this as a
known gap and `test/leave-earning-method-simplified.test.ts` excluded it BY ASSERTION.

MEASURED, not assumed: for an a2c type with an earned method the hire grant writes **0.00** — an earned type
earns, it is not granted — so the sweep was the only writer. The reporter's two figures are exactly the two
sides: 57/365 × 16 = 2.50 credited, 162/365 × 16 = 7.10 projected.

The engine now calls the SAME `isA2cFirstYear` / `a2cFirstYearEntitledToDate` the kernel uses. NOT "teach the
period arithmetic about a2c": an a2c first year is not a partial year being earned, it is a part-year
entitlement granted up front, and slicing it would be a third definition of one rule. The sweep also now
selects `terminatedOn`, so a first-year LEAVER is capped at their last day of service.

### ⚠️ WHAT THE FIX ACTUALLY DOES IS NOT WHAT THIS ROUND PREDICTED

The dry-run report says the sweep would apply **nothing** today: of 48 employee/type pairs, 42 are skipped,
4 unchanged, 2 move by −0.36 days, and the sweep only tops UP.

Employee 100814 already reads **7.00** (7.101, rounded down by their own custom table — r303's work). All
four of their ANNUAL ledger rows are `sys:a2c_recalc` corrections, the last written **14 September**, and
there are **79** such rows tenant-wide.

So the recalc path was ALREADY dragging these employees to the kernel's figure — repeatedly. **r307's real
value is that the corrections stop**, not that a figure moves. That is the oscillating-delta harm
`earnedToDateFor`'s own header warns about, observed in production data. Recorded because this round's
plan, its commit messages and its first report all described a different effect.

### THE DRY-RUN REPORT WAS WRONG TWICE BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT

`scripts/report-a2c-hire-year-deltas.ts` (read-only; every call is `dryRun`).

1. `before` was `sum(ALL ledger days)` vs an accrual target. The ledger carries three entry types and 36 rows
   that are neither accrual nor debit. It read **−362 days**.
2. Corrected to the accrual-class sum it read **−379**, because a pair the sweep SKIPS returns
   `earnedToDateTotal = 0`, and a skipped pair is not a zero target. `pairs` is the sweep's own record of
   what it processed; filtering on it is the fix.

Either version, sent to the reporter, would have told a customer that 24 employees were about to lose 362
days of leave. The per-employee list goes to a FILE on the box; the console gets counts only.

### OWED TO THE REPORTER — RAISED, NOT ASSUMED

`52aaee75` asks them to confirm what 100814 shows today, because this round corrected their premise and a
correction nobody can see on their screen is worth nothing. It also repeats that Full Entitlement 16.00 is
correct by design.

### NOT DONE / KNOWN

- **Why 42 of 48 pairs are skipped is not explained, and one theory is already dead.** "not configured / no
  entitlement / not earned" is the sweep's own reason. TESTED AND DISMISSED 2026-09-18: it is NOT a missing
  job grade. 11 of the 24 hire-year employees have `grade_id` NULL, but all 11 carry positive ANNUAL accrual
  (207.50 days between them), and 23 of the 24 have ANNUAL ledger rows at all — so neither "no grade" nor "no
  entitlement history" explains the skips. Whatever makes `entitlement <= 0` for those pairs at `asOf` is
  still unknown, and it is worth knowing: an employee the accrual sweep silently steps over earns nothing.
  Start from the entitlement COMPOSITION (template band validity window vs hire date), not from the grade.

- **Production runs with `ALLOW_DEMO_SESSION=true`.** Every script run prints the box's own warning that the

## r306 (2026-09-18) — Four approved items: inquiry day screen, Card ID, pooled Share columns, Web Clocking. `main@ce43d575`, **migration 0474**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `570fd56e`, `44bc1c33`, `39136455`, `7ac6b4db` (partly — see below). Gate: **925 files — equal to the suite file count — 14,125 tests, 0 AssertionErrors**, 14 chunks at `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=3`, THIRD run (see below). `gate:shadow` **PASS 390/390**. `next build` exit 0. Deployed: rsync dry-run zero lines, active, `GET /` 401, `/health` 200, `stale_build=0`, `built_ref` ce43d575, journal 390 = 390 applied.

### THE GATE WAS RED TWICE, AND THAT IS THE ROUND'S MOST USEFUL RECORD

Five real failures across runs 1 and 2, none of which any per-item targeted run could
have caught — every one of them was green before each gate.

- **Run 1, chunk 6:** `employee-import-field-parity` refused `employment.cardId` as neither an import column
  nor an excluded field. **Run 1, chunk 12:** `r279-earned-and-full-entitlement` caught a REAL DEFECT — the
  Employee Balances empty-state row still spanned `colSpan={13}` after 39136455 took the table to 15, so "no
  rows" would have drawn a cell two columns short. `sidebar-attendance-group` pinned the literal
  'Clock in/out'.
- **Run 2, chunks 4 and 7:** two MORE guards hardcoding `colSpan={13}` against the same page
  (`r196-entitlement-not-generated`, `leave-inquiry-surfaces`).

**The root cause is worth writing down: one shared table had FIVE separate guards pinning its column count,
in five files, none of which greps the directories the change touched.** Adding a column to Employee
Balances is therefore a five-file edit that looks like a one-file edit. The r279 guard is the one that
earned its keep — it DERIVES the header count and compares the colSpan to it, rather than quoting a number,
which is why it caught the defect instead of just the stale literal. The new `570fd56e` guard counts
headings for the same reason.

What changed in method after the second red: sweeping **every test naming the touched surfaces** (70 files,
1,360 tests) before re-gating, rather than discovering the class one 20-minute gate at a time. Run 3 was
first-pass clean.

### 570fd56e — Individual Attendance: eighteen columns become ten, and a per-day screen

Six of the eighteen held an overtime figure that is 0.00 on an ordinary day. Lateness, Early Out and the six
OT buckets moved to `app/attendance/individual/[date]` — **moved, not deleted**, and the guard asserts both
halves of that. The day screen is not a second source: same `attendanceForEmploymentRange` read for one
date, same `AttendanceFigureCells` island, same `explainAttendanceDay` working.

- **Edit is a LINK** into the existing correction workflow. A second write path to an attendance record
  would bypass its approval and attachment — that is how overtime changes with no trail.
- **Break time is DERIVED** (shift span less net scheduled minutes) and captioned as derived, because there
  is no break column on `AttendanceRangeRow`.
- Dates go through new `fmtDayDate` / `fmtDayName` with the viewer's locale, in UTC. The weekday was
  hardcoded `'en-GB'` inline.
- Both full-width rows tracked from `colSpan={17}` to 10 — pinned by COUNTING the headings, not by quoting
  a number, because a stale colSpan fails nothing and just draws wrong.

### 44bc1c33 — Card / Clocking ID (migration 0474)

`importAttendancePunches` matched only `employment.employee_code` and the IC on `employee_statutory_my`,
reporting anything else as unmatched rather than guessing. A terminal recording its own card numbers matched
NOTHING, with nowhere to fix it.

- **ONE COLUMN, ONE OWNER.** The Card Assignment screen and the Card ID field on the employee's Attendance
  tab edit the same `employment.card_id`, so "two interfaces, not separate data fields" holds by
  construction. No `card_assignment` table.
- **The collision that matters is not the one the unique index catches.** The importer builds code, IC and
  card into ONE flat map, so a card equal to another employee's code or IC would post their attendance onto
  the wrong person. No constraint can express that; `core/attendance-card.ts` refuses it, mirroring the
  importer's own lookup (same join, same active-only population), and names the holder. Cards enter the map
  LAST so an exact card match wins regardless.
- **DECISION — the "same as Employee ID" setting was NOT built**, and the reason is testable rather than a
  matter of taste: the importer already matches on employee code, so a device recording employee numbers has
  always imported with no card at all. A copy would duplicate one fact and need a sync rule on every code
  rename. A NULL card is the normal state; the screen says "Matched by: Employee ID".
- Leading zeros survive — `'007'` and `'7'` are different cards, pinned behaviourally, and the input is
  never `type="number"`.
- Exact-set nav guards UPDATED, not loosened, in **two** files (`attendance-pack`, `attendance-menu-relocation`).

### 39136455 — pooled balances: Share / Pending Share, partly reversing r209

r209 gave every member of a pool the SOURCE's figures, because before it a borrower showed its own
permanently empty ledger beside a balance it could in fact spend. That fixed the readable half and made the
other impossible: with Annual's figures mirrored on, there was no way to see how much Emergency Leave anyone
had taken. **Both halves ship together; r209's guards were re-pointed, not deleted.**

- Taken is attributed to the code the leave was FILED under, derived by joining `leave_ledger.source_request_id`
  to the request's own `leave_type_id`, COALESCEing back to the ledger's type for rows with no request behind
  them (grants, carries, adjustments — which belong to the pool and are nobody's share). **No schema change,
  no new stored figure.** `pending` already grouped by the filed type; only the pooling pass overwrote it.
- **⚠️ `available` STAYS POOLED even though `balance` is 0.** They answer different questions and the submit
  guard reads `available`; zeroing it alongside `balance` would have made Emergency Leave unapplyable for
  everybody. It has its own named test.
- **Negative zero** was a real defect the new guard caught, not review: `-0` fails `Object.is` and formats as
  "−0.00", a minus sign on a row that lent nothing out.
- Columns land on HR's grid, the employee's own grid (the shared `deriveBalanceRow` feeds both) and the
  CSV/XLSX export, whose own header forbids a screen column absent from the file.
- **THE INVARIANT, pinned:** across a pool the shares cancel, so members' balances sum to the pool's own
  ledger total. Nothing about the ledger changed.

### 7ac6b4db — Web Clocking: the rename and the shift, NOT the photo

The rename (row and heading pinned to agree, six locales, route untouched), the date as "18 Sep 2026,
Friday" formatted server-side, and a Current shift card reading the same resolved shift the "ends at" line
already used, with an explicit no-shift state.

**The webcam photo was deliberately not built, and it is owed to the reporter in plain words.** A face photo
is biometric-adjacent personal data — `core/pdpa.ts` already says exactly that about the profile photograph
— and there would be hundreds per employee per year rather than one. It needs a storage design that is NOT
`person_photo`'s in-row `bytea` (150–400 KB × 2 per working day ≈ 10–20 GB a year for 100 employees, inside
every backup), its own RLS policy, a place in the PDPA erasure path, a consent record, and a retention sweep
**on the box's crontab** — a script in `scripts/` that nobody schedules is not a retention policy. Half-landing
it beside a menu rename would be the worst version. A guard pins that no capture path was left behind and
that the erasure precedent it must join is still in place.

### NOT DONE / KNOWN

## r305 (2026-09-18) — Employee Leave Inquiry: the tab rail becomes a bar, and Full screen on the wide tables. `main@62be49d7`, **no migration**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `d990f14a`. Gate: **921 files — equal to the suite file count — 14,081 tests, 0 AssertionErrors**, first pass, 14 chunks at `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=3`. `next build` exit 0. Deployed: rsync dry-run zero lines, active, `GET /` 401, `built_ref` 62be49d7.

**Round number:** this is r305, not r304. r304 was taken by the Approval Workflow edit drawer (`85875e4b`, `main@70f4b774`), already merged and recorded — caught from the stale `.gate-receipt.json` note, not from the branch name, which was wrong until it was renamed.

### d990f14a — the rail cost the table 192px to hold three words

`sm:w-44` is 11rem = 176px, plus `gap-4` = 192px. 026e16b9 had already narrowed it from `w-56` and its
own guard header records what that bought: table area 1038px for 1047px of columns at a 1512px window —
9px still overflowing. A bar across the top costs the table nothing, so this finishes that job rather than
reducing it again.

- **It stays a `nav` with `aria-current`, NOT a `role="tablist"`.** The three pills are separate ROUTES;
  tablist semantics would tell a screen reader they are panels of one page and that activating one swaps a
  view. The look changed, the meaning did not.
- **Filters follow a tab change from a per-DESTINATION allowlist** (`CARRY` in leave-inquiry-nav), never a
  query-string passthrough. `type` is leave-type ids on both balances and records; `q` is a leave-code
  search on both, so it carries (records' box also matches a request reference — carrying one of those to
  balances filters to nothing, visible in the box that carried it, which is the stated trade). **`asOf` is
  balances-only and is never carried**; Employee Details keeps its own `edQ` namespace and carries `emp`
  alone.
- **`TableFullscreen` is promoted in place, not portalled.** Moving children into a portal is a container
  change at the same tree position, which React reconciles as a different element — the table would unmount
  and remount, resetting the horizontal scroll that is the whole point of the feature. The cost is a
  dependency on `Card` having no transform/filter/contain (a fixed child escapes `overflow:hidden` but not a
  transformed ancestor), and that is now pinned by assertion rather than left to be discovered.
- **Position:** the bar sits under the search bar and its FilterChips on Balances and Records, above the
  table it scopes. On Employee Details the filters live inside the card header, so the bar sits above the
  card — stated at the call site rather than silently inconsistent.

### DECISIONS the ticket did not settle

- The reporter asked only for Employee Balances; the Full screen control went on **all three tabs**, because
  a control that appears on two of three reads as a bug when the three are one screen.
- Threading `q` and `type` goes slightly beyond "layout only". It was done because a tab bar directly under
  the search bar makes losing the filters look like a defect rather than a reset; the plan says so and
  offers rejection of that part alone.
- Retention of the reporter's own earlier decisions: 20c699f8 asked for a left rail and 026e16b9 asked to
  narrow it. This reverses both, with their agreement, and the guards were re-pointed rather than deleted.

### GUARDS RE-POINTED, NOT LOOSENED

`test/leave-inquiry-layout.test.ts` — the two assertions pinning `sm:w-44` and `sm:flex-col` now pin the
ABSENCE of a rail, plus the horizontal strip, the nav-not-tablist property, bar-before-table ordering on all
three tabs, and filters-above-bar on the two that have a search bar. Everything else in that file (the
shared `max-w-[100rem]` cap, the calendar's own `max-w-6xl`, no `max-w-none`, no `table-fixed`, px-2 cells,
wrapping headings with non-wrapping values, `w-[26%] min-w-[13rem]`, Explanation last) still holds.
`test/leave-inquiry-entry-relocation.test.ts`, `test/leave-inquiry-surfaces.test.ts` and
`test/r269-employee-leave-inquiry-row.test.ts` quoted `withEmp('/leave/tracker')` literally to assert WHICH

### 05db6aa7 — Custom Rounding: From / To / Round To, inclusive

- **Engine decision (the builder's first version moved figures):** compare in THOUSANDTHS — a band matches when
  from×1000 ≤ fk ≤ to×1000 + 9 (to 0.99 also takes 1.000); no match keeps the raw value. The plan's premise "every input is
  2dp" is FALSE for full grants of a template's days (no decimal limit), and rounding to 2dp first moved 14.397 from 14.00
  to 14.50. A third decimal is now placed by the first two, so every stored table gives exactly its old results. The
  approved plan's line "worked out to two decimal places before the table is applied" is therefore not literally how it
  works; the promise it serves (nothing falls between 0.24 and 0.25) holds.
- **0473** converts every table valid under the old rules with from' = ceil2(from), to' = ceil2(to) − 0.01 (integer
  arithmetic; a JS-compatible tie path for half-thousandths), drops rows covering no 2dp decimal, leaves old-malformed
  tables untouched and names them, WARNS for a From = To table (old rules refused it, new accept it: starts rounding) and
  for a table with 3dp figures (3dp leave figures can round differently). Verifier: equivalence exact through the real SQL
  on 234 tables; classification and counts exact; guarded against a hand-written 1e131071 aborting the deploy.
- Out-of-plan fix kept: `app/admin/actions.ts` passed a string to `fail()`, so every refusal on the leave-type rules form

## r302 (2026-09-17) — Cancel Approved Leave, and the balance defects the verifier found under it. `main@bbc024e9`, **migration 0471**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `83511d3b`. Gate: **903 files — equal to the suite file count — 13,717 tests, 0 AssertionErrors, 0 deadlocks**, first pass, 14 chunks. `gate:shadow` **PASS 387/387**. `next build` exit 0. Deployed: rsync dry-run zero lines, active, `GET /` 401, `/health` 200, `stale_build=0`, `built_ref` bbc024e9. The deploy log's 0471 NOTICE: **all 19 existing production leave types keep employee cancellation ON** (no notice, re-approval, no notification).

### WHAT SHIPPED

A Cancel Approved Leave card per leave type (allow / notice days per leave date / approved automatically /
notify), a cancellation that walks a COPY of the original request's approval chain (leave_cancellation_step,
split survivors traced through splitFromRequestId), automatic approval through the same approve body as a
system actor, employee notifications for approved/rejected, and a specific sentence for every refusal.

### THE VERIFIER FOUND FOUR BALANCE DEFECTS THE BUILDER'S TESTS DID NOT — ALL HAND-FIXED, EACH RE-DERIVED RED

1. **Race (new exposure with auto-approve):** two requests at the same moment (two tabs or a crafted POST) each
   read the leave unlocked: the same day came back twice (+2 for one day) and approved rows overlapped (7 days on a
   5-day leave). The leave row is now locked `FOR UPDATE` for the whole request; the order is leave row → cancellation
   row in `requestLeaveCancellation`, `decideLeaveCancellation` and `adminCancelLeave`, so the three cannot deadlock.
2. **Per-date-approved leave with a rejected day:** the split ignored `leave_request_date`, reversed `req.days`
   (5) against a 4-day debit, and turned the rejected Tuesday into an approved survivor with no per-date rows —
   which /leave then offered, ending ONE DAY ABOVE the starting balance. The split now runs over the APPROVED dates,
   reverses the NET ledger sourced to the row (what `adminCancelLeave` already did), and **moves each
   `leave_request_date` row onto the split row whose span holds the date**, cancelled ones set to `cancelled`.
   Also fixes a main-era defect this exposed: after any split of a per-date leave, the ORIGINAL row kept every
   date row, so `approvedLeaveDates` and unpaid-leave payroll counted the moved-out dates on it as well.
3. **Closed payroll month at decision:** only the request checked it; a chain could outlast the month's close
   and the last approval gave days back inside a final payslip. Asked again in the approve body.
4. **Second pending cancellation:** a non-overlapping second request was accepted; whichever was approved first
   split the row and the other was "approved" with 0 days back and a notification saying the leave was cancelled.
   **Decision: one pending cancellation per leave row** (the screen already hid Cancel while one waits; refusal
   copy now says "a cancellation of this leave", six locales), and a cancellation whose dates are no longer on the
   row is refused at approval (`no_longer_cancellable`) — the approver can still reject it.
5. **`leave_cancellation_step` RLS is the PARENT cancellation's** (0471 edited before it was ever applied): it
   had copied `leave_approval_step`'s delegation branch, so a delegate could read the levels of a cancellation the
   parent table hides from them. Delegates cannot see or decide cancellations at all (0132, unchanged).

### DECISIONS the ticket did not settle

- Existing types read switched ON (column added DEFAULT true, default then moved to false — no UPDATE); every
  creator of a leave type writes OFF, including newly provisioned tenants' Annual and Medical.
- A leave approved through a multi-level chain now needs every level to cancel (the plan: "the same approval
  chain"); cancellations already pending at release have no steps and stay single-level.
- A manager level of the copied chain goes to whoever is the subject's manager NOW; a named approver stays that
  person; HR can clear any level (so one HR admin can clear manager → HR alone, as with leave approvals).
- Notice is counted in calendar days per leave date; 0 keeps "strictly after today".

### NOT DONE / KNOWN

- Split survivors created before r299 carry no `splitFromRequestId`: cancelling one copies no chain and the
  manager decides alone (today's behaviour, not stuck).
- Automatic approval is allowed in a PROCESSED but not closed payroll month (only `closed` refuses, as everywhere).
- HR cancelling on the employee's behalf rejects the pending cancellation but leaves its copied steps `pending`
  (untidy rows, no screen reads them).
- The employee's own session can UPDATE its cancellation's step rows at the database level, exactly as it can
  `leave_approval_step`; no action does. A tighter write policy for both is a separate change.
- A manager can still approve a cancellation after the leave date has passed (the started-date rule is checked
  when the employee asks, as on main).

## r300 (2026-09-17) — Leave Credit, after three verifications each found money defects the builder's tests did not. `main@769e6d9a`, **migrations 0469 + 0470**.

Closed and DEPLOYED: `3fb1a611`. Gate: **895 files — equal to the suite file count — 13,596 tests, 0 AssertionErrors**,
first pass, 14 chunks. `gate:shadow` **PASS 386/386** (384 → 386). `next build` exit 0. Deployed: rsync dry-run zero lines,
active, `GET /` 401, `/health` 200, `stale_build=0`, `built_ref` 769e6d9a. The deploy log's own 0469 NOTICE settles a fact
we could not read: **production had 0 toil_accrual rows**. The `toil` module is still NOT granted — Leave Credit is dormant
on production until the owner turns the add-on on.

### THE SHAPE OF THE ROUND: VERIFY, FIX, VERIFY AGAIN — THREE TIMES

1. **Builder** (9 commits): register migration 0469, HR add/reverse, day-type gate on the request path, cancellation
   give-back, Leave Credit screen with Rules tab moved off Company Rules, /admin/toil redirect, six locales.
2. **Verifier 1** found: expired credits over-valued (statutory branch pricing whole declared minutes, ignoring the used
   part — 3 days on one rest day 384.76 vs 230.76); HR add/reverse promising overtime outcomes payroll cannot keep; HR could
   credit themselves (366 days); Leave Adjustments/import refused RL on a module-OFF tenant (HR's only lever); pending
   Emergency Leave edits newly refused; a stored August policy would go live the instant the module was granted.
   Money + security hand-fixed; non-money deploy-day items by one fix-pass agent; D5 decided by me (below).
3. **Verifier 2**, on the INTEGRATED tree, found my payroll fix was still wrong three ways — a re-run prefill never zeroes a
   stale overtime figure (a draft whose only overtime was the credited day kept paying it), a reversal after a prefill named
   no draft, and a transferred employee's OLD company was not checked — plus my own early return broke a guard, the D5
   first-install check keyed on module SCOPE, and the Leave Credit health replacement swallowed r299's blocking finding.
   All hand-fixed (`9dd5e77e`, `5bd2ce22`), each re-derived red.

### DECISIONS the ticket did not settle

- **HR add/reverse on a date with recorded overtime is REFUSED while ANY payroll run exists for the date's month or the
  next — draft included, any company.** I first allowed drafts with a "re-run the prefill" banner; the verifier proved that
  advice false. Payroll only excludes a credited day at prefill and `overtime_amount` is a per-batch aggregate, so this is
  the ADR-0033 run-state question in its sharpest form; refusing is the only rule that keeps the screen's promise true.
  HR's remedy: act before payroll starts, or delete the draft. **Deliberately conservative**: a sister company's run
  refuses too (overtime follows the company that employed the person that day).
- **Migration 0470 `app.payroll_run_exists_for_periods(text[])`, SECURITY DEFINER, yes/no only.** payroll_batch RLS shows a
  run only to an admin for its company, so asking under RLS let a company-scoped admin miss a sister company's run
  (mutation: SECURITY INVOKER → the cross-company test goes red). GRANT EXECUTE to ai_hr_app.
- **Request-path and HR credits carry NO valuation day type** (`worked_day_kind` keeps the kind for screens): expiry pays
  ORP × remaining days, 296fc027's honest basis. The roster/auto paths still price whole minutes — pre-existing, recorded.
- **The register is invisible to an employee who never held a credit**: consumption and give-back read, write and log
  nothing, and the per-date assertion is skipped. Reading the type's ROLE (needed: production's RL is `role='replacement'`,
  code `RL`) had made every RL approval on a module-off tenant log `toil.consumption.shortfall` and reach an assertion main
  never ran. Now byte-for-byte main there (verifier's deploy-day scratch: approve/cancel/edit RL with zero credits all pass).
- **D5 — a toil_policy saved BEFORE the module was ever installed is kept but its three live switches are turned off on a
  FIRST install** (judged across every scope). `core/module-activation.ts` documents D4 "reactivation must never re-seed" —
  that is about edits made while owning the module; this is configuration that pre-dates the purchase, and the plan
  promised "nothing uses it until you do". Reactivation and later companies untouched.
- Leave Adjustments / import refuse the Replacement Leave type ONLY while the register is live (toil on); the Leave Credit
  health finding replaces only TABLE findings.
- HR cannot add/preview/reverse on their own record; the worked date must be within service; consumption is guarded against
  a concurrent reversal; expiry dates use `todayInKualaLumpur`.

### ⚠️ CORRECTION (2026-09-18, r306 session) — THE OWED READS ARE NOW MEASURED, AND ONE RECORDED FACT WAS WRONG

The four reads below were answered on 2026-09-18 as AGGREGATES (the auto-mode classifier permits counts and
existence checks against production; it refuses row dumps of customer data — a distinction this round did
not know when it wrote "I could not read production").

- `tenant_module` rows for `toil` = **0** ⇒ **FIRST INSTALL**, so D5's switch-off applies automatically.
  `toil_policy` holds **2 rows, both `enabled`** — which makes D5 load-bearing rather than theoretical.
- `toil_accrual` rows = **0**, confirming this entry's own deploy-log NOTICE.
- **`toil` is billable = yes, and `subscription_line` for it = 0.** So the grant WILL be refused by
  `applyModuleChange` until a commercial line exists. That is now the ONLY thing blocking the switch-on;
  `depends_on` is satisfied (`leave` is core, `attendance` is active) and no change request is queued.
- **THE RECORDED CLAIM ABOUT THE RL TYPE IS WRONG.** This entry says "production's RL is `role='replacement'`,
  code `RL`". Measured: leave types with code `RL` = **0**, with code `REPLACEMENT` = **1**, with
  `role='replacement'` = **0**. The tenant's replacement type therefore resolves through the CODE FALLBACK

corrects any type with an accrual row this cycle, so a SICK type the old sweep had been topping up would still be

(`9242afb4`) with the same boundary, so sweep, year-open and reprojection now agree: a **stranded** earned method

### `3fb1a611` LEAVE CREDIT — BUILT, VERIFIED, NOT SHIPPED, AND WHY THAT WAS RIGHT

The adversarial verifier found it would not break production on deploy day in the ways I feared most (a
Replacement Leave approval with zero credits logs a shortfall and succeeds), but found **two money defects, a
false promise and two deploy-day regressions**:
- **Expired credits over-valued**: stamping a day type on request/HR credits routed them to the statutory branch,
  which prices the WHOLE declared/overtime minutes and ignores the used part (3 days on one rest day: 384.76 vs
  230.76). The builder's re-pointed test used one whole unused day, where both bases agree.
- **Overtime promises the payroll cannot keep**: payroll only excludes a credited day at PREFILL (`overtime_amount`
  is a per-batch aggregate), so a credit added after a processed run paid the day twice and a reversal after one
  left it unpaid — while the banners said the opposite.
- **HR could credit themselves** (366 days on one date, consent box ticked by HR).
- **Deploy-day**: Leave Adjustments and import refused the RL type on a tenant WITHOUT the module, where RL is still
  entitlement-based and HR has no other lever; editing a pending Emergency leave with a balance source was newly
  refused.
- **Promise**: the Rules tab could not show the August eligibility before the module was on, and granting the
  module would make a stored `enabled` policy live instantly.

Money and security **hand-fixed** on the branch (`24c49a42`, `453f2e9c`, `0ec8b6e9`), each re-derived red: no
valuation day type on request/HR credits; HR add/reverse refused against a processed/closed run holding that date's
overtime, drafts allowed with the period named for re-prefill; self-credit refused; service dates checked;
consumption guarded against a concurrent reversal; Malaysian dates for expiry; give-back skips its unindexed event
scans when the employee holds no credit. Non-money deploy-day items are with a fix-pass agent. **Leave Credit ships
only after a final verification and its own gate.**

  Leave" (the lock is the mechanism). Stale switch state if two admins edit one type (ordinary lost update).
- `graphify update` after this entry.
