## r296 (2026-09-17) — an alarm for the outage that had none, one PERKESO writer, and the runbook that is the control. `main@5727b28b`, **no migration**.

Readiness **2.1** (alarm the entitlement engine going dark), **3.1** (two PERKESO builders disagreed),
**2.3** (monthly payroll runbook). Gate: **884 files — equal to the suite file count — 13,428 tests,
0 AssertionErrors, 0 deadlocks**, first pass, no red chunk. `next build` exit 0.

### THE BEST ARGUMENT OF THE SESSION: A STANDING ALARM CANNOT RIDE A LIVENESS SIGNAL

2.1 asks for an alarm. The obvious build is to fold it into `review-sweep` — no seventh cron line, nothing
new to forget, and this repo's own standing advice says prefer an existing sweep.

**It is wrong here, mechanically.** `cron-alert.sh` touches `heartbeat/<job>` **only on exit 0**, and
staleness of that file is the sole signal for the "job stopped running" class — the class r295 added it for.
This alarm's condition is **standing**: once a tenant's tables go out of force it is still true tomorrow
night, until a human fixes it. Fold it in and the first zeroed tenant pins `review-sweep`'s exit non-zero
**forever**, its heartbeat is never touched again, and the hourly staleness check starts paging
*"review-sweep has not succeeded"* — an alert about the wrong thing, on the channel that exists to catch a
dead job. **One misconfigured tenant would silently disable liveness detection for a real sweep.**

Hence a seventh line, with the risk mitigated rather than accepted: registered in `JOB_KEYS`/`JOBS` so
`/admin/scheduled-actions` shows **"Never run"** until the crontab line exists, and `test/job-run.test.ts`
pins that registry ABSOLUTELY so the job could not be added without its wiring in the same commit.

Same reasoning sets the staleness window at **48 hours, not 25**: this job's heartbeat means "checked AND
clean", so one night's standing alarm must not also page about staleness.

### THE PREDICATE, AND THE TERM THAT MAKES IT USABLE

`engineIsDark = templatesInForce === 0 && templatesStarted > 0 && activeEmployments > 0`

`templatesStarted` (`valid_from <= today`, retired or not) is the whole distinction between
**never-configured** and **went-to-zero** — a brand-new tenant has no rows, a tenant mid-setup has only
future-dated ones, a tenant that was configured and is now zero alarms. **Deliberately retired falls out of
the predicate rather than being special-cased**: retiring one rule while anything else is in force leaves
`templatesInForce > 0`, so the reporter's own 17:30 retirement of `e1aa6e06` is silent.

**Two alarms were DECLINED and the reasons are better than the alarms would have been.** No alarm on
rules-in-force reaching zero: one table with no rule resolves for EVERYBODY (r193 fault 3), so it would fire
on a correct configuration. No per-type "went dark": a type with no table in force was never meant to grant
days, and on the reporting tenant that would have raised eight findings on night one.

**Checked against production, which the agent was blocked from reading:** 9 templates in force, 11 ever
started, 75 active employments. `engineIsDark` needs `inForce === 0`, so **production would not alarm
tonight**. (The readiness doc recorded 1 in force on 2026-09-13; the reporter has been configuring since.)

### TWO PERKESO WRITERS PRODUCED DIFFERENT BYTES, AND ONE REPORTED THE WRONG WAGE

Not a documentation bug. `my.socso-eis` and `my.borang-8a` are two different PAPER documents, but PERKESO
ASSIST takes **ONE** combined upload file and both screens claimed to make it. Decisive evidence: the two
modules cite **the same specification at two revisions** — v1.0 of 22 Jul 2022 and v2.0 of 13 Feb 2026 —
with fields 1-10 at identical offsets.

The measured diff, same input, before consolidation: six field ranges per record, **plus a trailing CRLF on
one side only**, **plus the salary box drawn from two different facts** — Reports wrote
`payslip.gross_pay`, Borang 8A wrote `statutory.bases.socsoEis`. **Gross pay includes money PERKESO does
not charge on**, so one of those files was reporting the wrong wage to a statutory authority. Consolidated
onto the basis, which is the repo's already-documented decision. After: the diff is empty.

**The golden test and its fixture were not touched** (`git diff main...HEAD` on both: empty). That fixture
is the customer's own filed `BRG8A.txt`, 14 records, 3,918 bytes — the only bytes PERKESO is known to have
accepted. It passing unmodified is the primary safety property of this change.

**WHAT IS STILL UNSETTLED, AND IT IS DATED.** v1.0 is a layout PERKESO accepted in January.
**v2.0 has NEVER been uploaded from this system**, and `PERKESO_SKBBK_MANDATORY_FROM = {2026, 10}` starts
writing it in two weeks. Watch the first upload. Also unknown, recorded in code rather than guessed:
whether the cutover is measured against the CONTRIBUTION MONTH or the UPLOAD DATE — they differ only for a
late or amended return.

### A SECURITY FINDING THAT TURNED OUT NOT TO BE ONE — CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED

The agent flagged `app/payroll/reports/socso-eis-file/route.ts` gating on bare `isAdmin(s)` where its
sibling uses `scopedAdmin()`, with `borang-8a/shared.ts` warning that this "would let a guessed companyId
export another company's employee names, ICs and contributions" — and honestly said it had NOT verified
whether RLS blocks it.

**Verified: RLS blocks it.** `socsoEisFileForBatch` runs inside `withTenant` on the app pool
(`ai_hr_app`, NOBYPASSRLS); `can_see_employment` needs `is_admin_for(company)`, which a company-scoped
grant does not satisfy for another company — the export returns **zero rows, not another company's data**.
And today it is moot regardless: all 5 production `hr_admin` grants are **group-wide**, so `isAdmin` and
`scopedAdmin` have identical reach.

**It remains worth fixing** — the route relies on RLS alone where its sibling uses belt-and-braces, the same
shape as r290's knowledge base. Separate item, not an emergency. **I would have been wrong to escalate it
as a leak, and wrong to dismiss it without checking.**

### THE RUNBOOK IS THE CONTROL, AND SAYS SO

`docs/MONTHLY-PAYROLL-RUNBOOK.md`, written from the code: every step names its action and every "only
caller is a button" claim was checked by finding the callers. Three steps feed money into a run and **all
three are silent when skipped** — no warning, no zero-line. A run that forgot the overtime prefill completes
and looks normal; the overtime is simply absent from the payslip. The attendance recompute page has **no
navigation row at all** and nothing in the codebase recomputes after a shift, roster or rule change.

Until steps 3 and 4 are automated (`packs/attendance/index.ts` already names `PayrollInputContributor` as
the intended home), the runbook IS the control — stated in the document rather than left implied.

### CITATIONS OF MINE THAT WERE WRONG, AGAIN

"Four `app/` files reference the builders" — one contains an `href`, not an import, and the file that DOES
import it I failed to list. "Two different screens" — it is **three screens reaching two routes**. "Both emit
278 characters" — true per record, but the FILES were never the same length because of that trailing CRLF.

## r294 (2026-09-17) — two more services bound, four left with reasons, and an audit that says why. `main@909b7470`, **no migration**.

Closes the gap r292 declared. Gate: **882 files — equal to the suite file count — 13,399 tests,
0 AssertionErrors, 0 deadlocks**, first pass, no red chunk. `next build` exit 0.

### THE AUDIT IS THE DELIVERABLE, AND GREP CANNOT DO IT

An AST sweep of every `import` / `export … from` / `import()` / `require()` corrected **five of six rows**
in the importer table I handed the agent. Two failure modes, opposite directions, both worth carrying:

**Grep OVER-reports.** `core/loans-compute.ts:8` contains `from '@/core/loans'` **inside a doc comment**.
My table listed it and `core/loans.ts` as core-side importers of `loans`; neither imports it that way.
`test/helpers/import-ratchet.ts` documents this exact trap — "COMMENTS ARE NOT STRIPPED".

**Grep UNDER-reports, and this decided the round.** `core/admin.ts:119` is
`import { DEFAULT_PAYROLL_CYCLES, seedPayrollCycleCatalog } from '../packs/payroll/service'` — the pack
**FACADE**. A specifier grep for `payroll-cycle` cannot see it. My grep found "none"; **r292 was right and
I was wrong**, which is why r292's caution was correct and my table would have led to binding a file three
core surfaces depend on.

### BOUND: 2. LEFT: 4. THAT IS THE HONEST OUTCOME.

**`core/tax-relief.ts`** (~20 entry points) — every consumer outside the payroll route trees takes only
PURE exports (a const and a function over rows); none opens a transaction, so rebinding does not touch them.
This closes a real hole: **`app/me/actions.ts` posts `saveTp1Draft`/`submitTp1` from a CORE segment with no
payroll layout above it**, so that write path had no gate at all.

**`core/back-pay.ts`** (7 entry points) — zero consumers outside `app/payroll/back-pay/**`.
`approveAndPostBackPay` writes money into a draft batch.

**LEFT, each with its blocking consumer named in `core/module-gate.ts`'s header:**
- `pay-components` — Personnel page calls `listEmploymentPayComponents`/`listPayComponents`
  unconditionally, AND `core/attendance-allowance.ts` writes through `setPayrollBatchComponent`, so binding
  would refuse **a customer who bought Attendance and declined Payroll**.
- `cp38` — same Personnel page, `listCp38` unconditional.
- `loans` — `app/me/page.tsx:185` calls `listLoansForEmployment`; ESS, core.
- `payroll-cycle` — `app/admin/organization/[companyId]/page.tsx:82` calls `listPayrollCycles`.
  (`core/admin.ts:405` would NOT have broken: it passes its own `tx`, the documented tx-helper exemption.)

**All four are one shape: A CORE SCREEN DOES AN UNCONDITIONAL PAYROLL READ.**

### THE REAL FIX IS NOT MORE GATING

Two ways out, and the second is better:
1. Per-function `assertModuleGate` on the write entry points only — closes the action hole, leaves the
   reads. Mechanical, but it is **discipline**, the thing `core/module-gate.ts` exists to replace.
2. **Make the core screens ask before they read.** Personnel, `/me` and Organization should not be
   rendering payroll sections to a tenant that declined Payroll — that is arguably a defect in its own
   right, independent of gating. Fix it and all four files become bindable at the SERVICE, which is the
   mechanism. Needs a UI decision (does the CP38 card vanish, or say "not on your plan?") so it is a
   reporter-facing question, not an engineering one.

### THE 500 IS A REFUSAL, BUT IT IS THE WRONG SHAPE

Two route handlers now return **500 `ModuleNotEnabledError`** where they returned 404:
`/payroll/back-pay/export` and `/payroll/transactions/tp1/…/pdf`. Those are exactly where **no layout
runs**, same as a server action, so this is the hole actually closing and no data leaks. But an
authorisation decision should be a **403**, not a crash-shaped 500 — and r291 added a health endpoint with
(deferred) error alerting that would otherwise cry wolf on every un-entitled probe. **Follow-up, not a
blocker.**

### GUARDS THAT DISCRIMINATE, NOT GUARDS THAT MERELY PASS

Against r293's vacuity shape: with Payroll ON, `calculateBackPay` gets **past** the gate and fails inside
the engine with `BackPayNothingToCalculateError` — an error a gate refusing everyone could not produce. The
TP1 arm asserts the write landed (`toHaveLength(1)`), not merely that it resolved.

The core-surface arm was proven by **binding each of the four left-unbound files in turn** and watching
Personnel, `/me` and Organization fail with `ModuleNotEnabledError` — so "leaving them unbound" is a pinned
decision, not an omission.

### TEST FALLOUT: r292'S FIRST KIND, EXACTLY

21 failures in `tp1-self-relief` and `tp1-admin-on-behalf`, both a hand-rolled `employeeCtx` with no
snapshot. Fixed with a real snapshot, **not `entitlementsExempt`** — payroll is billable, and an exempt
context asked about a billable module throws `EntitlementsExemptForBillableError` by design. The `bound`
ratchet went 5 → 7; nothing was loosened.

## r293 (2026-09-16) — the approval builder over a structure that was already there, and a picker that stops lying by omission. `main@6d47077f`, **migrations 0467 + 0468**.

Board items `3c8037be` (approval workflow, four phases) and `04d163da` (mark non-accruing types).
`3fb1a611` still not built.
Gate: **882 files — equal to the suite file count — 13,392 tests, 0 AssertionErrors, 0 deadlocks**, first
pass, no red chunk. `next build` exit 0. `gate:shadow` **PASS 384/384**, 382 → 384.

### BOTH REPORTERS WERE WRONG ABOUT THEIR OWN SYSTEM, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS

`3c8037be` said approval steps are "only predefined options such as Direct Manager and HR" and levels are
capped at two. **Neither was true.** `leave_approval_template.levels` is jsonb of arbitrary length, and
`LEVEL_KINDS` already carried SEVEN kinds. The flexible multi-level structure they assumed was the hard part
was already built and already running — phase 1's commit title says it: *the visual builder over the
structure that was already there*.

`04d163da` said Earned Accrual "only recognizes Hospitalization Leave and Medical Leave". **`ANNUAL` IS in
`STANDING_LEAVE_CODES`.** Their tenant had three independent causes stacked: `AL` active with a non-standing
code, `ANNUAL` archived, `SICK` archived.

**And MY brief was wrong too**: I told the workflow agent phase 1 must deliver "drag to reorder, add/remove,
automatic renumbering". `StepListEditor` **already had all of them** (6fadb036). So the drag-and-drop
dependency question I braced for never arose and nothing was added. What was actually missing was the card
presentation, the Dynamic/Fixed badge, the per-level skip sentence, and the preview.

### THE MIGRATIONS ARE ON THE STEP, NOT THE TEMPLATE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE ITEM

`leave_approval_step` is the per-request snapshot, written once at submission and never re-resolved — which
is **precisely what makes a template edit safe for in-flight leave**. A step that went back to the template
for its approver or its alternates would silently undo that guarantee. So 0467 `approver_employment_id` and
0468 `approver_alternates`, both nullable, no backfill, **no CHECK** (a NOT VALID check fires on every
`decideLeave` status write), no GRANT.

Template needed none: `serializeApprovalLevels` writes a plain relationship level back as a **bare string**,
so every pre-r293 row round-trips byte-identically.

Numbering from `max(idx)`: 466 → 0467 → 0468. **`entries.length` was 382/383 — a 0383 would have been a
silent skip.**

### THE FIXED APPROVER STALLS, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT ANSWER

A dynamic level resolving to nobody is DROPPED and the chain continues (`core/leave-approval-policy.ts:36-38`).
A fixed level has no relationship to resolve, so `applyChainDropRules` keeps it unconditionally. **Dropping
it instead would silently remove an approval an administrator deliberately configured.** So it stalls, with
`facts.endedFixedApprovers` driving a red banner on the builder card and in the preview, and the HR-admin
override as the escape hatch — which is why it is a stall and not a deadlock.

### A REAL FUNCTIONAL LIMIT, PINNED RATHER THAN HIDDEN

RLS on `leave_request` is `can_see_employment` — subject, manager chain, admins. **A fixed approver who is
a stranger to the subject cannot SEE the request.** Authority passes, the row is invisible, HR clears the
step. That is where a payroll partner or unrelated department head has always been; r293 inherits it and does
not widen it. `test/r293-approval-builder.test.ts` carries a case named `KNOWN LIMIT: …` that fails the day
someone widens it. **Do not promise a customer an arbitrary named person at level 3 without reading it.**

### A DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM THE APPROVED PLAN, DECLARED

The plan told the reporter "the template holds a mode". The build **derived** the mode from the levels
instead, on r79 0322's precedent — *a flag that can disagree with the chain beside it IS the defect*. The
reporter still sees the radio, so the promise holds on screen; the stored shape differs from the plan's
wording. Declared rather than discovered, which is the only reason it is acceptable.

### THREE DEFECTS THAT ONLY RENDERING FOUND, ALL BEHIND GREEN tsc + eslint + SUITE

1. A kind→label map typed `Record<string, string>` printed a raw `specific_employee` on screen.
2. `step-list-editor` and `template-manager` each had their own kind→label `switch` with
   `default: labels.manager`. Phase 2 taught only one, so the template LIST printed **"Direct manager" for a
   Manager's-Manager level** — a WRONG name, not a blank, which no blank-check would have caught.
3. A direct manager refused at a `manager_manager` step was told *"You cannot decide your own leave
   request"* — `assertCanDecide`'s self-ban firing about the manager. Correct refusal, untrue message.

### THE PICKER MARKS ON THE CODE, NOT THE METHOD

`accrueEarnedLeave` returns on the code filter **before it reads a method**, so keying the marking on
`earned_daily` would have marked only half of what the engine declines. Keyed on the code, a festive type
granted in full is marked too — which is correct, because the engine refuses it just the same. Non-swept rows
stay **listed and selectable**, so the engine's typed empty reason remains the authority and the reporter can
still find the type they went looking for.

Names come from the tenant's own rows, never English defaults — verified in real Chromium on the account
with two types called Annual Leave: the one it can pick is marked, the one it cannot is plain.

### AGENTS CAUGHT THEIR OWN VACUOUS PROOFS, TWICE

Phase 4's first non-vacuity probe used a decider who **also passed the primary gate**, so truncating the
approver loop stayed green. Fixed with `payroll` as primary and a plain manager as alternate — the one case
that actually fails. And the picker agent listed exactly which arms stayed green under revert and **why**
(negative arms, vacuously true when nothing renders) rather than claiming a cleaner proof than it had.

### TWO CROSS-AGENT HAZARDS ON SHARED LOCAL STATE

`pkill -f "next dev"` run by one agent was **not scoped to its worktree** and could have killed another
agent's server mid-session (it survived). And `pnpm db:seed` truncated the shared dev database while a second
agent had a server on it. Both are documented procedure; neither is safe when agents run concurrently.
`git checkout <file>` during a revert proof reverts to **HEAD, not to the working state** — CLAUDE.md §10's
exact warning, hit once and recovered from a scratchpad copy.

## r292 (2026-09-16) — module gating goes service-deep, two lies in the code, and a filing state. `main@61bb400f`, **migration 0466**.

Commercial module gating (Part 4), the false email claim + anomaly thresholds (Part 4 / 2.4), and readiness
**3.2** (no filed state). Owner's goal, not the board.
Gate: **879 files — equal to the expected file count — 13,324 tests, 0 AssertionErrors, 0 deadlocks**,
no red chunk. `next build` exit 0. `gate:shadow` **PASS 382/382**, 381 → 382.

### GATING: BIND THE GATE TO `withTenant`, NOT TO 86 MORE PAGES

Only **7 of 198** `page.tsx` carried a module check, and in three of four optional packs it was just the
index page: **attendance 3/23, payroll 1/57, claims 1/6, performance 1/4**. A customer who declined Payroll
could reach **56 of its 57 screens** by typing the URL. The readiness doc named the shape exactly —
gating was **navigation-deep, not service-deep**.

The fix binds a module code to `withTenant` itself (`core/module-gate.ts`), so five one-line import changes
cover **165 entry points**, reads and writes, and every function added to those files later inherits it.
A mechanism, not a discipline — the same argument `db/client.ts` already makes for the suspension overlay.
Plus 25 `layout.tsx` route-level guards (there were none) for a clean redirect.

**Two safety properties, both verified:** `withModuleTenant('leave')` **throws at module load** for any
`isCore: true` code, so a core module cannot be gated by accident — and `leave` is exactly the trap, being
`isCore: true` AND `packBacked: true`. And `requireModule`'s fail-open on an unresolved snapshot was left
alone: `lib/authz.ts` argues it properly — redirecting there "would tell a paying customer their module had
been removed during an infrastructure incident."

**STATED GAP, NOT CLOSED: 6 of ~20 payroll service files are unbound** — `pay-components`, `loans`,
`payroll-cycle`, `tax-relief`, `cp38`, `back-pay`. Their SCREENS are covered by the layouts; their
**server actions are not**, because a POST passes through no layout. Stopping there was right:
`core/payroll-cycle.ts` is called by `core/admin.ts` and `app/admin/organization`, both **core** surfaces,
so binding it blind breaks a tenant that declined nothing. Each remaining file needs the same importer audit.

### THE FEATURE I WOULD HAVE ORDERED BUILT, AND WHY NOT BUILDING IT WAS RIGHT

`payroll_anomaly_config` is empty with no admin screen, so 2,359 findings were classified by thresholds
`core/payroll-anomaly.ts` itself calls numbers "nobody should mistake for empirical". The obvious answer is
a settings screen. **It would have caused real harm**, and the argument is verifiable:
`core/control-tower.ts:155` computes `thresholdsTuned = count(payroll_anomaly_config) > 0`, pushes
`'thresholds_untuned'` into `blockedBy` at :213, and `impliedOperators` nulls on any blocker at :239 — it
**refuses to print a staffing headcount**. Ship a form and the first admin who saves anything at all flips
that flag, and the tower starts projecting headcount from a number with no more evidence than the
placeholder. That file's own header names the stake: **"a confident wrong one gets somebody's job cut."**
Disclosure shipped instead, derived through the same resolver the evaluator uses so the two cannot diverge.

### THE CODE SAID IT SENT EMAIL. THERE IS NO EMAIL. FIVE PLACES, ONE CUSTOMER-VISIBLE.

No transport in the repo (grep for nodemailer/sendgrid/postmark/mailgun/ses/resend = 0), and
`notification_pref` / `notification_delivery` have **zero code references** outside `db/schema.ts` —
migrated in 0078, never built. The one a customer could read was `notices.fNotifyHelp`, in all six locales:
*"Sent through the existing notification settings, so each person's preferences still apply."* There are no
preferences. Now: recipients see it in the in-app bell, no email is sent.

The 0279 recipient exclusion was **re-justified, not deleted**: a notification row **outlives the block and
is not re-authorized when read**, its RLS is person-scoped and role-blind, and its body is frozen text about
another employee — so a lapsed admin would silently accrue a readable backlog. Correct for in-app, for a
reason email had nothing to do with.

### 3.2: A FILING STATE THAT REFUSED TO IMPLEMENT AN ENUM MEMBER

`submitted` and `amended` only. **`final` deliberately not built** — it means "figures locked, not yet
sent", a state in which `statutoryFiled` has no honest answer. *"Implementing a state because the enum
listed it is how 3.2 happened."* `amended` is **derived, not asked**: filing for a
`(company, reportType, periodKey)` that already has a live filed sibling is an amendment by the agencies'
own vocabulary.

**`filed_on` is split from `filed_at`** — the agency date a deadline is judged against, versus the instant
it was keyed. A CP39 lodged on the 15th and entered on the 20th has both; collapsing them makes an on-time
filing read as late.

**3.4 was not made worse:** filing does NOT gate unlock or reset. `batchDownstreamWarnings` has always been
"read and recorded, never a gate", and blocking there would leave a customer who filed a wrong figure unable
to correct it at all.

### EVERY GATE FAILURE WAS A GUARD, NOT A DEFECT — IN EXACTLY TWO KINDS

Five red chunks (2, 4, 10, 12, 13), one file each:

- **Synthetic context, no entitlement snapshot** (2, 10, 12) — the pack services are now gated, so a
  hand-rolled `SessionContext` throws. **The obvious fix is wrong**: every gated pack is `billable: true`,
  and an exempt context asked about a billable module throws `EntitlementsExemptForBillableError` by design.
  `entitlementsExempt` is the majority idiom in `test/` (21 files vs 3) precisely because most of those are
  asked about CORE modules. Resolved a real snapshot instead, reasoning written into each file.
- **Ratchets pinning an exact call spelling** (4, 13) — the decision held, the signature gained an argument.
  **Updated, never loosened**: assert the declared param set is exactly `['moduleUnavailable']`, and count
  CALL SITES rather than matching an argument list. Both stricter than what they replaced and immune to the
  next signature change.

Binding a gate into `withTenant` changes the PRECONDITIONS of 165 entry points, so anything that built a
context by hand or matched a call's exact text gets caught. The agent ran thousands of tests but not all 879
files; this is what the integration gate is for.

### TWO OPERATOR ERRORS OF MINE, BOTH SELF-INFLICTED AND BOTH CONCURRENCY

1. **Ran vitest beside a running gate** → `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5433` when it rebuilt the cluster.
2. **Started the five-chunk re-run while run B still had chunks 23 and 24 to go.** I read
   `grep -c "exit=" run-b.log` → **10**, and treated 10 as 12. Two gates on one cluster produced **7
   deadlocks and 148 failures** in chunk 24, with zero AssertionErrors. Re-run idle: 36/36, 542 tests.

**THE READING RULE, CORRECTED.** "Red chunk with AE=0 is environmental" is INCOMPLETE and nearly cost a real
defect. The discriminator is `counted == asked`:
- AE=0 **and** `counted < asked` → files failed to spawn → environment.
- AE=0 **and** `counted == asked` → every file ran and something **THREW** rather than asserted → real code.
Chunk 2's first failure was the second case (`EntitlementsUnresolvedError`) and the old rule would have
dismissed it. A `deadlock detected` count is the cleaner environmental tell.

Also worth carrying: the final total's `files == expected file count` (879) is `counted == asked` applied to
the whole suite — it is what proves no chunk quietly ran a short list.

## r291 (2026-09-16) — deploy detachment, a health endpoint, and backups. `main@ad5287b8`, **no migration**.

Readiness **7.1** (detach the remote deploy; detect a partway failure), **1.6** (health endpoint + the
alerting configs, written not installed), **1.5** (backup + a restore rehearsal that can fail).
Owner's goal, not the board. Gate: **875 files, 13,274 tests, 0 AssertionErrors**, first pass, every chunk
counted==asked. `next build` exit 0.

### THE CATCH OF THE SESSION: AN EXIT TRAP TURNS A REFUSAL INTO A SUCCESS

Detaching the deploy means an EXIT trap in `deploy/deploy.sh`. **Merely installing one changes what bash
returns after a parameter-expansion error.** Measured here, bash 3.2.57:

```
bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; : "${X:?nope}"'                    → 1
bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; trap "true" EXIT; : "${X:?nope}"'  → 0
```

**Every preflight in `deploy.sh` is that construct** — including r290's `SHARE_PASSWORD` guard, whose entire
job is refusing to publish an open, ungated HRIS. The obvious implementation
(`trap 'rc=$?; finish "$rc"; exit $rc' EXIT`) **silently converts all three refusals into successful
deploys**, undoing a security fix shipped four hours earlier, with nothing red anywhere.

Fixed with an `AIHR_DEPLOY_COMPLETED` flag set at the script's two real end points: the trap believes the
flag, not `$?`. Pinned by seven tests, and the naive version is kept as a revert probe that fails exactly
the three refusal tests.

**The general lesson: a change to a shell script's control flow can disable a guard in a DIFFERENT feature
without touching it.** r290 found the same shape across two branches; this is the same shape across two
rounds.

### AND THE INTEGRATION CHECK THAT r290 TAUGHT US TO RUN

Before the full gate, the cross-branch surface was run on its own — the two r290 deploy files plus the three
new ones, **8 files / 194 tests / 0 AssertionErrors**. That is the check that would have caught r290's merge
defect an hour earlier instead of at chunk 23. **Run the interaction surface before the gate, not after it.**

### A HEALTH CHECK MUST NOT ESCAPE THE FAIL-CLOSED ARM

`/health` bypasses the **401 challenge** but sits BELOW 1.4's unconfigured **503**, verified in the merged
tree's middleware ordering. A deployment with no `SHARE_PASSWORD` is not serving, so `/health` must 503 there
too and the monitor must alarm. **Hoisting that bypass one block higher would report a broken deployment as
healthy** — precisely the failure 1.6 exists to remove.

The disclosure question is answered by making the endpoint **worth nothing to read**: exactly
`{"status":"ok"}` or `{"status":"unhealthy"}`, no version, build id, host, driver text or counts. The reason
is **redirected, not withheld** — it goes to the journal, already behind ssh. Exact path match, so
`/health/anything` stays gated and the unauthenticated surface is one enumerable URL.

**My citation was wrong and the truth is worse.** "77 error lines in the journal went nowhere" is not
reproducible — `journalctl -u aihr -p err --since '7 days ago'` returns **zero**. The real finding:
**Next writes errors to stdout, and systemd files plain stdout at priority `info`, so a priority-based alert
can never see an application error at all.** Anyone wiring `journalctl -p err` would build something
permanently blind. Real failures in that window existed (8 failed employment queries, 4 missing static
files, 4 invariant errors) and were invisible to priority.

Second correction: the provisioning log is **81,847 lines**, every one `· nothing to do`, and **none carries
a timestamp** — after rotation there is nothing to date a line by.

### "DOES IT PARSE" IS NOT AN INTEGRITY CHECK

`pg_restore --list` **reads only the header**. It succeeded unchanged on a dump truncated to half its length
AND on one with its middle overwritten. The obvious verify-the-backup implementation would have been this
session's seventh vacuous guard. Only the checksum and an actual restore catch damage.

**A superuser cannot tell you a restore is usable**, and the proof is the round's best test: a
`--no-privileges` dump restores with **identical schema and identical row counts**, `pg_restore` clean — and
is correctly REJECTED, because the application role can read nothing. A superuser holds every privilege by
construction, and RLS here is ENABLED not FORCED so the owner bypasses every policy. Two real failure modes
live entirely outside its view: lost GRANTs (a database `psql` reads perfectly and the product cannot) and
lost policies (rows back without the isolation — after r290, a cross-tenant leak with the customer's data
already in it).

### THREE DEFECTS THAT ONLY EXECUTION FOUND

1. **`psql -d ""` does not error.** A `sed` substitution delimited by `#` returned an empty database name for
   any name containing `#`; `psql` handed an empty `-d` falls back to the local socket and the invoking
   user's own database. **The restore rehearsal would have inspected a different server and reported
   success.**
2. **The health probe announced a recovery that never happened** — the first healthy probe of a fresh
   process logged `✓ HEALTH: … recovered`.
3. **A status read landing mid-write reported `died` over a deploy that had just started.** Fixed with one
   atomic rename; same class in `finish`, where `last-ok` must be published before `current` is marked ok or
   a clean deploy momentarily reads as `stale-build`.

### THE DETACHMENT TEST HAS A CONTROL, AND NEEDED ONE

It runs the **pre-r291 attached form** through the identical harness and asserts the group SIGKILL *does*
kill it. Without that, "detached survives the kill" would pass against a deploy that was never in danger.
The first `setsid` check compared `ps -o sess=`, **which prints 0 for everything on macOS** and would have
passed vacuously; replaced with a real pgid comparison.

### WHAT IS STILL THE OWNER'S

`BACKUP_DEST` has **no default anywhere** (asserted by a test) and the script refuses without it — writing
beside the database is the current state and is what makes today's dumps worthless. Still to decide: where
backups live, when they run, who hears a failure, whether PITR is needed (`archive_mode` is still `off`),
retention, and whether `deploy.sh` should take a pre-deploy dump — deliberately not wired, because it would
either block every deploy when the destination is unreachable or fail quietly, and which of those is wanted
is not the agent's call.

**The RTO is not yet a real number**: 0.05s against a fixture, because nothing ran `pg_dump` against
production. The first real one has to be taken on the box.

**No observability dependency was added.** The dependency-free path for "application 5xx reaches a human" is
`instrumentation.ts`'s `onRequestError` emitting a `<3>`-prefixed line — designed and deliberately NOT built,
because it also fires for `AuthRequiredError`, one per anonymous visitor, 13 in seven days. Without an error
taxonomy that is an alarm that cries wolf at every logged-out visit, **and a muted channel is worse than
none.**

### TWO SMALL TRUTHS FOR WHOEVER INSTALLS THIS

The logrotate file's installed name **must contain no dot** (`tabooext` skips it wordlessly), and
`su ubuntu ubuntu` must stay or logrotate refuses the group-writable directory and does nothing. Also:
`review-sweep` was **missing from the crontab for six weeks**, which is why the runbook now carries a
staleness check — a job that stops running has no exit code to alert on.

A dangling `# Aged-leave forfeiture — 03:30 daily.` comment sits in the crontab with no command under it.
**Checked: benign** — no such script exists in the repo or on the box, so it is a stale heading from a job
removed with its script, not a sweep silently not running.

## r290 (2026-09-16) — four customer-readiness items, and the merge defect neither branch could see. `main@f87b6c7b`, **migration 0465**.

Readiness **1.1** (the deploy path seeds demo data into a customer's database), **1.4** (the password gate
fails open), **1.7** (the last RLS hole), and the Part 4 **knowledge base** hole — plus a second authoring
door the survey never found. Driven by the owner's goal, not the board.
Gate: **871 files, 13,171 tests, 0 AssertionErrors**, every chunk counted==asked. `next build` exit 0.
`pnpm gate:shadow` **PASS (381/381 against the live-shaped schema)**, 380 → 381.

### THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE HURT A CUSTOMER ON DAY ONE

`deploy/deploy.sh` hard-required `DEV_TENANT_ID` and ran the demo seeder whenever that tenant row was
**absent from the target database** — which on a fresh customer database is **always**. Following the
documented runbook on a customer's box planted `Demo Group` in their production database on the first
deploy, and `db/seed.ts` had no refusal of any kind.

**The lesson is in the guard's shape, not the fix.** The survey proposed refusing on
`NODE_ENV=production && ALLOW_DEMO_SESSION unset`. On its own that is worth very little, and the reason is
worth keeping: **the gated demo box and a customer box that copied the demo template are, in the
environment, the same deployment** — both `NODE_ENV=production`, both `ALLOW_DEMO_SESSION=true`. A guard
built only out of environment variables is satisfiable by the single likeliest operator mistake there is.

So `db/seed-guard.ts` layers four refusals of deliberately **different kinds**, and R4 is the one that
carries the weight: **the target database already holds a tenant row this seeder did not create**, read
live through the owner client immediately before the TRUNCATE. It is the only signal that is about the
DATABASE rather than about a file somebody copied.

**Residual gap, stated rather than hidden:** a customer who copies the DEMO template AND runs the DEMO path
against an EMPTY database is by construction indistinguishable from the demo box. No env guard can close
that. It is closed structurally — the customer path cannot reach the seeder at all.

**Operational consequence on THIS box, verified:** `./deploy/deploy.sh --reseed` will now be **refused**,
because `System (auth audit)` (`00000000-…`) is a second tenant and the seeder's TRUNCATE list includes
`domain_event`, `app_user` and `role_assignment`. That is the guard working — a reseed genuinely would
destroy the auth audit trail. `SEED_MAY_DESTROY_OTHER_TENANTS=1` is the documented escape. **Normal
deploys are untouched**: the demo tenant exists, so the seeder is never invoked, proven by a byte-identical
execution trace against main for no-args, `--reseed` and `--migrate-only`.

### THE MERGE DEFECT: TWO GREEN BRANCHES, ONE RED TREE

Chunk 23 came back **RED with 9 AssertionErrors** — *not* the `AE=0` environment signature, so it was real.
Every failure read `expected 1 to be +0`.

1.4 added a hard `: "${SHARE_PASSWORD:?…}"` preflight to `deploy/deploy.sh` **above everything 1.1's
deploy-path tests exercise**. On the merged tree the script exited 1 before reaching any seeder decision,
and nine assertions failed while saying nothing whatsoever about seeding. **Neither agent could have caught
it: each branch was green alone.**

**The product was correct** — both `deploy/.env.customer.example` and `deploy/.env.production.example` set
`SHARE_PASSWORD`, so no operator is affected. Only the fixtures, written before the preflight existed, were
out of step with the templates they model. Fixed there, with the refusal left pinned where it belongs in
`test/share-gate.test.ts`.

**This is the argument for an integration gate over per-branch greens**, and it is the first time this
session that the merged tree failed where every branch passed.

### 1.4 — A PER-REQUEST GUARD CANNOT BE A STARTUP REFUSAL, SO IT IS BOTH

Middleware runs per request, so "refuse to start" is not achievable there. The **real** arm is a deploy
preflight (`deploy/deploy.sh:113`), before install/build/migrate, so the box is never rebuilt and keeps
serving the previous gated build. The **backstop** is a per-request **503** for any start that did not come
through the deploy script — and auth routes refuse too, because a missing password is a broken deployment,
not a gate decision.

Deliberately **not** a `next.config.ts` throw: that would break `next build` for every developer and the
repo's own gate. Proven on a real `next start` built WITHOUT the variable (503 on `/`, `/login`, `/people`)
and the same build with it supplied at runtime (401), which also proves nothing is inlined at build time.

### 1.7 — BOTH REMEDIES, BECAUSE ONE OF THEM SILENTLY UNDOES ITSELF

`tenant_suspension_window` was the one table of 173 without RLS, with `ai_hr_app` holding full CRUD.
Chose **revoke every privilege AND enable RLS with no policy** — not either/or. The reason: the grant exists
only because `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` hands it out, so **a re-bootstrap would silently restore it**;
RLS-with-no-policy survives that. Not `FORCE`, because here the legitimate writers *are* the owner.
All six cron jobs checked first — none references the table, all connect as `ai_hr_owner`, which `ENABLE`
does not filter.

**0453's own comment is wrong, and that is why this survived.** It lists this table among those `ai_hr_app`
"CANNOT read … LEFT ALONE, BECAUSE THEY ARE CORRECT." True of a REBUILT cluster; false of every
BOOTSTRAPPED one. Production measured `DELETE,INSERT,SELECT,UPDATE`.

**Migration numbering, checked rather than assumed:** 0465 is also taken on `build/r279-credit`. That branch
is permanently unmerged and this history's own r279 entry says the *resumed branch* must re-derive — so 0465
was free on main and was used. Verified: not in main's tree, r279-credit not an ancestor of main.

### THE KNOWLEDGE BASE HAD TWO DOORS, AND NO DATABASE BACKSTOP

`createArticleAction` ran on a bare session with no admin gate. The survey missed **`uploadFileAction`** —
identical exposure, any employee uploading 10 MB at any audience. Both now admin-only.

**The detail that matters for anyone who later touches this:** `0039_kb_rls.sql`'s INSERT policy is
`WITH CHECK (tenant_id = app.current_tenant_id())` and nothing more — ADR-0017 §3 deliberately chose open
contribution. **There is no RLS backstop for a create.** Unlike every other admin write in this product,
the application guard is the only one. A test pins that a raw INSERT is *still accepted by Postgres*, so a
green refusal test can never be mistaken for RLS doing the work.

### TWO FINDINGS BEYOND THIS ROUND'S SCOPE

- **`ai_hr_platform` does not exist on production.** Migration 0351's `DO` block took its skip branch, so
  ADR-0077 D5's plane isolation is **currently unrealised on the live box** — a defence one might believe is
  in place and is not.
- **`next build` warns the `middleware` file convention is deprecated** in Next 16.2.7 ("use `proxy`").
  Untouched, but 1.4's enforcement now lives partly in that file.

## r289 (2026-09-16) — the paste box takes the Employee ID you can see. `main@b2f55cb8`, **no migration**.

`0d2b17ce`, raised by the operator loop after r288 and approved by the reporter. `3fb1a611` still not built.
Gate: **868 files, 13,106 tests, 0 AssertionErrors** across 24 chunks at 2 workers, every chunk counted==asked,
no chunk with a single failure. `next build` exit 0.

### I CALLED THIS GAP THE WRONG SHAPE FOR A WHOLE ROUND

At the end of r288 I told the owner that closing the paste-door gap "means a second, weaker validator in
front of `resolveOrgCriteriaTargets`, which the module header warns against", and left it as a decision.
**That framing was mine, not the code's, and it was wrong.**

The actual defect is smaller and worse: the paste box accepts ONLY the internal employment uuid, which is
**never displayed anywhere in the product**. It does not accept `EMP-0008` — the Employee ID a person can
see, copy and paste out of a spreadsheet. The box was unusable for the one job it exists to do, and its help
text said "paste employee references" while every reference a human can obtain was the wrong kind.

The fix is a **RESOLVER, not a validator**, and that distinction is what makes the header irrelevant rather
than violated: it translates code to id BEFORE the restriction is handed over. `resolveOrgCriteriaTargets`
still decides who qualifies, unchanged. The unmatched-token report is a MESSAGE, not a gate — and an
unmatched token is **still passed through** so it resolves to nobody, because dropping a typo would make a
smaller run look like one that succeeded.

Proven off the real write path rather than from a helper: a mixed paste reached Postgres as
`employment.id in ($3, $4)` with `params: …,89d13468-…,NOPE-1`. The code became a uuid; the typo survived
verbatim.

### THE AGENT BROKE MY BRIEF ON PURPOSE AND WAS RIGHT

I wrote "no new query — the picker has already loaded the list". **The client's list cannot reach the write
path.** A resolution performed only in the browser puts the population the screen CONFIRMS out of step with
the one the write COVERS — precisely the class `lib/employment-selection.ts` exists to prevent, as its own
header says. So `core/read.ts` gained `listEmployeePickOptions` and the three server actions resolve for
themselves. "No new endpoint, no round trip" still holds on the browser side.

**And my "three consumers" undercounted by half.** `mergeEmploymentSelection` has SIX call sites — three
forms and three server actions — and the write paths were the load-bearing half.

### THREE THINGS THE CODE KNEW THAT THE PLAN DID NOT

1. **`fold()` was module-private.** "Reuse it" was impossible as written; it is now exported as
   `foldEmployeeCode` with `const fold = foldEmployeeCode` so existing call sites read unchanged.
2. **`employee_code` IS NULLABLE** (`db/schema.ts:844`, no `.notNull()`). I had asserted uniqueness and
   stopped there. Decision taken and pinned: **a NULL or blank code names nobody.** Postgres treats NULLs as
   distinct in that unique index, so a tenant that has not adopted Employee IDs has many such rows, and
   indexing the empty string would let a stray token match whichever was read first. Those people stay
   reachable by picker and by internal id.
3. **`EMP-0008` and `EMP0008` are both legal codes that FOLD TO ONE KEY.** A folded collision is refused,
   not guessed (`core/payroll-txn-import.ts`'s precedent); the exact spelling still wins.

### THE SEPARATOR ATE THE SPELLING THE MOCKUP PROMISED

The plan's mockup showed `EMP 0008` working. Whitespace is the box's OWN separator, so it arrives as two
tokens (`EMP`, `0008`) and no amount of folding fixes that. `repairRuns` rejoins runs of up to four tokens —
but **only tokens that resolved to nothing on their own**, and **only when the join resolves to exactly one
employment**. So it can move a token out of "matched nobody" into "matched exactly one real person" and out
of no other state. It never re-reads a token that already named someone, and never picks between candidates.

Worth keeping as a general lesson: **a mockup can promise an input format the parser cannot deliver**, and
the separator is the first thing to check when it does.

### THE DOM GUARDS GO THROUGH REAL next-intl NOW

r288's lesson applied rather than restated: the leave screens' `t(key, { list })` is exercised through
`NextIntlClientProvider` with the real message catalogue, which is what makes these assertions blind to
nothing — unlike the sixteen jsdom guards that were green over r288's `FORMATTING_ERROR`s because they read
`messages/en.json` directly. Dev log across all three routes: `FORMATTING_ERROR|MISSING_MESSAGE|IntlError`
count **0**.

Locale parity is now checked by **key-path SET equality per locale**, not by count: 11,079 leaf keys,
identical paths in all six. A count alone cannot see a swapped key.

### ENVIRONMENT

The wedged-cluster backlog came down from 69 to the high 30s, partly from the gate's own draining and partly
by hand, after establishing what the earlier note got wrong: **one of those directories was a SYMLINK to the
LIVE RAM-disk data**, left by a `mv` that moved the link instead of the directory — exactly what
`scripts/dev-db-rebuild.sh:96-99` warns about. A guard comparing `readlink -f` output does NOT catch it
(BSD `readlink -f` returns empty for the live link), and nothing was lost only because `rm -rf` does not
dereference a symlink given as its argument. **Test `-L` directly.** The remainder are all real directories.

The cleanup was killed mid-run for low memory while the gate was running — free pages were down to ~3,769.
That is the correct thing to sacrifice, and the reason not to run the two together.

## r288 (2026-09-16) — the two items CLAUDE AI raised, and a 200 that was lying. `main@aabe4134`, **no migration**.

`686dc512` (warn when an earned method can never accrue) and `8521e160` (the real picker on Leave
Adjustments + Notice Board) — both raised by the operator loop during r287 and approved by the reporter
within the hour. `3fb1a611` still not built.
Gate: **866 files, 13,071 tests, 0 AssertionErrors** across 24 chunks at 2 workers, every chunk counted==asked, no chunk with a single failure. `next build` exit 0.

### A GREEN 200 WITH A BROKEN SCREEN BEHIND IT, TWICE, IN DIFFERENT WAYS

Both agents ran a dev server, and both found that **`200` plus a clean-looking payload is not a render**.

**`8521e160`.** `/admin/notice-board/new` returned 200 while the log carried three
`FORMATTING_ERROR: The intl string context variable "query" was not provided`, and the payload carried the
raw key path `notices.fEmployeeNoMatch` where the empty-state sentence belongs. **The popover would have
shown users a key path.** The three template labels are ICU strings the client substitutes; a bare `t()`
formats them, finds no variable and falls back to the key.

**tsc, eslint and all sixteen jsdom guards were green over it** — and structurally had to be: a jsdom guard
builds those labels straight out of `messages/en.json` and never touches next-intl, so the entire failure
class is invisible to it. Fixed with the `app/admin/personnel/[employmentId]/page.tsx` idiom,
`t(key, { query: '{query}' })`, which keeps the keys inside i18n check C. **`t.raw()` would have worked and
hidden them from that check** — worth knowing which of the two options is the trap.

**`686dc512`.** `/admin/leave-config/types` returned 200 and the catalogue string WAS in the payload — with
a literal unsubstituted `{swept}`. The agent refused to count it, correctly: the warning lives on tab 3, the
workspace mounts only `panels[selected]`, and `activeTab` defaults to `identity`, so the form is **never in
the SSR HTML at all**. That is CLAUDE.md §8's "a key is not a screen" trap in its purest form — the string
being present proved only that the catalogue had been read.

It proved the boundary from the RSC payload instead (`codeIsSwept:false` for the AL type and `true` for
ANNUAL in the same payload), then used the repo's existing real-browser project for the paint:
`oklch(0.666 0.179 58.318)` = amber-600 from compiled Tailwind, box 390x64, and the sentence naming
**Cuti Tahunan Syarikat, MC, Ward Leave** — renamed tenant types, not the English defaults. That last
assertion is the one that matters: this tenant has two types both called a variant of Annual Leave, and a
hardcoded string would have produced a riddle on the exact account that raised the item.

### I DESCRIBED THE NOTICE BOARD DEFECT WRONG, AND IT IS WORSE THAN I SAID

My plan said the typed text is "carried all the way to Save and refused there". **It is not refused. It is
SAVED.** `notice.criteria` is a **jsonb** column (`db/schema.ts:4664`) and `cleanNotice`
(`core/notice.ts:143-146`) only checks the list is non-empty, so `"Irwin"` is stored verbatim. The draft page
then computes reach as `(n.criteria.employmentIds ?? []).length` (`[id]/page.tsx:60`) and promises
**"1 employee"**, and the publish confirmation repeats that number, before dying at `publishNotice`
(`core/notice.ts:304`). Measured against a real database, not argued:

```
STORED criteria: {"employmentIds":["Irwin"]}
PUBLISH ERROR:   invalid input syntax for type uuid: "Irwin"
```

**Checked production before reporting it: 1 notice total, 0 using individual targeting, 0 poisoned.** No
live data affected, so nothing for the reporter to clean up — which is the only reason this did not become a
third correction item.

My second claim was also wrong and in the same direction: I said a failed preview on Adjustments leaves a
**stale count**. It does not — `setPreview(null)` renders `adjustmentsMatchedPending` ("Working it out…"),
i.e. *exactly* the defect r287 fixed on Generate. `test/leave-adjustment-step-flow.dom.test.tsx` was
already pinning that behaviour and was **updated rather than deleted**; the new guard asserts the superset.

### THE MESSAGE-KEY COUNT I KEPT QUOTING WAS THE WRONG METRIC

Both agents flagged "11605 keys" as a wrong citation. It was not wrong, it was a different measure: **11605
counted every `"key":` including object nodes; the leaf count was 11059.** Both moved together and both
stayed identical across all six locales, which is the invariant that actually matters. Recorded so the next
round quotes **leaf keys** and the two numbers stop looking like a contradiction. After r288: **11076 leaf
keys, identical across six**, verified by key-path set equality per locale rather than by count alone.

### `STANDING_LEAVE_CODES` IS NOW REFERENCED FROM `app/` FOR THE FIRST TIME

That absence was the whole gap: the editor would accept an earned accrual method on a code the sweep can
never reach, silently, which is how `*Annual Leave` came to look correctly configured. The warning reads the
three swept names **from the tenant's own rows** (the `core/leave.ts:7391-7394` query, not `:7383-7390` as I
cited — that range is the `standing` Set and the `notSwept` filter) and **does not block the save**: a
tenant may legitimately keep such a type for a non-accruing purpose.

### PROCESS NOTE THAT COST A SILENT FALSE GREEN

`686dc512`'s agent hit this and caught it: `NODE_FILES=$(...)` followed by `$NODE_FILES` **does not
word-split in zsh**. Its first affected-tests run silently executed **6 files instead of 52 and reported
green**. It was caught by comparing the counted file total against the requested one — the same
`counted == asked` assertion the gate script makes, applied by hand. Third time this session that check has
caught something the exit code did not.

### RESIDUAL GAP, FLAGGED RATHER THAN FIXED UNASKED

The **paste door can still carry a typed name to failure on all three screens**, including the one that
shipped in r287. Closing it would mean a second, weaker validator in front of `resolveOrgCriteriaTargets`,
which `lib/employment-selection.ts`'s own header warns against. Left as a decision rather than taken.

Also retired this round: `adjustmentsEmploymentIdsHelp`, `notices.fEmploymentIdsHelp` and their orphaned
labels, across six locales, after verifying nothing references them **including computed `t(\`…${x}\`)`
forms** — the search that a plain grep would have missed.

## r287 (2026-09-16) — four approved items, three worktrees, and six plan claims that did not survive contact. `main@69967dc2`, **no migration**.

`f3e6c36e` + `e4471e3c` (attendance, sequential in one worktree because they rewrite the same nav arrays and
the same exact-set guards), `ec991c2a` (archived leave types), `ff1c935f` (Pick individually).
`3fb1a611` deliberately NOT built — superseded, its own rev-2 plan says press Withdraw.
Gate: **862 files, 12,997 tests, 0 AssertionErrors** across 24 chunks at 2 workers, every chunk counted==asked, no chunk with a single failure. `next build` exit 0..

### THE PLANS WERE RIGHT ABOUT WHAT WAS WRONG AND WRONG ABOUT WHY — AGAIN

Three of the four builds corrected a plan I wrote. The conclusions held every time; the **mechanisms** did not.
That is now a nine-round pattern and it is worth naming: a plan that reasons from a grep is confident in
exactly the places it should not be.

**`ff1c935f` — the worst of them.** I wrote that the resolver "tries to match typed text against employee
REFERENCES" and a name "resolves to nothing". There is no reference resolution anywhere on that path.
`core/org-criteria.ts:338` does `inArray(employment.id, scopeIds)` against a **uuid** column, so Postgres
rejects the statement outright:

```
ERROR:  invalid input syntax for type uuid: "Irwin"
```

The action throws, the caller's `catch` set `preview = null`, and null rendered as the **pending** sentence.
So the reporter's screenshot was **two defects wearing one symptom**, and my framing described one of them.
I also named the wrong file: the textarea is in `components/leave/generate-form.tsx`, not the page.

**`ec991c2a` — half the plan was already built.** I cited `app/leave/page.tsx:225` as feeding the Apply Leave
dropdown. The line was right, the claim was wrong: the dropdown comes from `listEligibleLeaveTypesFor` on
:228, which has carried `isNull(leaveType.archivedAt)` all along, and `listLeaveTypes` already defaults to
excluding archived. The page's own comment says so. **Only the `core/read.ts` balance leak was real** — that
citation (:2364) was correct and both `where` clauses genuinely had no archived predicate.

**`f3e6c36e` — a guard claim that was conditional, not factual.** I wrote that a new route "needs a SCREENS
entry or `test/function-access.test.ts` fails". It does not: that test only collects pages whose source
matches `/requireAdmin|…|scopedSession/`, and all five sibling self-service rows deliberately use
`getSession()` and are unregistered. The agent made the claim true rather than dodging it.

### AN ACCESS-CONTROL GUARD THAT A COMMENT CAN SATISFY

`test/function-access.test.ts:41` is `GUARD_RE.test(fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8'))` — **raw source, comments
included**. A doc comment quoting `'scopedSession'` is enough to make an unguarded page count as guarded.
It over-includes rather than under-includes (a real guard call always contains the string), so this is a
wart and not a hole — but it is a wart on the file that decides which pages get access-checked at all,
and it should be reading stripped source.

### TWO MORE VACUOUS GUARDS, BOTH CAUGHT BY THE AGENT THAT WROTE THEM

That is the fifth and sixth this session, and the first two found by the author rather than by me.

- **`ec991c2a`**: the history assertion passed with the fix reverted, because an *approved* request enters
  none of `leaveBalances`' three tails. Adding a ledger accrual made it live — the non-vacuity probe went
  from 3 failures to 4.
- **`ff1c935f`**: "picked AND pasted for the same person is ONE person" passed with de-duplication removed,
  because `core/leave-generation.ts` calls `dedupe()` further down and the engine reported 2 either way.
  **The guard was measuring the engine, not the merge.** Fixed by asserting the merge's own output.

Both wrote the reason into the test file so nobody strengthens it back out. That is the habit that works.

### THE DEFECT ONLY A LIVE SAVE COULD FIND

`e4471e3c`'s rounding form was first keyed on `attendance_rule_ot_row.id`. `updateAttendanceRule`
**deletes and re-inserts the bands**, so every row id changes on every save of the rule — an id-keyed field
silently matches nothing after any intervening save and the edit is discarded **behind a 303**. No type
error, no failing assertion, no log line. Re-keyed on `fromMinutes` (unique per rule by the ladder
validation, stable across re-insert) with a guard that reproduces the churn.

**This is the argument for rendering instead of reasoning, in one paragraph.** tsc was clean, the tests were
green, and the form silently threw away the user's edit.

### WHAT WAS DECLINED, AND WHY THAT WAS RIGHT

- **`ec991c2a` — no server-side refusal of an archived type in `requestLeave`.** It looks like the obvious
  completion of "cannot be chosen for a new request". It would have broken production: Emergency Leave
  decomposes into **ANNUAL + UNPAID children** (`core/leave.ts:2712`), and ANNUAL is the archived type on
  this tenant. A hard refusal kills EL submissions on the very account that raised the item.
- **`ff1c935f` — did not fix the same bug on Leave Adjustments and Notice Board.** Same `inArray` over a uuid
  column, same shared "paste employee references" help string, worse symptoms (a **stale** matched count,
  and a refusal that only lands at Save). Widening an approved item into two screens the reporter never
  approved is not thoroughness. **Raised as `8521e160` with its own plan.**
- **`e4471e3c` — the deduction switch did not move**, as the plan promised. Proven three ways: no control in
  the page source, the action never reads the field, and a crafted request body cannot flip it.

### A CORRECTION OWED TO THE REPORTER, NOW ON THE BOARD (`686dc512`)

`cf9dcb98`'s business half told them `*Annual Leave` generates nothing because its entitlement tables start
on 14/15 September — which implies that changing those dates would fix it. **It never will.**
`STANDING_LEAVE_CODES` (`core/leave.ts:6031`) is `['ANNUAL','SICK','HOSPITALIZATION']` and the filter at
:7362 runs **before any employment is read**. The engine's own comment at :7195 already said
*"THIS IS THE PRODUCTION CASE: AL is not ANNUAL"* — the build was right and the explanation was not.

The raised item also closes the gap that created the problem: **nothing under `app/` or `messages/`
references `STANDING_LEAVE_CODES`**, so the Leave Type editor accepts an earned accrual method on a code
that can never accrue, in silence. That is how `*Annual Leave` came to look correctly configured.

### THE "DATA LEAK" WAS A COMMENT THAT WAS WRONG, AND IT IS NOW THE COMMENT THAT IS FIXED

`f3e6c36e`'s agent reported that a plain employee opening `/attendance` saw a colleague's month-summary row.
Its evidence for "plain employee" was the absence of the recompute / import / OT-export controls — and those
are gated on `hr_admin || super_admin` ONLY, so their absence proves very little. I expected a misread.

**The observation was right and my expected explanation was wrong.** `EMP-0004` really does hold `employee`
and nothing else, and really can see three other employments. Evaluated `app.can_see_employment` directly
with the RLS GUCs set, branch by branch:

| row | branch that grants it |
|---|---|
| EMP-0002 | `heads_department_of` |
| EMP-0006 | `is_admin_report_of` |
| EMP-0007 | `heads_department_of` |

**It is not a leak.** Line management and department headship are ORG-STRUCTURE facts held on the employment
row; they are independent of the RBAC role list. Someone can carry only `employee` and still be an HOD, and
RLS is correct to show them their tree.

What was actually wrong is `lib/permissions.ts:19`, which said a `scopedSession` page means "an employee opens
the page but sees only their own rows". That is false for any line manager or HOD, and **an agent checking the
screen against that sentence correctly concluded something was broken.** Replaced with the four branches
spelled out and the seed evidence, so the next reader stops where this round stopped.

Method note worth keeping: RLS was confirmed live along the way by accident — an un-tenanted `ai_hr_app`
session reads `SELECT count(*) FROM employment` as **0**, because `tenant_id = app.current_tenant_id()` is
false. `postgres` (BYPASSRLS) sees 8. That contrast is a cheap standing check that RLS is actually on.

### ENVIRONMENT — THE SAME ONE, STILL UNFIXED

69 abandoned Postgres clusters (~233 MB each, ~16 GB) still sit in `/opt/homebrew/var`. Clearing them is
what r286 identified as the durable fix and **the permission classifier blocks the bulk delete**; I did not
route around it. Note for whoever does: `scripts/dev-db-rebuild.sh` rebuilds the cluster at 5433, which
hosts **both** `ai_hr_dev` and `ai_hr_test` — so a running gate wipes the dev database, and an agent doing a
live render check against it mid-gate will see its data vanish. One agent hit exactly that and reported it
as "another agent re-seeded the database".

## r286 (2026-09-16) — text overspill: one shared component, and an SVG that cannot wrap. `main@7bf6e051`, **no migration**.

Reported directly by the owner, not through the board: *"throughout the system, there's a lot of such cases
where the words overspill"*, with the org chart and the Control Tower loop as the two screenshots.
Gate: **857/857 files, 12,931 tests, 0 AssertionErrors**. Verified live: service active, `GET /` 401, fresh
BUILD_ID, migrations 380, rsync dry-run clean.

### THE SYSTEMIC HALF WAS ONE COMPONENT, WHICH IS WHY IT LOOKED EVERYWHERE

`components/ui.tsx` `EmployeeName` renders from **28 files**. Callers pass `truncate` in `className` and
reasonably expect clipping. **It could never work.** `truncate` is overflow-hidden + text-overflow-ellipsis
+ nowrap, and on an **inline-flex** box the ellipsis applies to that box's own inline text — of which it has
none — never to its flex children. The name span was itself a flex item sitting at its automatic minimum
content width, so it refused to shrink and ran straight through the card border.

The reporter's screenshot contains the proof: in the same card the *role* line (a plain block with
`truncate`) ellipsised correctly while the *name* beside it overspilled. Same class, same card, different
box type.

Fixed as: `min-w-0` on the group so it can shrink inside its parent; `min-w-0 truncate` on the NAME so it
actually clips; `shrink-0` on the employee ID, because a half-eaten identifier is worse than a clipped name.

### THE SECOND SCREENSHOT WAS A DIFFERENT BUG WITH THE SAME SYMPTOM

The Control Tower loop's five step boxes are SVG `<text>`, which neither wraps nor ellipsises. A caption
wider than the 172px box ran past both edges into its neighbours — `step4Sub` *"accept, fix, or approve what
the AI proposes closing"* is ~250px at 10.5px. Replaced with `foreignObject` + HTML, which wraps on its own.
**Shortening the English string would have fixed the screenshot and left the bug**, since the five other
locales run longer again. Geometry unchanged, so every arrow and coordinate still lines up. Verified in a
real browser: all five boxes report `scrollHeight == box height`, `overflows: false`.

### THE GUARD IS SOURCE-SHAPE ON PURPOSE

`test/r286-employee-name-truncation.test.ts` pins the three class names that carry the behaviour.
**jsdom has no layout engine — it reports every width as 0** — so a rendered test cannot observe overflow and
would pass just as happily against the broken version. This session found four vacuous guards; that reasoning
is written into the test rather than left for a later reader to rediscover.

### THE GATE COMPOUNDS ITS OWN ENVIRONMENT, AND THAT IS NEW

Chunks 21-24 failed on the first pass with **zero AssertionErrors**, chunk 23 counting **34 of 35** files, and
**116 "does not exist"** — the cluster-died signature. Load went **8.9 at chunk 12 to 56 by chunk 21**.

Cause: each chunk rebuilds the Postgres cluster, and every rebuild moves the old one aside for a background
`rm -rf` — queued behind a **116-deep backlog** of wedged clusters. Caught `rm -rf …wedged-20260910-081436`
burning 20% CPU DURING the run, feeding Spotlight (**152% CPU**) and Trend Micro's endpoint extensions
(38% + 16%). So a longer gate degrades the conditions it is running in. Re-run at load ~12: all four green,
`counted==asked`, chunk 23 back to 35/35. **Durable fix is the owner's: AV/Spotlight exclusions for the repo
and the pg RAM disk, and clearing the wedged backlog.**

### TWO MISTAKES OF MINE, RECORDED

1. **The gate receipt was invalid JSON** — heredoc written without a closing brace, so it would not parse.
2. **`rsync … | tail -1` swallowed the exit code and I printed "rsync ok" over a real failure.** The transfer
   had died with `Network is unreachable` and NOTHING deployed on that attempt. Same class as trusting a
   background task's notification instead of reading its log: **the check must be on the thing itself, not on
   what is printed near it.** Re-run with the exit code captured and branched on.

## r281 (2026-09-15) — eight approved items shipped: the Leave Config restructure, the archived filter, the approval tie-break, the Schedule Group assignment. `main@f7a0bc9e`, **no migration**.

Closed: `09386e29` · `a73d1e14` · `cdd7500b` · `8a494721` · `a3411394` · `53e914fe` · `f513ec02` · `f3e6c36e`.
Gate: **849/849 files, 12,828 tests, 0 AssertionErrors** across 24 chunks; `next build` clean. Verified live:
rsync dry-run clean, service active, `GET /` 401, fresh BUILD_ID, migrations **380** (unchanged — no
migration this round), **0 employments in a Schedule Group**, **toil module not granted** so the Replacement
Leave section stays gated. Four worktrees, disjoint clusters, merged with zero conflicts.

### MY PLANS WERE WRONG IN SEVEN PLACES AND THE AGENTS WERE RIGHT EVERY TIME

Recording this as a pattern, not as seven incidents: **the plans were written faster than their specifics
were verified against the code.** Each correction below came from an agent reading the file I cited.

1. **`53e914fe`: I named the wrong code entirely.** All four `ORDER BY` sites I cited are listings —
   `listLeaveApprovalRules`, `listOrgScopedApprovalRules`, `listLegacyApprovalRules`,
   `listActiveApprovalRules`. **None routes anything.** The read that decides is `loadApprovalRuleSet`
   (`core/leave-approval-policy.ts:183`), which had **no `ORDER BY` at all**, and `decideApproval` takes
   `matching[0]` whenever `beats()` separates nothing. My plan would have shipped an item titled "this
   changes who approves a person's leave" that changed nothing about approval.
2. **…and the mechanism was half right.** `now()` being transaction-start is real, but the operative cause
   needs no transaction: the driver returns `created_at` as a JS `Date` in **milliseconds** while the column
   holds **microseconds**, so rows written 300µs apart tie in JS and not in SQL. That is what actually made
   the flaky test flaky — it used two consecutive autocommit inserts that never shared a transaction.
3. **…and the test shape I prescribed would have been vacuous.** "Stability across repeated calls" stays
   green against the defect, because repeated identical queries return the same heap order. The agent ranked
   the in-memory array in both directions instead — and its own first draft passed with the fix reverted
   (it had omitted the tied-pair insert), which it caught and fixed in its own second commit.
4. **`f513ec02`: "the Employment tab, beside Holiday Group" is self-contradictory.** Holiday Group has been
   on the **Attendance** tab since `52a30630`. Built where it actually lives.
5. **…and "the same service that writes the column" did not exist.** r277 shipped the column, the resolution
   and the refusal but **no writer at all**.

## r279 addendum (2026-09-15) — the block that wrote an audit event for a transition that never happened

Correcting the r279 entry below, which recorded only half of this.

`scripts/improve/remote.ts` `markBlockedSql` runs THREE statements in one transaction:

1. `UPDATE feedback_request SET status='blocked' … WHERE id = X AND status = 'approved'` — guarded
2. `INSERT INTO feedback_block … WHERE EXISTS (… status = 'blocked')` — guarded
3. `INSERT INTO domain_event … 'feedback.blocked' …` — **UNGUARDED**

Blocking `3fb1a611` while it was `building` therefore changed nothing (0 rows), recorded no block question
(`blocked_reason` NULL, no `feedback_block` row), and **still wrote a `feedback.blocked` domain event** —
2026-09-15 12:13:41, with `updated_at` still reading the previous day's `build.started`. The audit trail
asserts a transition the state never made, and the CLI printed success throughout. **The unguarded
statement is the one that writes history.** Fix: guard statement 3 like statement 2. Not done here — it is
tooling, and it wants its own change rather than a drive-by.

**The false status blocked its own cleanup.** `core/feedback.ts:377` refuses `cancelFeedback` for a
`building` item and `assertReporter` limits withdrawal to the reporter, so the item could not be cancelled
*because* it claimed to be building. There is no `cancel` verb in the improve CLI (12 verbs; the 20 existing
cancellations came from the app), and production is SELECT-only. Resolved through the only supported lever:
**`push-plan` revision 2 on `3fb1a611`**, which moved it `building` → `planned` and asks the reporter to
press Withdraw — stated plainly as "do not approve this one".

**Chronology, verified from `domain_event`, since it is the whole justification for stopping the build:**
`3fb1a611` submitted 14 Sep 17:25, approved 18:09, build started 18:18. `8a494721` (remove Replacement
Leave) submitted 14 Sep **19:18 — an hour after that build began** — and approved 15 Sep 10:32. The removal
is the later instruction, so Leave Credit does not ship. `build/r279-credit` keeps its 6 commits unmerged;
main's journal stays 380 entries / max idx 464 and 0465 is not in the tree. **If it is ever resumed, do not
reuse 0465 — re-derive from max(idx) then.**

The map build's attribution assertion (`toContain('© OpenStreetMap contributors')`) **stayed green after

### ENVIRONMENT, NOT CODE — and it cost hours

The first two gate attempts went red with **zero AssertionErrors**, four files never spawning, and durations
50× normal (import 10,255s). Cause: **Spotlight `mds` at 104% CPU and Trend Micro `iCoreService` at 35%**,
scanning every file the suite creates — the gate rebuilds the Postgres cluster per chunk on a RAM disk.
Fix that worked: **24 chunks instead of 12** (35 files each) at `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2`, so a `resetDb` never
queues behind 70 workers. Chunks 1/8/12 re-ran green unchanged; the four files that timed out at 30s inside
a 71-file chunk pass **alone in 43s**. Durable fix is a machine-level AV/Spotlight exclusion — the owner's
call, not ours.

**I made it worse:** I piped the gate through `grep | tail`, which buffered all output AND backgrounded it —
the exact thing this file already warns against. Redirect to a file; never pipe a gate.

### FOUND EN ROUTE — raised separately, deliberately NOT fixed here

**Which approver routes a leave request is decided by an unstable sort.** Four `ORDER BY` clauses on
`leave_approval_policy` end at `createdAt` with no `id` tiebreak — `core/leave-approval-policy.ts:707`,
`core/leave-approval-template.ts:248`, `core/leave-approval-consolidation.ts:196` and `:468`. `createdAt`
is `defaultNow()` and **Postgres `now()` is transaction-start time**, so two policies written in one
transaction tie exactly and the order is formally undefined. Same defect class as r270's `winReasonFor`.
Not fixed in this round on purpose: adding the tiebreak changes **which** policy wins wherever timestamps
currently tie, and that is a live change to approval authority with no business in a round about balance
columns, a menu row and a map.

## r278-plan (2026-09-14) — the two open items planned. `main@b27351d8`, nothing built.

### `3fb1a611` "Leave Credit" — the reporter designed, in detail, the engine we already shipped

They sent a fourteen-point architecture for replacement leave as an earned credit: earn on a non-working
day, manager approves, credit with expiry, FIFO consumption, `Available = Earned − Used − Reserved`, an
eligibility policy instead of a hard-coded salary rule. **`core/toil.ts` (1503 lines, ADR-0033) already is
that engine, and TOIL and Replacement Leave are one thing named twice** — the UI already says "Replacement
Leave" everywhere; "TOIL" survives only in table names and `/admin/toil`.

Eight of their fourteen points are shipped: `bankToilCreditTx` (:575) behind three earn paths; the mint is
the manager's approval (`core/replacement-request.ts:433`, and `submitReplacementLeaveRequest` says in its
own header that it "GRANTS NOTHING"); expiry frozen at approval (`:701-703`); **FIFO by expiry at
`core/toil.ts:970`** — the only such consumption in the repo; `availableLeaveBalance` already subtracts
pending; the 8-criterion eligibility picker exists **and this tenant has already filled it in** (55 grades,
21 positions, 18 departments, 9 companies, 6 named employees).

**Why it looks absent — three switches, any one of them sufficient, all verified live:** no `tenant_module`
row for `toil` (9 modules active, `toil` not among them); **no leave type with `role = 'replacement'`** —
the only candidate, code `REPLACEMENT`, was archived 2026-08-14 **with `role` NULL**, so `leaveTypeIs` is
false for it and un-archiving alone would not be enough; and `auto_accrue_on_approval = false` on both
policies. Result: **0 credits, 0 requests, 0 `in_lieu_accrual` ledger rows — against 44 attendance days
carrying 7,258 OT minutes (~121 h)** worked 2026-06-22 → 09-10. They saved that config screen four times in
August and watched nothing happen.

**DECISIONS the ticket did not settle:**
- **Refused: a separate Leave Credit Ledger.** `leave_ledger` is the single balance authority
  (`core/leave.ts:4499`); `toil_accrual` is a register whose `ledger_entry_id` points INTO it
  (`core/toil.ts:762`), supplying the three things a flat ledger cannot express — per-lot identity, per-lot
  expiry, partial consumption. Their proposed table maps almost column-for-column onto it. A second one
  would make three structures each claim to know the replacement balance. §1. **Extend, and adopt their
  word "Leave Credit" on screen, which costs nothing.**
- **Their RM4,000 premise is inverted, and it is a legal point.** It is not "> RM4,000 ⇒ eligible". It is a
  statutory floor: at or below the ceiling the employee is entitled to overtime **in cash**; banking time
  instead is lawful only with `allow_first_schedule_eligible` **and** the employee's own recorded consent
  (`core/toil.ts:660-669`, migration 0123), and unused credit must then convert to pay rather than lapse.
  The figure is not hard-coded — it resolves from the country pack's `ot.wageCeiling`.
- **The one genuinely user-visible dead end is cancellation.** `core/leave.ts:5097-5101` and `:5471-5473`
  both hard-refuse cancelling an approved replacement leave because **there is no inverse of
  `consumeReplacementLeaveTx`**. Building that inverse is the real work in this item.
- **Money, on two independent paths, so hand-fixed:** a `toil_accrual` row SUPPRESSES that day's overtime
  pay in both payroll reads (`EXCLUDE_TOIL_BANKED_DAYS`, `core/payroll.ts:501-506`, applied `:2588` and
  `:3635`) **unconditionally, not behind the module flag**; and `convert_to_pay` expiry computes the EA
  s.60(3)/s.60D(3) figure. So an HR manual grant and a reversal both move money.
- **`toil_policy.replacement_leave_from` (0380) is written, defaulted and read by NOTHING** — the gate is
  the hard-coded `RL_ELIGIBLE_DAY_TYPES = Set(['rest_day','holiday'])` at `core/toil.ts:467`. The screen
  already admits it is recorded only.
- **Off-day earning deferred with a reason:** `attendance_day_type` is a 3-value enum on purpose
  (`core/attendance.ts:969-976`) because an off day is paid at ordinary 1.5× under EA s.60A(3)(a).
  Widening it is money-bearing across `plan_ot`, `PlanOtDayType`, `OtDay` and `core/payroll.ts`.

**CORRECTION TO THE SURVEY, made before planning:** the survey read the 2026-09-11 `entitlement-config.reset`
as having destroyed the customer's RL type. `fe9c73bc` is the **reporter's own reset request**, and the
replacement type was archived 2026-08-14, *before* it. The plan says so plainly rather than implying we
broke something.

**ATTACHMENT READ FIRST this time** (§8 — the r270 process miss). `Leave Credit.docx` is the Leave Config
menu, **not** the "Credit Reference / Entitlement Year / Expiry Date" screen their §13 describes. No screen
in this product carries those fields together, so their §13 is a TARGET, not a description of our UI — asked
in the plan rather than assumed. (The survey agent was blocked from the attachment by the PII classifier;
the parent had already extracted it by attachment id.)

### `3fbf7a02` Leave Balance Health — a menu row, and the reporter is right

`LeaveConfigHealthCard` is mounted at `app/admin/leave-config/types/page.tsx:241` — three clicks in, on the
Entitlements screen's Leave types tab, with nothing in the menu naming it. So the one screen that explains
