## r223 (2026-08-26) — ADR-0082 slice 2: the assistant substrate + the access-scoped tool registry. `0451`.

Four tables, the billable `assistant` module, the per-user grant service, and **nine tools** each
wrapping an existing `core/read.ts` function inside the CALLER'S OWN `SessionContext`, so RLS scopes
them. `search_handbook` is deliberately held for its own slice — it is the one tool that is not a
wrapper (no full-text search exists here) and **Postgres FTS stems per language**, which collides with
the six-locale answer decision. Nine tools, not ten, is the shipped state.

⚠️⚠️ **THE BUILD AGENT DIED MID-RESPONSE AND THE VERIFICATION WAS BETTER FOR IT.** The tool-registry
agent wrote its files and then died before reporting, so the three verifiers ran against a NULL build
report — with no builder claims to anchor on they read the code directly, and the completeness critic
returned "slice 2 is NOT done". It was right. **A build report is a claim, not evidence; its absence
cost nothing.**

⚠️ **THE DEFECT THAT GENERALISES PAST THIS ROUND: A READ BEING RLS-SAFE DOES NOT MAKE IT ANSWER-SAFE.**
ADR-0082 §4 mapped `upcoming_holidays` to `upcomingHolidays` (`core/read.ts:1886`), which filters on the
DATE ALONE — no company, no state, no holiday group — because its only caller is a dashboard card
already inside a company-scoped page. Pointed at "when is my next public holiday" it names days the
asker does not observe. Fixed with `holidayDatesForEmployment` over the ADR-0054 resolver. **Ask both
questions separately for every tool that is ever added.**

⚠️ **AND THE ONE THAT ALMOST SHIPPED UNGUARDED: `leave_entitlement_explain` BOUND TO `emps[0]`.**
`leave_type` is TENANT-scoped, so a leaveTypeId from `my_leave_balances` cannot say which employment it
came from — a shared-services employee asking about Company B was answered with Company A's figures,
silently. Now one block per employment with every figure INSIDE its block: a single top-level
`cycleStart` beside a list reads as "the" answer and gets quoted for the wrong company. **The
non-vacuity check is what caught that the fix was unguarded** — the existing test had ONE employment,
where `emps` and `emps.slice(0,1)` are the same list, so reverting the fix broke nothing. A
concurrent-employment fixture now guards it.

⚠️ **TWO MODEL-INPUT DEFECTS OF ONE FAMILY: EVERY IDENTIFIER AND DATE A TOOL RECEIVES IS
MODEL-SUPPLIED.** `Date.parse('2026-02-30')` does NOT fail — it ROLLS OVER to 2026-03-02 and returns a
finite timestamp — so 30 February reached Postgres and came back as `22008` thrown OUT of the tool
instead of the refusal it declares; and three tools passed a model-supplied id into a uuid comparison
behind only a non-empty check, so a hallucinated `"E12345"` raised `22P02`. Both now refuse. This is the
ordinary case for a tool registry, not the edge one.

⚠️ **THE MISSING SECURITY TEST NOW EXISTS, AND 0451 ALREADY CITED IT.** The migration named
`test/assistant-grant-rls.test.ts` in the PRESENT TENSE as the guard for its REVOKEs; the file did not
exist. It pins the critic's highest-value gap: **`assistant_grant_read` ORs in `app.is_admin()`, so RLS
hands an admin EVERY grant row in the tenant** — only the explicit `app_user_id` comparison in
`mayUseAssistant` stops an admin resolving `allowed: true` off SOMEBODY ELSE'S grant. A companion case
asserts RLS really does return that row, so the first cannot pass vacuously. Verified on production:
DELETE revoked on grant/budget/usage, KEPT on `assistant_exchange` (a user erasing their own history is
the PDPA right), RLS on all four.

**THE SLICE STILL HAS NO LOOP, NO BUDGET ENFORCEMENT AND NO SCREEN** — `converse()` (r221) and the
registry (r223) exist and still have no caller between them. Next: `core/assistant.ts`.

## r221 (2026-08-26) — ADR-0082 slice 1: the AI gateway learns to converse. NO MIGRATION.

**THE ROUND DID NOT COME FROM THE BOARD.** The owner asked to start "the real AI part". `lib/ai` was a
governed gateway with four single-shot drafting callers and nothing else; the north star's Phase B
(assistant) had never been started. **ADR-0082** designs it and **slice 1 is now deployed**.

⚠️ **THE ASSISTANT DOES NOT RETRIEVE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN.** ADR-0007 §3 rejects naive RAG
over tenant data, and this repo makes the reason concrete: access control is **per-row and in the
database** — `db/client.ts:186-190` sets `app.tenant_id/user_id/roles/grants` as transaction GUCs and
**128 migrations carry `CREATE POLICY`** against them (`payslip_rls` → `app.can_see_employment`,
`compensation` → admin-or-self). A vector store is a DERIVED store and inherits none of it: you would
re-implement `can_see_employment` as index-time ACL tags and re-index on every reporting-line change,
delegation, transfer and termination — a second authorization system that must agree with the first
forever. So the assistant calls the reads the SCREENS already call, inside the caller's own
`SessionContext`. ~40 functions on `core/read.ts` already take `ctx` first; that signature is the seam.

⚠️ **SLICE 1 HAS ZERO CALLERS AND THE ROUND SAYS SO.** `converse()` + the three adapters are ~1,800
lines no production path reaches. Deployed because main-ahead-of-production is its own hazard (r159),
NOT because it does anything yet. Every defect below was latent, never live.

⚠️⚠️ **THE ADVERSARIAL PASS FOUND 3 MAJORS UNDER 58 GREEN TESTS, ALL THE SAME SHAPE: ANTHROPIC (the
reference) WAS RIGHT AND THE OTHER TWO DIVERGED SILENTLY.** (a) Google's `providerState` replayed
`functionCall` parts even when `normaliseStop` had SUPPRESSED those calls on refusal/`max_tokens`, so
the next request showed the model a refused call as an outstanding request with no result closing it;
(b) `String(raw ?? 'STOP')` read an ABSENT `finishReason` as `end`, though the SDK documents empty as
"has NOT stopped generating" — a truncated answer reported as finished; (c) OpenAI emitted
`{role:'assistant', content:null}` with no `tool_calls`, which the SDK documents as invalid — one
`ConverseArgs`, legal on two providers, a 400 on the third surfaced as "Could not reach OpenAI".
**Hand-fixed, not sent back for a second agent pass (rule 23b), and each fix PROVEN non-vacuous** by
reverting it from a `cp` copy and watching exactly its own named test fail.

⚠️ **ONE OF THOSE FIXES WAS WRONG AND AN EXISTING TEST CAUGHT IT — RULE 18, EXACTLY.** Routing Google's
400 away from "Invalid API key" broke a deliberately-pinned behaviour whose premise was RIGHT: **the
Gemini Developer API answers a bad key with 400, not the 401 Anthropic and OpenAI use.** 400 only became
ambiguous once `converse()` made the request shape variable (a rejected tool schema is also a 400). So
`reason()` now takes the PATH: `generate`/`validate` keep "Invalid API key" (fixed shapes — nothing else
CAN be invalid), `converse` names both causes. The half still true stayed.

**FOUR ADR-0082 §8 DECISIONS ARE SETTLED (2026-08-26), TWO AGAINST THE RECOMMENDATION** — both kept
visible in the ADR rather than overwritten. (1) Audience is **a per-user grant the HR admin assigns and
removes** — neither option offered, and a mechanism this codebase DOES NOT HAVE:
`payroll_permission_grant` is keyed by ROLE, `lib/permissions.ts SCREENS` is static with no backing
table, and no per-user screen access is persisted anywhere. (2) The **full §4 tool catalogue**, which
commits `search_handbook` — the one tool that is not a wrapper over an existing read, since **there is
no full-text search in this codebase at all**. (3) Refuse at the ceiling. (5) **Answers in all six
locales**, which promotes one guardrail to load-bearing: the assistant may never ORIGINATE a statutory
figure or interpretation in any language, because model quality in ms/ta/th/vi for statutory HR
terminology is UNMEASURED here. Still open: transcript retention, and whose API key pays.

**STILL NOT DONE IN SLICE 1, deliberately:** the cache-read assertion ADR §2.2 says the build MUST make
(needs a live key); the `claude-opus-5` default in `lib/ai/registry.ts:16` (still `claude-opus-4-8` —
valid, just behind, and moving it changes behaviour for FOUR shipped drafting callers, so it is the
owner's call); and localising the gateway's raw-English error strings, which decision 5 makes overdue.
**THE DRY RUN IS CLEAN WHEN YOU EXCLUDE `next-env.d.ts`, AND THAT EXCLUSION IS CORRECT:**
`next-env.d.ts` (UNTRACKED and generated — a tree that has run `pnpm dev` says `.next/dev/types/…`,
production says `.next/types/…`, and each side is correct for its own build mode). DELETE the deploy's own
`deploy-rNNN.log` off the box when you are done with it, or `--delete` will report it forever. Anything
ELSE in that dry run is an undeployed release.
**NO MIGRATION SINCE r209** — r210 six items / 52 files; r212 two / 30; r215 two / 16.

verified on production by its EFFECT: all four tables present, RLS on all four, and the DELETE

**Next free is `0452`.**
**Board after r220 (2026-08-25): `deployed = 738` · `cancelled = 14` · EVERYTHING ELSE ZERO — the board
is completely clear for the THIRD time in its life.** r220 shipped two: `00806b4c` (the CP39 e-Data PCB
file fills all four identity boxes, refuses an over-long one, and the two downloads are named apart) and

⚠️⚠️ **r220's DECISIVE FINDING, AND IT IS THE SECOND TIME: THE REPORTER'S "WRONG FORMAT" WAS THE WRONG
BUTTON, NOT A WRONG FORMAT.** `00806b4c` sent a full LHDN fixed-width specification and asked for the CP39
text file to be rebuilt to it. Generating **ISEDECOR's own January 2026 file from production** (19
employees, aggregated per employment exactly as `cp39FileForBatch` does) produced
`009457390901_2026.txt` — **the filename in their own ticket, byte for byte** — with a 57-character header,
nineteen 136-character detail lines, no other line length present, CRLF between and after the last, and no
delimiter anywhere. It already met every clause they sent. What they had almost certainly downloaded was
**"Download as text"**, the READABLE COPY on the review screen, whose own tooltip already said it is not
the upload file. r218 was the same shape (PERKESO). **Generate the tenant's own file before agreeing that
a format is wrong.**

⚠️ **AND THE REAL DEFECT WAS UNDERNEATH IT: THREE OF THE FOUR IDENTITY BOXES WENT OUT EMPTY ON EVERY
LINE.** `buildCp39File` has always placed old K/P at 73–84, passport at 97–108 and Kod Negara at 109–110;
`cp39FileForBatch` simply never fetched them. Now it does. **Filling them made silent truncation reachable
for the first time** — the three columns are unbounded `text` and two are free-text inputs, and `alpha()`
hard-truncates — so `overlongCp39Identities` refuses and names the person and the box instead. A half
passport number is not most of an identity; it is a different identity, on a tax filing.

and pre-r220's output from the same rows gives **byte-identical files**. The value lands when HR enters a

⚠️ **THE REPLACEMENT-LEAVE NOTICE QUOTES SWITCH CAPTIONS THAT ARE ENGLISH IN ALL SIX LOCALES, AND THAT IS

⚠️ **r215's LESSON, CHEAP TO REUSE: A `method="get"` FORM DISCARDS ITS ACTION'S QUERY STRING.** The
Borang 8A validation-report button was written `formAction=".../file?report=1"` — reads correctly, passes
tsc, the suite and `next build`, and hands over THE FILE, because a GET submission rebuilds the query
from the form's fields per the HTML spec. A hidden input is the OPPOSITE trap: every button in the form
submits it, so both downloads would have returned the report. The one mechanism that works is the submit
button's OWN `name`/`value`, sent by that button alone. Pinned on both halves in
test/perkeso-socso-file.test.ts. **Both `borang-a/preview` and `borang-8a/preview` use GET download
forms**, so this applies to any button added to either — including `da4fc817`'s, if the EA gains one.

r217 — the planning detail is in `docs/HANDOFF-HISTORY.md` → r215 and r217.** The format facts that

the twelve-field table) live in `lib/perkeso-socso-file.ts` and `test/perkeso-socso-file.test.ts`, which
are the authority now.

⚠️ **TWO LESSONS FROM r212 THAT COST REAL AGENT TIME:**

  - **A FILE FENCE CAN SILENTLY DELETE THE DELIVERABLE.** r212's `elig` brief fenced the agent out of

    When a plan names a specific guard, its absence from the build report is a finding in itself.

**MEASURED, SO NOBODY RE-LITIGATES IT:** the new eligibility explanation runs once per leave type in
`no_eligibility_match`, which on this tenant is nearly every type. Reproduced locally (7 types × 4 tables,

"`localization/my/multicycle.ts` is unwired, wire it" was NEVER the fix — `core/payroll.ts` already ran

⚠️ **THE ONE CORNER WHERE r210's EPF PROMISE DOES NOT HOLD. The reporter HAS been told — see below.**
The plan promised, in plain words, that two runs in a month equal one run. Across the RM5,000 employer
step the published table steps DOWN (13%→12%), so a small bonus can make the month's combined figure
SMALLER than the regular run already contributed; `deltaStat` clamps the negative delta to 0, the bonus
payslip prints employer EPF 0.00, and the month sits up to **RM38** over the table figure. RM5,000 + RM50
= 650 + 0 against a one-batch 612. Pinned in `test/epf-combined-month-bdf7d248.test.ts`
(`twoRuns - oneRun === 38`). Nobody is short-paid — the excess is in the employee's own EPF account —
and closing it needs a negative EPF line, i.e. the reversals ADR (§6), not a code change.
**ALREADY RAISED AND CLOSED — do not raise it again.** It is board item `e52ce9b6` "EPF - the one case
where a bonus cycle does not add up to the month (RM5,000 step)", raised as CLAUDE AI on 2026-08-20 and
now `deployed` (`build_ref 1766c2b0`). The line that used to sit here said the reporter had NOT been
told; checking the board before acting on it is what caught that — AGENTS rule 7 applies to this file as
much as to a ticket.

**PROVE THE DEPLOY CLAIM INDEPENDENTLY** rather than trusting the line above: `git for-each-ref
refs/heads/build` plus a dry-run rsync FROM mainwt. **"Nothing in flight" is a claim about BRANCHES and
is NEVER a claim that `main` has been deployed** — r159 exists because those two were conflated. Every
unmerged `build/*` branch older than r209 is STALE, not pending: `r71`, `r83`, `r154` (squashed,
ancestrally unrelated), `r163-g-release3` and `r163g-picker`, whose content reached main another way
(their `0405` is on main as `0410_entitlement_reset_drop_old_layers.sql`, and `main` DELETES ~45,000
lines relative to both — that is the tell). r209's seven `build/r209-*` branches are all merged.

**IF YOU ARE ASKED TO BUILD SOMETHING, READ AGENTS RULES 23 AND 23b FIRST.** They are the most expensive
lesson in this repo: a workstream reporting tsc-clean and test-green is not evidence it is right, the
adversarial verify is the load-bearing step, and a second agent pass on the same code is where rounds go
backwards. Budget verification at roughly the cost of building.

  - **The EPF multi-cycle aggregation needs an ACCOUNTANT'S SIGN-OFF** before it is wired in (ADR-0024

## r220 — 2026-08-25 · the CP39 identity boxes, and the blank C.P.8A

**Shipped:** `main@3ac9294b`. Two approved items, one worktree each off `main@14646e3b`, merged after an
adversarial plan-versus-build pass. No migration; next free is still `0451`.

**`00806b4c` — CP39 e-Data PCB file.** The reporter sent LHDN's fixed-width specification and asked for a
rebuild. Their own January file, generated from production, already met it — `009457390901_2026.txt`,
57/136, CRLF, no delimiters. The real defect was that `cp39FileForBatch` never fetched `old_ic_number`,
`passport_number` or `passport_issuing_country_code` (migration 0450, r217), so three of Exhibit 4's four
identity boxes were empty on every line. Now carried, plus two refusals: no identity of any kind, and an
identity too long for its box. The readable copy was relabelled in six locales and the real upload file
gained a button on the review screen.

**`61c2e30f` — the blank C.P.8A and the field register.** `/payroll/ea/blank?lang=en|ms` renders the
Pin. 2024 form through the SAME renderer with `{ blank: true }`, which suppresses the money column;
verified on a dev server as one page in both locales with no amount of any kind on it. The 72-box field
register (`lib/ea-field-register.ts`) GENERATES `docs/forms/ea-cp8a-field-register.md`, and the contract
test binds register and renderer in both directions.

**Decisions the tickets did not settle:**

- **An old identity card counts as an identity.** The brief said refuse when new IC and passport are both
  blank; because the file now actually carries the old card, an old-card-only employee's line is complete,
  and the strict rule would have refused a whole month's filing for a correct record.
- **The blank needed an explicit flag, not an empty object.** Every Part B–E amount is a required number,
  so an "empty" statement is a statement of zeros and zeros print. `{ blank: true }` is said in as many
  words so a real employee's C.P.8A can never fall into blank mode by accident.
- **The upload-file download is a `formAction` submit on the review screen's existing form.** A nested
  form is invalid HTML and browsers drop the inner one.
- **Two gate lessons.** Three chunks is no longer enough for a 738-file suite: chunk 2 hit 99% on the RAM
  disk, Postgres died, and 25 unrelated files "failed" in 6–16ms with `ECONNREFUSED`. At `CHUNKS=6` the
  same tree was green — 738 files, 10,623 tests, peak disk 64%. A killed gate is not a red gate; read the
  error signature before believing either.

`f72cdba3`. Five approved items built as five workstreams in their own worktrees with nine adversarial

field names) · `ca7766ab` (entitlement effective date) · `7966ee35` (replacement-leave reason).
`68147833` — ours — closed with `build_ref` = no-code-change.

**THE VERIFY PASS FOUND SEVEN MAJORS AND THE TWO WORST WERE ON TAX DOCUMENTS.**

- **The EA printed a derived `0.00` on 1(b) and 1(c).** Each is ONE agency box over one payroll-derived
  figure and one that only an `ea_override` can supply, so a salary-only employee's C.P.8A stated "no
  fees, no director's fees, no commission". That is r209's defect wearing the agency's own numbered
  caption, which reads MORE authoritative, not less — and the approved plan had promised the reporter that

  expression was UPDATED, keeping the half still true.

  wording that gained the form's numbering. **The guard whose absence allowed it now exists on BOTH traced
  forms**: every caption is checked against the hand transcription beside the specimen. Every geometry case
  measures whether a caption FITS; not one checked what it SAYS.

  that accepts a past date; `supersedeNote` promised "nothing is overwritten" on the exact save this item
  makes overwrite. Rewritten in six locales and pinned so neither can promise either thing again.
- **The plan's "forwards or backwards" was half-built.** Any lineage superseded once could move its future
  head FORWARD only — the retie had already extended the predecessor over the span being reclaimed — so a
  mis-keyed forward move was irreversible, which is the correction the whole item exists to make. One
  overlap is now not a conflict: the lineage's own CONTIGUOUS predecessor, while its boundary AND the new
  date are both still in the future. A predecessor whose window has elapsed is a closed year and refuses.

**PROCESS — the parent's own two mistakes, which are the durable half.**

- **MARKING THE ITEMS `building` BEFORE LAUNCHING MADE EVERY APPROVED PLAN UNREADABLE TO THE AGENTS.**
  `improve:pull-approved` returns only `approved` rows. One agent disclosed it in `notBuilt`; the rest

  arrived at from the other end — the parent did the plan-vs-build diff by hand and it found two of the
  seven majors.

  screens at 500 with "No valid dev principal". `pnpm db:migrate && pnpm db:seed`, and read the dev log
  rather than the status code.
- **ONE FINDING WAS DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT.** The replacement-leave notice
  quotes switch captions that are English in all six locales — because it interpolates the settings
  screen's own key. Translating the quote while the screen stays English would be the real defect.

  failed to LOAD), then as a drift-ratchet failure. Same fix both times: a deferred import of

## r215 (2026-08-21) — THE PERKESO FILE, BUILT FROM A FILE THE AGENCY ACCEPTED

`433bbd3b`. Two approved items, built by the parent alone (no workstream agents) and self-verified. No
migration. 16 files, +862/−1. Gate 731 declared / 731 counted / every chunk exit=0 / 0 AssertionErrors at
CHUNKS=5; `next build` clean; three changed screens rendered with 0 `MISSING_MESSAGE`.

  `perkesoFileEmployeesFrom` and asserts byte-for-byte equality. Their written spec left the padding open

  ADJACENT. Non-vacuity: swapping two of them fails the golden on the bytes.

## r211–r212 (2026-08-20/21) — FOUR PLANS, TWO SHIPPED, ONE HANDED BACK, AND THREE "ALREADY BUILT"

`682c5af5`. r211 planned the four items waiting after r210; the reporter approved all four the same day;
r212 then discovered that only TWO of them were builds. Two workstreams, each adversarially verified, then
ONE fix pass. No migration. 30 files, +3,995/−199. Gate 730 declared / 730 counted / every chunk exit=0 /
0 AssertionErrors at CHUNKS=5; `next build` clean; four changed screens rendered with 0 `MISSING_MESSAGE`.

Shipped: `8ebf77ae` (leave eligibility explanation + the editor affordances) · `5206539f`
(`leave.apply_on_behalf`). Closed without a build: `e52ce9b6`. Blocked on the reporter: `c1b14600`.

**DECISIONS — what the diff cannot reconstruct.**

- **THREE OF FOUR APPROVED ITEMS WERE NOT BUILDS, AND SAYING SO WAS THE WORK.** `c1b14600`'s whole
  workflow already shipped as 296fc027, down to the ticket's empty-state sentence verbatim; the reporter
  could not reach it because 7 of their 9 companies have no `toil_policy` row. `e52ce9b6` was our own
  disclosure and its plan proposed nothing. Only `8ebf77ae` and `5206539f` had code in them.
- **WE DID NOT WRITE THE CUSTOMER'S CONFIGURATION FOR THEM.** Enabling Replacement Leave gives every
  employee in a company the ability to bank worked time, and nine companies were on offer with no way to
  know which they meant — approve carries no payload. The owner's call (2026-08-21) was to hand it back,
  so it is `blocked` with the two questions on the board, not guessed at.
- **AND WE CORRECTED OUR OWN PLAN IN THAT MESSAGE.** The r211 plan claimed the retired "Replacement Leave
  (in lieu)" type was appearing beside the live one. It is not: every employee-facing read filters
  `archivedAt`, so it shows only on the admin config list. Told the reporter rather than quietly dropping
  the bullet.
- **THE TWO ELIGIBILITY LAYERS STAY SEPARATE, and the plan says why to the reporter's face.**
  `leave_type.eligibility` asks *may they take it* (a yes/no); `entitlement_eligibility_rule` asks *which
  of sixteen tables do they get* (a choice). A yes/no cannot pick between tables. What IS duplication is
  the shared criteria vocabulary, so the rule editor now shows the type's own conditions read-only and
  offers a named "everyone this leave type is available to" shape.
- **ONE VERDICT, READ BY BOTH SCREENS.** The first build let the admin panel and the employee panel each
  derive the top-level verdict with its own precedence, and they rendered OPPOSITE sentences from one
  object for a sole-table type outside the employment window. `eligibilityNoticeFrom` now computes the
  verdict once and a source guard fails if either renderer starts re-deriving it. Precedence chosen
  deliberately: a winner outranks the employment window, because "no rule can reach them" is false about
  an outcome the engine just produced.
- **THE "EVERYONE" RULE KEEPS ITS REACH COUNT.** The first build shipped it as a bare form; two existing
  headers call that count "the only thing standing between 'no restrictions' and a whole-company
  assignment", and the write fires `recomputeAfterSave` immediately. It is now a count-then-confirm island
  with submit disabled until a number is on screen — stricter than the full editor's opt-in check, which
  is right for the one shape that always means everybody.

**PROCESS — two lessons worth more than the code.**

- **A FILE FENCE CAN DELETE THE DELIVERABLE.** The `elig` brief fenced the agent out of `core/read.ts` and
  `EntitlementBreakdown.tsx`, which are exactly what carries the employee notice to a real page — so the
  plan's headline bullet shipped as dead code. The agent disclosed it; the verifier proved it rendered
  nowhere. Check the fence contains the read that feeds the screen BEFORE launching.
- **A NAMED GUARD TEST THE BUILD SKIPPED FOUND A REAL HOLE.** "A holder is accepted in scope and refused
  outside it" was in the plan and absent from the build. Built in the fix pass, it failed immediately:
  `subject?.companyId ?? null` judged the permission against tenant-wide overrides only, so an employment
  the caller could not see fell through the on-behalf gate. A named guard missing from a build report is
  itself a finding.
- **MEASURE THE FLAGGED RISK; IT IS NOT ALWAYS THE LAST ONE.** The agent warned the new explanation runs
  per leave type on the busiest employee screen. Reproduced (7 types × 4 tables, 3 rules): 160–210ms
  against a 188ms baseline. Immaterial — unlike r210's `entitlementDeleteBlocks`, which really was 7s at
  scale. Same shape of warning, opposite answer.

## r210 (2026-08-20) — SIX ITEMS, ONE MEASURED EPF REVERSAL, AND A VERIFY PASS THAT PAID FOR ITSELF AGAIN

`1aa0c3a2`. Six approved items built as six workstreams, each adversarially verified, then ONE delegated
fix pass for the three with no money in them while the parent hand-fixed the other three (AGENTS 23b).
No migration. 52 files, +5,749/−686 over 21 commits. Final gate: 726 declared / 726 counted / every chunk
exit=0 / 0 AssertionErrors at CHUNKS=5; `next build` clean; six changed screens rendered on a dev server
with 0 `MISSING_MESSAGE`.

Shipped: `bdf7d248` EPF combined-month · `cc74dcb2` KWSP Borang A upload file · `5a29686c` Individual
Payslip selection · `9f8cd608` Reset Payroll screen · `7ad37961` TP1 full width · `0c367864` delete
entitlement tables and eligibility rules.

**DECISIONS — the part the diff cannot reconstruct.**

- **The EPF rule was REVERSED on the customer's figures, not on a source document.** Malaysia's Third
  Schedule is now read ONCE on the month's normal wage plus additional remuneration combined, instead of
  banding the salary and adding a straight percentage of the bonus. The reporter demanded 176/192 twice;
  that is exactly `epf(9063.71,0) − epf(7413,0)`. `docs/architecture/STATUTORY-SOURCES.md` recorded the
  OLD reading inside a section headed as verified — it now says plainly that the line is the customer's
  approved reading and has NOT been re-verified against LHDN/KWSP since. If anyone ever produces the
  source document, that is the line to check.
- **The RM5,000 employer step is a KNOWN, PINNED divergence, not an oversight.** See CURRENT STATE.
- **A bonus-only month moved too** (182/215 → 183/216 on RM1,650.71): right under the approved rule,
  outside the case the reporter measured, so it is pinned rather than left to be discovered.
- **`multicycle.ts` STAYS UNWIRED.** Two rounds have now proposed wiring it as the EPF fix. It is a
  duplicate of the kernel's own increment method and produces the same wrong figures; ADR-0024 §5 stands.
- **The Borang A file's field map came from a REAL KWSP file this time.** Item 3aae0789's map was
  reverse-engineered without a sample and put wages where the employer's contribution belongs. The
  sample is now a committed fixture and the golden asserts byte-for-byte equality with it.
- **The trailer control total is DERIVED but its field is read NARROW (12-zero filler + 9 digits).** The
  sample cannot settle 21-wide against 12+9 — its own hash fits in nine digits either way. Two pieces of
  evidence chose it: the 00 record ends in exactly that shape, and 3aae0789's independent transcription
  said so. A sum that will not fit writes ZEROS (never a truncation, never a refusal — a 46-employee
  employer must still be able to file) and the validation report says it happened.
- **The entitlement grant-blocker was DEFERRED OFF the page render, against the finding's first
  suggestion.** `leave_ledger`'s RLS calls `can_see_employment` (SECURITY DEFINER, two recursive walks)
  per ROW before any filter, so the pre-computed blocker measured 1.7s at 50k ledger rows and 7s at 200k
  on two admin pages that read no ledger at all before. Delete is offered and the refusal explains; an
  index would not have fixed it because the cost is the function, not the scan.
- **YTD on Individual Payslip is fenced on `scopeIds`, NOT the selected company.** Filling the Company
  box in — the point of the item — made the screen's own button post a companyId that a panel click does
  not, so the same visible selection printed two different year figures for a transferred employee and
  disagreed with the PDF beside it. The selection chooses which payslip; it does not redefine the column.

**PROCESS — what the verify pass caught that a green gate would have shipped:** 2 blockers and 4 majors,
nearly all introduced by the builds. A golden asserting the very rule the round reversed (the branch was
NOT test-green and the builder did not know); a Borang A mapping that could be transposed with all 214
tests staying green; a YTD that halved on a no-op form submit. The fix that closed the mapping hole was
to DELETE THE DUPLICATION (one `borangAFileEmployeesFrom`, driven by the golden) rather than add a test
beside it.

**AND THE GATE'S ONE RED FILE WAS A GUARD MEASURING A CHARACTER COUNT.** `statutory-explain` asserted
`/payroll/transaction-view` sat within a fixed 12,000 characters of the payroll `screenKey`; the block is
15,460 and this round's Reset screen pushed it to 12,767. Every entry was present and correctly attached.
Fixed by slicing to the NEXT `screenKey` — the question it was really asking. Look for the other magic
windows before one of them costs a round.

## r209 (2026-08-20) — ELEVEN ITEMS, SEVEN WORKSTREAMS, migrations `0448`+`0449`, `main@ef343c93`


Every approved item on the board, built as seven workstreams grouped so no two agents touched the same
files: `7ee14bbc` CP39 · `6036dab7` EA (BM) · `273e6fc7`+`70ac09ef`+`301d3f6b` leave entitlement ·
`6b4ca488`+`5a29686c` payslip · `0bade264`+`6448574f` attendance · `7ad37961` TP1 · `bdf7d248` EPF
worksheet. **The board is now completely clear for the first time.**

**THE PROCESS LESSON IS NOW AGENTS RULES 23, 23b, 24-28** — all seven workstreams reported tsc-clean and
test-green, and the adversarial verify then found 19 majors, 13 self-introduced. Read those rules; they
are the durable half of this round.

WHAT WAS WRONG AND IS NOW FIXED, kept here because each is a live behaviour someone may ask about:
 - **TP1 `tp1CountForYear` collapsed newest-wins-per-month BEFORE narrowing to what was effective**, so a
   correction keyed in August silently deleted the superseded row's money from every month between —
   payroll fed 0 instead of RM 1,000, reachable through the shipped UI. r201 filtered first and did not
   have this. **The order of those two steps is the whole correctness of that function.**
 - **TP1's `reconcileTp1ForYear` `agrees` was an algebraic identity**, true for every input. `counted`
   now comes from a set the function did not already collapse (only declarations that existed by that
   month), so it can fail.
 - **The EA printed `RM 0.00` for money it printed elsewhere** — see rule 28. Manual Part B boxes are now
   drawn only when an `ea_override` supplies a figure.
 - **CP39** stopped printing a false row-count assurance, stopped reporting one person with two
   employments as a duplicate tax number, and gained the unfinished-name warning the plan promised.
 - **The leave health card** measured the sole-table gate on a different set than the resolver does, so
   it reported green for a type the engine grants to nobody; a pooled row printed "create an entitlement
   table for it" over days the employee can actually spend.
 - **The payslip statutory explanation** captioned EPF as "percentage of wage" when ≤RM20,000 is a Third
   Schedule BAND lookup, and derived an "effective rate" on bonus runs by dividing a delta by the whole
   month's base.
 - **The EPF worksheet** aged employees at day 28 rather than PERIOD END (so anyone turning 60 on the
   29th-31st was modelled a year young and printed a fabricated difference), and omitted `socsoSkbbk`,
   an employee-deducted leg larger than the SOCSO employee share beside it.

Gate: tsc 0 · **721/721 files green at CHUNKS=5** · next build 0 · shadow rehearsal PASS (363→365) ·
i18n parity + base-aware audit CLEAN · zero-change `rsync --dry-run` · `0448`/`0449` columns verified on
the live schema · service active · `GET /` → 401. The gate caught two things no targeted run could — a
UTC "today" in the worksheet and a layout guard whose file had become a redirect — both now rules 27/18.

Moved here from HANDOFF.md on 2026-08-21; the two live-behaviour warnings it carried (the EPF worksheet
is a report not a switch, and EA employment income still folded into allowances) stayed in HANDOFF.md.

`df29af37` (`16f2aac1` Borang 8A) · `eb9a2e2f` (`cc9f9420` EPF Borang A, `5570c6a2`, `464b58e6`) ·
`774a7257` (`1b0943d5`+`3c88d593` entity transfer stage two with migration `0446`, `45df860a` PCB detail).

**EVERY ONE OF THE SIX BUILDS CAME BACK GREEN — tsc, its own tests and `next build` — AND FIVE OF THE SIX
STILL NEEDED FIXING.** That is this entry's point. The verify pass found what a targeted test run
structurally cannot see, and the worst of it was pay-affecting:

1. **`DEFAULT_PAYROLL_CYCLES` SEEDS THREE CYCLES ONTO ONE `run_type`** — 'Off-cycle', 'Advance Salary' and
   'Mid-Month' are all `off_cycle` (core/payroll-cycle.ts:115-125). The first `c11e81aa` build matched a
   transaction's intent to a run BY RUN TYPE, so a row saved as Mid-Month was collected and paid by an
   Advance Salary run. Only `regular` is protected from that, by two independent invariants at once (one
   active regular cycle per company, one regular batch per period). **Run type is not an identity.** The fix
   gives the BATCH a `payroll_cycle_id` and matches ID to ID through one shared resolver that both the run
   and the card read. The same collision existed a second time on the ATTACHED write path, and
   attach-on-generate never revisits an attached row, so it would have paid there too.
2. **A `<select>` WITH NO BLANK OPTION STAMPED A CYCLE THE OPERATOR NEVER CHOSE**, and editing only the
   AMOUNT of a legacy row re-pointed it. Rule 17 in a new costume: the field is always submitted. Fixed with
   an explicit empty option plus a `cycleTouched` flag, so an untouched field sends nothing at all.
3. **THE COMMENT IS THE GUARD, AND THERE WERE FIVE COPIES OF IT.** `listUnattachedTxnSummary` documented
   "attach-on-generate is REGULAR-RUN-ONLY" as a load-bearing invariant and keyed its join on it;
   `unattachedHoldersOutsideSelection` returned `[]` on the same reasoning, silencing the Payroll Process
   pre-flight for exactly the rows a regular run now abandons. Fixing those two left THREE more statements
   of the dead rule, one of them in a file the change had itself edited.
4. **A FIX INTRODUCED A DOUBLE-COUNT AND ITS OWN AUTHOR CAUGHT IT** — the new join could match two batches
   in a month holding two runs of one cycle, doubling money in every consumer that sums groups.
5. **THE `payitem` BRANCH GATED THREE OF FOUR LISTS.** `overtimeLines`/`bonusLines` went through
   `payItemLinesReconcile`; `allowanceLines` did not, on the reasoning that it agrees by construction —
   precisely the claim OT/Bonus carried until `display_category` re-routed money between the box and the
   bucket. The ungated list was the one nobody re-checked.

**WHAT THE AGENTS GOT RIGHT, AND SHOULD BE COPIED:** `ad52212d` REFUSED to rename
`attendance-allowance-policy.status-changed` because its rows are already on production and that is a
separate decision about existing history; a build agent REFUSED to widen `test/pack-drift-allowlist.json`
because the guard's own message says the list only shrinks; `5ff7daff` verified its plan's "NO rebuild"

## r186 (2026-08-12) — EIGHT APPROVED ITEMS, SHIPPED. Migrations `0428` + `0429`.

UNCHANGED**, `GET /` 401, zero-change arrival dry-run.

⚠️ **`7c834696` REDUCED TWO NAMED EMPLOYEES' RECORDED OVERTIME BY 60 MINUTES EACH.** Production was
paying 120 minutes where 90 and 100 were worked, because rounding to the NEAREST 60 pushes a day past
its own band ceiling. The fix is `Math.round` → `Math.floor` — **not** "nearest then clamp", which returns
90 and contradicts the plan. Measured across all 63 clock-out days since 2026-08-04: exactly two figures
move, both down. The 14 `Standard`-rule rows are all exact multiples of 60 and are untouched.

⚠️ **ITS SCOPED RECOMPUTE IS DELIBERATELY NOT RUN.** The two stored rows keep their 120 until someone
recomputes **2026-08-05, employments 100814 and 100815 ONLY**. A wide recompute would rewrite 41
historical days against shift times that were reassigned mid-day on the 5th.

#### AN AGENT REFUSED TO BUILD, AND IT WAS RIGHT — a plan's stated order beat my file map
`b8aa3466`'s BUILD NOTES say verbatim "Build af7a8eb4 FIRST … building this item first would write the new
form inside `app/admin/attendance/page.tsx` and then move it wholesale, and would falsify af7a8eb4's
already-approved mockup". I had scheduled `af7a8eb4` LAST because it looked cross-cutting. The agent
stopped rather than build 4 of 9 sub-items that would have been rewritten. **Group by file overlap, but
read each plan for a declared dependency FIRST — the plan may state an order the file map does not.**

#### A MOCKUP IS A PROMISE, AND `af7a8eb4` DISCHARGED ITS OWN
The approved sketch says "the same content at full width … no new field, no new column, no renamed
heading, nothing removed", against a diff that **deletes 721 lines net**. Proof it was relocation: diff
the UNION of the old files against the UNION of the new ones — **19 POSTed form fields, identical set;
zero i18n keys removed.** Copy that technique for any "move, don't change" claim.

#### THE `off_day` ENUM THAT WAS NOT WIDENED, AND WHY THAT IS CORRECT
`b8aa3466`'s plan said add `off_day` to `DayType`. That widens a SHARED Postgres enum (`plan_ot` uses it
too), three TS types, the payroll OT policy allowlist and `core/payroll.ts`. **An Off day pays 1.5× hourly
under s.60A(3)(a) — exactly the workday leg** — so it ships as a workday with a zero-minute normal day.
Same money, no enum change, `core/payroll.ts` untouched. Asserted in ringgit AND by `day_type`, with a
Rest-day test proving Off did not swallow Rest.

#### THE HALF-DAY BUG THE MONEY TEST CAUGHT
Halving `scheduledMinutes` produced **zero** overtime: on a resolved shift the engine measures workday OT
as minutes past the shift's TIME-OUT, not as an overshoot of scheduled duration. A half day now ends
halfway through the span too. **Row shape would not have caught this; a generated payslip did.**

#### THE PACK RATCHET FIRED ONCE, AND THE ALLOWLIST WAS NOT THE FIX
`core/absence-days.ts` imported `core/attendance` directly so absence derivation and the engine resolve a
working day identically — right intent, wrong edge. Fixed by importing `packs/attendance/service`, which
that file **already** does for approved-leave dates. The guard refuses allowlist additions in its own
message: it only ever shrinks.


## r185 (2026-08-12) — SEVEN APPROVED ITEMS, SHIPPED. Migrations `0426` + `0427`.

`98e69987` · `f35f758a` · `2aed39d4` · `587ee719` · `4157a498` · `510f4bd1` · `009c8a37`.
74 files, +9046/−2075. Gate **638 files / 6 chunks / every chunk exit=0 / 8,216 tests / 1 expected fail /
0 AssertionErrors**; tsc 0; `next build` 0; `gate:shadow` PASS 347/347; render check 0 MISSING_MESSAGE
across 16 routes × 6 locales. All seven marked `deployed`.

**THE BOARD SAID `approved = 1` AND IT WAS ACTUALLY 8** — and by the time the round finished it was 16.
This file's own instruction ("Counts live in CURRENT STATE … **Always RE-COUNT**") is the only reason the
round was not planned around one item. It has now been wrong in this direction three times.

#### ⚠️ THE DEPLOY ORDER WAS NOT THE USUAL ONE, AND THE FAILURE IT AVOIDED LOOKS LIKE NOTHING YOU EXPECT

**`scripts/repair-fixed-transaction-overlaps.ts --apply` had to run BEFORE `0426`.** `deploy.sh` is what
runs `db:migrate`, and the repair script only reaches the box via the release rsync — so the release was
split: **rsync → repair → `deploy.sh` → zero-change dry-run**, not one `improve:release` call. Keep that
shape for any migration whose precondition is a data repair.

Production carried ONE inverted row (`valid_to` before `valid_from`). An inverted row does **not** raise an
exclusion conflict — `daterange()` raises `range lower bound must be less than or equal to range upper
bound` while merely BUILDING the index entry, so the `ALTER TABLE` aborts on an error mentioning neither
overlaps nor the constraint. **`gate:shadow` cannot catch this**: it dumps the live schema STRUCTURE ONLY,
no rows, so it passed 347/347 while production would have failed. A shadow PASS proves a migration is
well-formed, not that it will apply.

Applied outcome: 9 rows superseded (1 inverted + 8 overlapping), 52 → 43 live, payslips untouched at 84,
and **0 remaining overlapping pairs measured with the constraint's own predicate**. X000001 keeps the
150.00 written last, which does NOT match the 100.00 its July payslip paid — stated in the approved plan,
intended, not a defect.

#### THE `daterange` EXCLUDE IS NOW PROVEN, AND THE BOUNDS ARE LOAD-BEARING
Executed on **PostgreSQL 16.14, which is what production runs**, across eight probes:

    daterange('2026-01-01','2026-07-01','[]') && daterange('2026-07-01','9999-12-31','[]')  ->  true
    daterange('2026-01-01','2026-07-01','[)') && daterange('2026-07-01','9999-12-31','[)')  ->  false

`employment_pay_component.valid_to` is **INCLUSIVE**; `compensation.valid_to` is **EXCLUSIVE**. The two
precedents for this constraint shape (`0004`, `0117`) are both HALF-OPEN — **copy their shape, never their
bounds.** `COALESCE(valid_to, DATE '9999-12-31')` because `'[]'` cannot be applied to an infinite bound.
The same asymmetry bit twice: `overlapsClosedPeriod` was written for `compensation` and its `to` is
EXCLUSIVE, so it is called with `addDaysIso(validTo, 1)` or a row whose last paid month IS the closed month
walks past the guard.

#### THREE APPROVED PLANS WERE WRONG ABOUT THE TREE, AND THE BUILDS WERE RIGHT TO REFUSE THEM
A plan is a specification, not scripture. Each was reported, not silently followed or silently dropped.
1. **`2aed39d4` step 5 misread `test/fixed-transaction.test.ts:323`** — its two windows do not touch, so
   "gap is intended" still holds. The overlapping sibling was what changed.
2. **`2aed39d4` step 7 named `processedPeriodsTx`**, which returns processed-OR-closed and would have
   re-implemented the very rule the step exists to reverse. `closedPeriodsTx` is correct.
3. **`f35f758a` item 4 called a comment stale** that the SAME ROUND made true again.

#### ⚠️ A LINT RULE FIRING IDENTICALLY IN EVERY LOCALE IS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE LINT RULE
`scripts/i18n-check.mjs` flagged `payroll.historyImport.missingColumns`, diagnosed TWICE (by an agent and
by the parent relaying it) as a translated placeholder name that would throw `FORMATTING_ERROR`.
**Both diagnoses were wrong.** `{count, plural, one {column} other {columns}}` — `column` is a plural
BRANCH BODY, ordinary text, not an argument. The tell both missed: it fired in **all five** non-English
locales. Five translators do not make the same mistake; a checker does. Its regex cannot tell a branch body
from an argument name. Verified properly by FORMATTING all 786 messages in the namespace through
`intl-messageformat` with the arguments the call sites pass (0 failures) and parsing all 51,564 (0
unparseable). **Follow-up, not on the board: teach the checker to skip plural/select branch bodies.**

#### THE SIX CATALOGUES SURVIVED FIVE BRANCHES BECAUSE THE MERGE WAS AUDITED, NOT ASSUMED
Five branches edited all six files and **28 keys were deliberately DELETED**. This is the r138/r141 trap:
a naive recursive merge reads "present in theirs, absent in ours" as an addition and resurrects every
retired key. **PRESENCE IS A VALUE — consult the merge BASE for absence too.** Git's line-based merge did
handle it, but that was verified with a base-aware audit (RESURRECTED / LOST / CLOBBERED) against the base
and all five sides: **8549 → 8668 keys, zero problems**, union +127/−28 reconciling exactly, all 28
deletions confirmed absent BY NAME. Note agents' self-counts ran high — **a REWORDED key is not an
addition.** Tool kept at `scratchpad/check-catalog-merge.mjs`; worth promoting into the repo.

#### `i18n/request.ts` IGNORED next-intl's REQUESTED LOCALE — A WHOLE FEATURE WOULD HAVE SHIPPED SILENT
`getRequestConfig` took no arguments and read the cookie unconditionally, so `getTranslations({locale})`
resolved to the COOKIE's catalogue: HTTP 200, a valid PDF, wrong language, every gate green. Now honours
`requested`, falling back to the cookie. **Blast radius measured before accepting: exactly 1 of 269
`getTranslations` call sites passes an explicit locale.** Proven by decompressing both PDFs' content
streams — the override beats the cookie in BOTH directions and the row count holds at 52 across the swap.

#### VERIFY ON THE ARTEFACT, NOT ON THE LAYOUT MATHS
r175a's CP22 lesson applied to the new two-column payslip: rasterised in **both** `mutool` and `pdftoppm`
across five fixtures, row count read off the artefact (all 70 items present in both, `missing=0`), geometry
read back with `pdftotext -bbox`. **The plan's own pt budget was pessimistic** — it predicted a spill that
does not happen; its figures came from a re-implementation, as it warned.

#### TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY RENDERING THAT NO TEST HELD
`?txnStatus=processed` returned rows the same grid labelled *Pending reprocessing*; and a wholly-failed
month produced no row at all in the import preview. Related and worth keeping: **`cleanBatchStatus` FAILS
OPEN** — an unrecognised filter value returns `undefined`, which DROPS the filter and silently shows
everything.

#### DELIBERATE ASYMMETRIES A REVIEWER WILL QUESTION — ALL INTENDED
- **`2aed39d4`'s key excludes `run_type`** though the ticket asked for it: the kernel never reads it and
  pays every returned row in full, so including it would have LEGALISED 2 of the 10 live clashes.
- **`4157a498` never lets `Override?` overwrite an occupied month**, and reports `updated = 0` always.
  `loadBatchRows` selects every batch for a (company, period) with no `run_type` and no `status` filter and
  SUMs, so a second load would submit someone paid 5,000 as 10,000. There is no undo — `0011` blocks UPDATE
  and DELETE on a closed batch at trigger level.
- **`4157a498` folds on (Employee No, Payroll Period)**, not the five-part key — `payslip_batch_employment_uq`
  allows exactly one payslip per employment per batch.

#### c8052ae3 — STILL NOT RUN. THE PLAN'S BACKUP COMMAND DOES NOT WORK ON THIS DATABASE.
Step 0's `pg_dump "$U" -Fc -f …` **exits 1** and leaves an ~889 KB partial that looks like a backup and is
not: `ai_provider_config`, `leave_adjustment_batch` and `platform_user` are FORCE RLS, `ai_hr_owner` has

both verified with `pg_restore -l`: a broad dump with those three tables' DATA excluded (85.5 MB, 1954 TOC
entries) plus a targeted dump of `leave_ledger`, `leave_entitlement_recalc_audit` and
`leave_ledger_reset_archive`. **All three excluded tables hold 0 rows, so the broad dump is complete.**

## r180 (2026-08-10) — TWO DEFECT FIXES, BOTH DEPLOYED. One of them was paying people twice.

**1. RECURRING PAY ITEMS HAVE BEEN PAYING TWICE, AND IT REACHED ISSUED PAYSLIPS.** Found while planning
board item `2f889bae`, then verified independently on production.

`setEmploymentPayComponent` closed the prior row ON the new start date, and its comment claimed "so there
is no double-count". **`validTo` is INCLUSIVE for pay components** — the kernel selects
`validFrom <= periodEnd AND (validTo IS NULL OR validTo >= periodStart)` and pays each returned row its
FULL amount — so both rows sat in the month containing the change.

MEASURED ON PRODUCTION, not inferred: **four employments carry overlapping live rows**, two of them real
customer records (Eee Lee Yong / Fiamma, TEST0002 / ISEDECOR). **Aisyah Rahman's 2026-04, 2026-05 and
2026-07 payslips each read allowance 140.00 where a single row gives 120.00** — RM20 per month on three
issued slips. One row is structurally impossible (`valid_from 2026-01-31`, `valid_to 2026-01-06`); Postgres'
own `daterange` refuses to construct it, which is how it surfaced.

**THE ROOT CAUSE IS A SEMANTIC MISMATCH BETWEEN TWO TABLES THAT SHARE A WRITER SHAPE.** `core/comp.ts` does
the IDENTICAL close-at-`effectiveFrom`, and compensation is safe — because its kernel reads a single open
row and its `compensation_no_overlap` EXCLUDE constraint uses a HALF-OPEN daterange, i.e. `valid_to` is
EXCLUSIVE there. Same writer, opposite boundary semantics, opposite safety. **Do not "align" one to the
other without moving the reader that goes with it** — this is recorded at the call site.

**WHAT SHIPPED:** the prior row is closed the DAY BEFORE the new start; a restatement from the row's own
start date SUPERSEDES it rather than inverting the window; a backwards restatement is refused. Chosen over
flipping the kernel's `gte` to `gt`, which would silently change what every EXISTING end-dated row pays in
its final month.

⚠️ **THE FIX IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, AND THE SUITE SAYS SO.** A MID-MONTH restatement STILL pays
twice: the two windows are adjacent (`…-05-09` and `05-10-…`) but both overlap the month, and the kernel
pays full amount for any overlap. The first regression test written returned **1554 = 777 + 777**. It is
recorded as `it.fails` in `test/fixed-transaction.test.ts` — the same idiom this repo uses for the known
width no-op — so the gate goes RED when someone fixes it. **Fixing it is a DESIGN DECISION**: prorate a
partial window, take latest-row-wins per period, or refuse a mid-period restatement. Each changes what
correctly-dated rows pay today, so it belongs to the reporter, not to a patch.

**THREE EXISTING ASSERTIONS PINNED THE BUG** while calling it "no double-count"; they are corrected. The new
boundary test asserts the MONEY through a real payslip — the pre-existing "no double-count" test only ever
checked row shape and never generated a payslip, which is exactly how this shipped.

**NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY:** the data repair of the four employments and the overlap EXCLUDE constraint. Both
change customer records and sit in `2f889bae`'s pushed plan awaiting approval. The constraint CANNOT be
applied before the repair. **The uniqueness key is an open question** — the pending constraint is keyed on
employment + component, while board item `2aed39d4` asks for employee + pay item + PAYROLL CYCLE.

**THE REPORTER HAS INDEPENDENTLY REPORTED THE SAME DEFECT as `2aed39d4`** ("the system can create duplicated
Start Date / End Date / Payroll Cycle records ... incorrect payroll calculations"). They arrived from the UI,
we arrived from the data. Do not plan the work twice.

**CORRECTED MEASUREMENT:** the paid-item removal guard depends on payslips storing WHICH component produced
a line. This file used to cite 7 of 50 payslips (~14%). Re-measured 2026-08-10: **19 of 83 carry
`componentLines`**, and of the 24 live non-BASIC items a processed payslip covers, only 12 carry line
evidence — so the guard still refuses about half of what it should.

**2. THE PERSONNEL RECALC-REASON LABELS.** `people.detail.recalcReason.*` is a COMPUTED key, invisible to
i18n coverage check C. The page had a fallback that COULD NEVER FIRE: it compared the translated value
against the RELATIVE key while next-intl returns the FULLY-QUALIFIED path on a miss. Measured live:
**50 of 72 audit rows rendered a raw key path at the user**. Fixed with `t.has` (the house idiom —
`app/admin/scheduled-actions/page.tsx` does the same), so an unlabelled reason degrades to the raw word;
five missing labels added in all six catalogues. **It PREDATED r179** — the block is byte-identical at
`d51c8f4d`. `test/recalc-reason-labels.test.ts` pins both halves, strips comments before source assertions
(its own explanation quotes the broken expression), and deliberately does NOT claim to enumerate every
emitted reason: six catalogued reasons appear nowhere in source, so any static list is provably incomplete.


## r184 (2026-08-11) — THE PAYROLL REPROCESS PAIR, BUILT AND DEPLOYED

`fbcf706d` (add a period-eligible employee to a processed run without resetting it) and `7076f8af` (Reset
lands back in the run flow; the adjustments panel and CSV import move off the run screen). Built in ONE
worktree, sequentially, because they overlap `app/payroll/[batchId]/page.tsx`, `app/payroll/actions.ts`,
`core/payroll.ts` and all six catalogues — the file-overlap rule, not the theme rule.
Gate **637 files / 6 chunks / every chunk exit=0 / 8,121 tests**; tsc 0; `next build` clean; render-checked
on a seeded dev server with zero MISSING_MESSAGE; deployed and proved by a zero-change dry-run.
**NO MIGRATION — `0426` is still free.**

**THE VERIFY-BEFORE-BUILDING GATE IS WHY THIS WORKED, AND IT SHOULD BE COPIED.** The plan's load-bearing
claim — that the subset path inserts a correct payslip for an employment with no payslip — was derived by
READING the engine and had never been executed: **0 of 123 production result-history rows had a null
`version_before`.** The build was gated on proving it first, with an explicit instruction to STOP and
re-plan if it failed. It held (gross 4000.00 at version 1, batch totals moved by the addition alone, the
already-paid payslip byte-identical), and measuring it turned three PREDICTED gaps into MEASURED ones:
`employee_count` stayed 1, the audit row rendered a phantom 0.00→4000 rise, and the no-salary case failed
closed with a misleading message. A premise that has never executed in production is a hypothesis; test it
before you build a screen on it.

**TWO MONEY GUARDS WERE ADDED BEYOND THE PLAN, AND THAT WAS RIGHT.** Item 5's scope bypass makes two
previously UNREACHABLE double-payment paths reachable: a claim allowance already written into
`payroll_input` by the draft-only prefill would be paid from the added payslip AND left payable on the next
run. Both now fail closed with a truthful message. **The claim mark-paid on a subset is deliberately
STRICTER than the full path** — the full generation infers "got a payslip therefore was disbursed" because
prefill and generation are one workflow; an add is not that workflow, so the requeue arm is not present on
a subset at all. A reviewer will notice the asymmetry; it is deliberate.

**`applyLoansForBatch` gained an OPTIONAL 5th parameter.** Omitted ⇒ byte-identical for the sole existing
caller. An empty array means "nobody" and returns early rather than widening to "all" — the difference
between those two readings is a double loan advance.

**THE PANEL WAS MOVED, NOT DELETED, and the board point was honoured BY PATH.** It is the only route by
which approved overtime, claims, loan instalments, shift differential, zakat, TP1 relief and attendance
allowances reach a payslip. Deleting it would leave approved amounts with no path to anyone's pay, silently.
`test/tp1-relief-reaches-payroll.test.ts` went red on all six bridges the moment the panel left the run
screen — it exists because `prefillTp1Action` once shipped bound to no form — and it was MOVED AND
STRENGTHENED, not relaxed. Seven prefill actions gained a `returnTo` because they hard-redirected to the
very screen this item removes from the path.

## r177 + r179 + r180 — SHIPPED 2026-08-10 (deployed together, main@34cc8137)

r177 was held for a week and released on the owner's command alongside r179. `0425` applied 344 -> 345
after a shadow rehearsal PASS. r179 carried four approved board items plus a shared employee search field
and the sidebar highlight fix. r180 followed with two defect fixes (see the HANDOFF entry for r180).

The two sections below are the in-flight entries as they stood while the work was held, kept verbatim
because their DECISIONS are the part that cannot be reconstructed from the diff.

### ⚠️ r177 — ADR-0076 IS BUILT, GATED AND **DELIBERATELY NOT DEPLOYED**

**`main@7eff1b87` carries the whole payroll anomaly layer — the ADR-0074 control-tower keystone — and it
is HELD at the owner's explicit instruction: "build to completion and testing, then build the guide, and
stop there to wait for my command to deploy."** Do not deploy it without that command. Everything else
(non-control-tower work) deploys automatically as usual.

**It is ready.** Gate: **630 files across 6 chunks, every chunk exit=0**; tsc 0; `next build` clean;
**shadow rehearsal PASS, 344 → 345** against a live-shaped schema. Render-checked on a dev server in all
six locales, empty AND populated, with zero MISSING_MESSAGE / IntlError / RSC errors.

**MIGRATION `0425` IS THE ONLY SCHEMA CHANGE** — three tables (`payroll_anomaly_verdict` / `_finding` /
`_config`), RLS + GRANTs on all three. Production is still on 344, so the deploy will apply exactly one.

**What it does:** `evaluateBatchAnomalies` reads a processed batch's payslips and writes a verdict per
employee (auto_clear / review / block) from 11 PURE detectors — 8 needing no history, 3 prior-period ones
that self-disable on cycle one and are recorded as SKIPPED WITH A REASON. `closeBatch` refuses while
unresolved `block` verdicts stand. A run-level circuit breaker catches the global mis-key that every
per-employee detector is blind to. Queue at `/payroll/<batch>/anomalies`; nightly sweep
`scripts/anomaly-sweep.ts` (`anomaly.sweep`, 02:30, crontab documented in DEPLOY.md).

**THE THREE THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE TOUCHING IT:**
1. **It is read-only with respect to money.** It never mutates a payslip, a batch total or a statutory
   figure, and no LLM is involved in any classification. Pinned by a test asserting the payslip rows are
   byte-identical before and after an evaluation.
2. **Both guards are ADDITIVE.** A batch with no verdict rows closes exactly as it does today — pinned by
   its own test. The circuit breaker needed an explicit `anomalyEvaluated()` gate to earn that, because
   unlike the per-employee guard it is RECOMPUTED and would otherwise fire on batches predating the layer.
3. **The thresholds are UNTUNED PLACEHOLDERS** (30% / 15%), labelled as such in code and in the guide.
   ADR-0076 §6 is blunt that only real history or a shadow run gives defensible numbers. **Never quote an
   auto-clear rate from the synthetic harness** — it proves the detectors work, nothing about thresholds.

**Deliverable for the owner:** an operator guide PDF ("Payroll exception checking — how to use it"),
written for the person who runs payroll, covering the daily rhythm, the four metrics (and why coverage is
read first), all 11 checks, the three resolution buttons, threshold tuning, and an explicit section on
what the layer does NOT do.

**The board, RE-COUNTED ON THE BOX after r179: `deployed = 633` · `cancelled = 14` · `approved = 5` ·
`planned = 1` · `open = 1` · `contested = 0`.** The reporter approved FIVE of r178's six plans within
hours. **Four of the five are BUILT — see r179 below; the fifth (`c8052ae3`) needs no build, it needs an
operator run.** `planned = 1` is `42afb2d2` (the roster question, finally answerable — see below).
`open = 1` is **`2ec1e3d2`**, which WE raised: the Roster screen shows every viewer a "Manage shift
schedules" link to an administrators-only screen, and the `42afb2d2` plan promised in writing that we would
raise it separately. Re-count rather than trusting this line.

### ⚠️ r179 (2026-08-10) — FOUR APPROVED ITEMS BUILT AND GATED, **DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED TO `main`**

**`build/r179-integration@c63d5064`** carries all four items the reporter approved after r178's plans:
`b00f9e6e` (overtime seeder guard) · `388e53c2` (leave nav move) · `98e69987` (Transaction Detail) ·
`f35f758a` (Individual Payslip screen + document), plus a shared employee search field and the sidebar
highlight fix. **NO MIGRATION — `0426` is still free.**

the dry-run rsync can confirm at a glance. Merging r179 would make that two releases while deploy is
blocked, and buys nothing. **A branch is also MORE discoverable than a silent main merge** — the
unshipped-round check (`git for-each-ref refs/heads/build`) finds it, which is precisely the check r159
proved does NOT find merged-but-undeployed work. Merge it when r177 is released, not before.

**Gate: 633 files across 6 chunks, every chunk exit=0, 8,046 tests** (106+106+106+105+105+105 — counted
files equal files asked, peak disk 30–48%); `tsc` 0; `next build` clean, all r179 routes present and `ƒ`.

**RENDER-CHECKED FOR REAL** (four identities, ten renders, dev-server log read): zero MISSING_MESSAGE,
IntlError or FORMATTING_ERROR. **The access-critical branch is verified by RENDER, not by test alone:** on
`/leave/tracker` an hr_admin gets the Employee Details listing (`name="edQ"` present, calendar absent) and
a manager and a plain employee both still get the calendar (`edQ` absent, calendar present). On `/leave`,
an unlinked admin gets no balance card while an employee and a manager do.
**METHOD NOTE, because the obvious check is a lie here:** grepping rendered HTML for a LABEL proves
nothing — Next embeds the whole i18n catalogue in every payload (a ~563KB floor on these pages), so
"Employee Details" appears on a plain employee's page whether or not it rendered. Discriminate on FORM
CONTROL NAMES and payload deltas, which cannot appear from the catalogue.

**What the agents found that the plans did not:**
- **`b00f9e6e` was mutation-tested, and the obvious test does not pin what matters.** An archived
  *per_hour* reference reaches the archived throw from either side of the ordering, so the natural test
  stays green if the throw is moved. Only an archived reference that ALSO lacks an hourly rate
  distinguishes the two placements; that case exists now. Also confirmed by mutation that the pre-fix
  behaviour is a SILENT SUCCESS (it creates OT2_0/OT3_0 scaled off a switched-off rate), not a mislabelled
  error.
- **`f35f758a`: fixing the truncation with greedy word-wrapping ALONE would have shipped the same bug
  silently.** A single token wider than its column emits as one over-wide line that overprints the amount.
  Character-level breaking was added, and the result was rasterised in BOTH `mutool` and `pdftoppm` across
  three fixtures (43 deliberately over-long pay item names, long employee/department/company names) —
  the r175a two-renderer rule, applied.
- **The round brief's own guard premise was wrong on `98e69987`**, and the agent caught it:
  `test/employee-scope-panel-guard.test.ts` had NO transaction-view case to rewrite. Five were ADDED and
  then PROVED to bite by restoring the pre-change page from a `cp` backup (3 of 5 fail against it).
- **`388e53c2`'s sidebar highlight — the reporter's ORIGINAL complaint — could not be fixed from inside the
  leave lane and was correctly held back with a written spec rather than reached for.** It is now landed
  solo: `exactHref` / `ownedSubpaths` on `NavChildDescriptor`, read by an EXPORTED `isNavRowActive` so the
  truth table drives the real predicate rather than a copy that would pass on day one and drift.
  Mutation-verified. The held-back agent deliberately did NOT pin the wrong behaviour — which is why the
  table could be written as the CORRECT one.

**Two environment traps this round, both cheap and both cost time:**
1. **A FRESH WORKTREE HAS `node_modules` BUT NO `.env.local`** (it is gitignored), and `global-setup` loads
   it from cwd. The failure is actively misleading: vitest prints `No test files found, exiting with code 1`
   with the real cause (`TEST_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL must be set`) buried below. Copy `mainwt/.env.local`
   into every new worktree at creation.
2. **A RAM-DISK CLUSTER DOES NOT SURVIVE A REBOOT** — the symlink dangles and `psql` reports the server is
   not running. That is not a wedge; run `./scripts/dev-db-rebuild.sh`. Also: a between-chunk rebuild makes
   the cluster briefly unreachable, so a liveness probe during `gate-chunked.sh` can read as "server down"
   when the gate is perfectly healthy. Read the per-chunk log, not the socket.
